1301.description:
A trail runs south through a light, airy wood of silver birches, their
white trunks bright against the gloom of the Old Forest that stands
close on either hand. Step off the trail east or west and you would be
among the dark trunks at once, and easily lost. Birch leaves flicker and
turn in the faintest breath of air. North, the golden trees mark the end
of the Path of Light.

1302.name: A Trail Through A Light Forest

north.description: To the north lies A Trail Through A Light Forest.

south.description: To the south lies A Trail Through A Light Forest.

1302.description:
Aspens grow among the birches here, their round leaves trembling and
chattering with every stir of wind. The trail is a ribbon of short grass
and fallen leaves, easy to follow, but the Old Forest looms only a few
paces away east and west, its shadows reaching across the path. Ferns
grow tall along the verges. The trail runs on north and south between
the pale trunks.

1303.name: A Trail Through A Light Forest

north.description: To the north lies A Trail Through A Light Forest.

east.description: To the east lies In The Old Forest.

south.description: To the south lies A Trail Through A Light Forest.

west.description: To the west lies In The Old Forest.

1303.description:
A fallen birch lies along the edge of the trail here, its white bark
peeling in papery curls and its wood gone soft and orange with rot.
Beyond it, east and west, the dark ranks of the Old Forest wait, and
paths of a sort lead into them, worn by those who strayed. The light
trail itself continues north and south, bright and narrow, between the
pale trees.

1304.name: A Trail Through A Light Forest

north.description: To the north lies A Trail Through A Light Forest.

east.description: To the east lies In The Old Forest.

south.description: To the south lies In The Old Forest.

west.description: To the west lies A Trail Through A Light Forest.

1304.description:
The trail turns west here, swerving around a dense knot of holly beyond
which, south and east alike, the Old Forest begins at once, black and
close. Faint ways lead into it, but they would soon have you wandering
in circles. Bracken grows thick at the bend, bronzed at its tips. North,
the trail runs back between the birches.

1305.name: A Trail Through A Light Forest

north.description: To the north lies In The Old Forest.

east.description: To the east lies A Trail Through A Light Forest.

south.description: To the south lies A Trail Through A Light Forest.

west.description: To the west lies In The Old Forest.

1305.description:
The trail bends again here, coming in from the east and turning south,
and the pale wood narrows to a strip only a few trees wide. The Old
Forest presses close to the north and west, so close that its roots
creep across the grass of the trail. A young rowan, bright with berries,
grows at the corner as if to mark the way. Lichen hangs in grey beards
from the nearest dark branches.

1306.name: A Trail Through A Light Forest

north.description: To the north lies A Trail Through A Light Forest.

east.description: To the east lies In The Old Forest.

south.description: To the south lies A Trail Through A Light Forest.

west.description: To the west lies In The Old Forest.

1306.description:
The light wood widens a little here into a long, narrow glade of grass
and harebells, sunlit and quiet. On either side, east and west, the edge
of the Old Forest is as sharp as a wall, dark trunks standing shoulder
to shoulder just beyond the last of the birches. The trail runs straight
through the glade, north and south.

1307.name: A Trail Through A Light Forest

north.description: To the north lies A Trail Through A Light Forest.

east.description: To the east lies In The Old Forest.

south.description: To the south lies A Trail Through A Light Forest.

west.description: To the west lies In The Old Forest.

1307.description:
A little stream crosses the trail here, shallow and clear over a bed of
pale pebbles, and someone has laid a pair of flat stones in it for
stepping across. The water comes out of the Old Forest on one side and
vanishes into it on the other, and dark paths follow it both east and
west into the gloom. The trail goes on north and south among the slim
white trees.

1308.name: A Trail Through A Light Forest

north.description: To the north lies A Trail Through A Light Forest.

east.description: To the east lies In The Old Forest.

south.description: To the south lies At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest.

west.description: To the west lies In The Old Forest.

1308.description:
The birches here are hung with the first golden leaves again, a few at
first and then more, as the trail nears the edge of the Radiant Forest
to the south. The Old Forest still hems the trail east and west, but its
gloom seems to shrink back from the brightening trees. North, the pale
trail runs on through the birch wood.

1309.name: A Corner In The Radiant Forest

north.description: To the north lies In The Old Forest.

east.description: To the east lies At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest.

south.description: To the south lies At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest.

west.description: To the west lies In The Old Forest.

1309.description:
Two ancient yews of the Old Forest stand guard at this corner, one to
the north and one to the west, their red trunks twisted like rope and
their needles so dark they look black. Between them the golden light of
the radiant wood grows thin and grey. A post of grey stone stands at the
very corner, topped by an empty iron cage where a lantern once hung to
mark the border. The bright margin runs east and south from here.

1310.name: At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest

north.description: To the north lies In The Old Forest.

east.description: To the east lies At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest.

south.description: To the south lies In The Radiant Forest.

west.description: To the west lies A Corner In The Radiant Forest.

1310.description:
Overhead the canopy changes abruptly, pale gold leaves meeting the dark,
heavy crowns of the Old Forest along a line as sharp as a seam. Roots of
both kinds of tree knot together underfoot and make the going slow. The
Old Forest lies north, the radiant margin runs east and west, and south
a path leads in beneath the golden boughs. Somewhere in the dark wood a
branch creaks with no wind to move it.

1311.name: At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest

north.description: To the north lies A Trail Through A Light Forest.

east.description: To the east lies At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest.

south.description: To the south lies In The Radiant Forest.

west.description: To the west lies At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest.

1311.description:
The birch trail ends at the bright margin of the Radiant Forest, where
golden boughs arch overhead and the light thickens into a warm glow. The
edge of the wood runs east and west, gold on one hand and the brooding
Old Forest on the other, and south a path leads on beneath the shining
trees toward a scent of honeysuckle. North, the pale birch trail runs
back toward the Path of Light.

1312.name: At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest

north.description: To the north lies In The Old Forest.

east.description: To the east lies A Corner In The Radiant Forest.

west.description: To the west lies At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest.

1312.description:
Along this stretch of the margin the golden trees stand in a long,
unbroken line, and their roots and those of the Old Forest wrestle
together in the moss beneath. North, the dark wood begins at once, its
shadows lying across the grass like spilled ink. The bright edge runs
east toward a corner and west toward the end of the birch trail.

1313.name: A Corner In The Radiant Forest

north.description: To the north lies In The Old Forest.

east.description: To the east lies In The Old Forest.

south.description: To the south lies At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest.

west.description: To the west lies At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest.

1313.description:
The Radiant Forest turns a corner here, its golden margin bending away
south while the Old Forest wraps around it to the north and east like a
dark cloak. A white stone, smooth and round as an egg, has been set into
the moss at the very corner, the first of a line that runs on south
along the edge. West, the bright margin leads back toward the birch
trail.

1314.name: In The Radiant Forest

north.description: To the north lies At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest.

east.description: To the east lies In The Radiant Forest.

south.description: To the south lies In The Radiant Forest.

1314.description:
A long fallen log lies half sunk in the moss here, so old that ferns and
tiny saplings sprout along its back. Bluebells crowd the ground around
it in a haze of blue beneath the gold. Paths lead north to the edge of
the wood, east into a nook among hazels and south into a ring of tall
ferns. The air smells green and sweet, like crushed stems after rain.

1315.name: In The Radiant Forest

west.description: To the west lies In The Radiant Forest.

1315.description:
Hazel bushes close around this quiet nook on every side but the west.
Their roots have been coaxed, over many years, into the shape of a low
bench, smooth and polished from use, set facing a gap in the leaves
where the light pours through. Cobnuts hang in pale green clusters above
it. It is the kind of place where someone might sit for a whole
afternoon and never notice the time passing.

1316.name: In The Radiant Forest

east.description: To the east lies In The Radiant Forest.

south.description: To the south lies In The Radiant Forest.

1316.description:
A single silver birch grows among the gold-leaved trees here, white and
slender, its bark peeling in papery curls and pocked with the neat round
holes of woodpeckers. It looks out of place, like a guest who has
wandered into the wrong house. The way bends here, running east under
low boughs and south toward a towering trunk. The leaf litter is deep
and dry and rustles at every step.

1317.name: In The Radiant Forest

north.description: To the north lies At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest.

east.description: To the east lies In The Radiant Forest.

west.description: To the west lies In The Radiant Forest.

1317.description:
Honeysuckle climbs the trunks here and hangs in sweet-smelling curtains
from the lower branches, its cream and yellow flowers almost the colour
of the light. North, the trees thin toward the edge of the radiant wood,
where darker boughs show beyond. A path winds east toward a hidden dell
and west past a lone white birch. The scent of the flowers is heavy
enough to make you drowsy.

1318.name: In The Radiant Forest

west.description: To the west lies In The Radiant Forest.

1318.description:
This hidden dell lies below the level of the surrounding wood, its sides
steep with moss and roots, and the only easy way out is the path
climbing back west. At its bottom stands the statue of a slender figure
in a long robe, holding up a lamp of carved stone. Moss has grown over
her shoulders like a shawl, but her face is still clear and calm. The
light in the dell is brighter than anywhere around it, and seems to come
from the lamp.

extra_descs.statue figure lamp:
The figure is plainly elven, tall and fine-boned, her hair bound back
with a circlet of leaves. Words are cut into the base in a flowing
script, and a patient scholar might make them out as THE LIGHT
REMEMBERS.

1319.name: At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest

north.description: To the north lies A Corner In The Radiant Forest.

south.description: To the south lies At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest.

west.description: To the west lies In The Old Forest.

1319.description:
An old earth bank runs along the border here, with a ditch on its far
side where the Old Forest begins. Ivy has swallowed the bank completely
and climbs the first dark trunks to the west as though trying to drag
them down. On this side the gold-leaved trees grow right up to the bank
and lean slightly away from it. The margin leads north to a corner of
the wood and south along the bank.

1320.name: In The Radiant Forest

north.description: To the north lies In The Radiant Forest.

1320.description:
Tall ferns grow in a ring here, higher than your head, enclosing a
circle of short turf like the walls of a green room. In the middle sits
a shallow basin of grey stone, filled with rainwater in which a few gold
leaves turn slowly. There is no way through the ferns except the path
back north. The quiet is so complete that you can hear the drip of dew
from the fronds.

1321.name: At A Great Tree

north.description: To the north lies In The Radiant Forest.

east.description: To the east lies In The Radiant Forest.

south.description: To the south lies In The Radiant Forest.

west.description: To the west lies In The Radiant Forest.

up.description: To the up lies Stairs On A Humongous Tree.

1321.description:
A tree of impossible size rises here, its trunk wider than a cottage and
its bark grey and smooth as old silver. A stair has been shaped out of
the living wood, spiralling up around the trunk toward the hidden halls
of Elvandar, but a gate of woven silver branches closes its lowest step
and will not open. Paths leave the roots to the north, east, south and
west. Gold light rains down from the canopy far overhead.

extra_descs.gate silver branches stair:
The gate is not forged but grown, a lattice of thin silver-barked
branches woven so tightly that not even a hand will pass. A leaf-shaped
hollow at its centre looks as though it waits for a key that is not made
of iron.

1322.name: In The Radiant Forest

north.description: To the north lies In The Radiant Forest.

east.description: To the east lies In The Radiant Forest.

south.description: To the south lies In The Radiant Forest.

west.description: To the west lies At A Great Tree.

1322.description:
The great tree's trunk bulges out of the ground just west of here, so
broad that it fills half the view. Smaller gold-leaved trees crowd
around it like children at their mother's skirts, and the leaves they
drop lie thick and round as coins. Paths lead north past a lone silver
birch, east among the trees and south toward a crossing of deer trails.
A faint, sweet scent drifts down from blossoms high above.

1323.name: In The Radiant Forest

east.description: To the east lies At A Great Tree.

west.description: To the west lies In The Radiant Forest.

1323.description:
A path of flat white stones has been laid here between two of the great
trees, each stone sunk level with the moss and worn hollow in the middle
by countless soft footsteps. East the stones lead to the roots of one
giant, and west they run back toward the other. Lesser trees line the
way, their gold leaves meeting overhead. The stones are cool underfoot
even where the light falls full on them.

1324.name: At A Great Tree

north.description: To the north lies In The Radiant Forest.

east.description: To the east lies At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest.

south.description: To the south lies In The Radiant Forest.

west.description: To the west lies In The Radiant Forest.

up.description: To the up lies Stairs On A Humongous Tree.

1324.description:
Another of the giant trees stands here, its roots arching out of the
earth in great loops that you could walk beneath without stooping. A
stair winds up the trunk toward the high halls of the elves, but its
lowest flight ends well above the ground, and whatever ladder once
reached it has been drawn up. Ways lead north into a sunken dell, east
toward the edge of the wood, south to a stony brook and west along a
path of white stones.

1325.name: At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest

north.description: To the north lies A Corner In The Radiant Forest.

east.description: To the east lies In The Old Forest.

south.description: To the south lies At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest.

1325.description:
The gold-leaved trees stop short here at a line of white stones, set
into the moss at even paces as if someone once marked where the light
should end. Beyond the stones to the east the Old Forest begins at once,
a wall of black-trunked oaks hung with grey lichen and filled with a
breathless gloom. The bright margin runs north toward a corner of the
Radiant Forest and south along the line of stones. Behind you the canopy
glows a soft, unhurried yellow.

1326.name: At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest

north.description: To the north lies At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest.

east.description: To the east lies In The Radiant Forest.

south.description: To the south lies At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest.

west.description: To the west lies In The Old Forest.

1326.description:
A great hollow stump stands at the boundary, its jagged rim taller than
a man and its inside packed with gold leaves blown in from the radiant
wood. Beside it a narrow game trail slips west into the Old Forest,
where brambles close over it within a dozen paces. The edge of the
golden trees runs north and south. Eastward the wood opens beneath the
crown of a tree so vast that it dwarfs every other.

1327.name: In The Radiant Forest

north.description: To the north lies At A Great Tree.

east.description: To the east lies In The Radiant Forest.

south.description: To the south lies In The Radiant Forest.

west.description: To the west lies At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest.

1327.description:
The ground here heaves up in long ridges where the roots of a vast tree
run beneath it, some of them thicker than a horse's body. North, the
trunk itself rises like a grey cliff, its crown lost in a blaze of gold
far above. Narrower ways lead east and south between the lesser trees,
and west the light thins toward the edge of the wood. Moss fills every
crease between the roots.

1328.name: In The Radiant Forest

north.description: To the north lies In The Radiant Forest.

east.description: To the east lies In The Radiant Forest.

west.description: To the west lies In The Radiant Forest.

1328.description:
Several narrow deer trails cross here, pressed into the leaf litter by
generations of hooves. One of the trunks beside the crossing has been
rubbed bare and scored by antlers, the scratches glinting with golden
sap. The trails lead north toward the flank of a giant tree, east to a
spring among the clover and west toward a ridge of great roots. The
ground is soft, and every track shows plainly.

1329.name: In The Radiant Forest

south.description: To the south lies In The Radiant Forest.

west.description: To the west lies In The Radiant Forest.

1329.description:
Clover and wild violets cover the ground here so thickly that the air is
sweet with them, and a tiny spring trickles out from beneath a tree root
to lose itself among the flowers. The trees grow close, their trunks
banded with pale lichen. A path leads south beneath a woven arch, and
another runs west to a crossing of trails. Gold leaves float in the
little pools the spring has made.

1330.name: In The Radiant Forest

north.description: To the north lies At A Great Tree.

south.description: To the south lies In The Radiant Forest.

1330.description:
A quick brook crosses the path here, running clear over gold-flecked
pebbles, and a little bridge of three silver-grey planks, joined without
a single nail, spans it. North, the roots of a giant tree loop out of
the ground beyond the water, and south the path climbs gently into a
clearing ringed with birches. Water-mint grows along the banks, and its
smell rises sharp and clean when you brush against it.

1331.name: In The Radiant Forest

north.description: To the north lies In The Radiant Forest.

south.description: To the south lies At A Great Tree.

1331.description:
The way runs narrow here between two high banks thick with ferns, their
fronds meeting overhead in a green tunnel shot through with gold. Water
seeps from the banks and keeps the path soft and dark. North the tunnel
opens toward a ridge of great roots, and south the glow of hanging
lanterns shows where another giant tree stands. Your shoulders brush the
cool fronds on either side.

1332.name: In The Radiant Forest

north.description: To the north lies In The Radiant Forest.

east.description: To the east lies In The Radiant Forest.

south.description: To the south lies In The Radiant Forest.

1332.description:
Two young trees have been trained toward each other here until their
branches meet and twine together, forming an arch of living wood over
the path. Their leaves are a deeper gold than those around them, and a
few late blossoms still cling to the weave. Beyond the arch the way runs
north to a spring among the clover, east into a circle of birches and
south toward a sunny bank. The arch creaks softly whenever the wind
passes through it.

1333.name: In The Radiant Forest

north.description: To the north lies In The Radiant Forest.

east.description: To the east lies At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest.

south.description: To the south lies At A Great Tree.

west.description: To the west lies In The Radiant Forest.

1333.description:
Seven white birches stand in a perfect circle here, too evenly placed to
have grown that way by chance, and the clearing they enclose is carpeted
with short, springy turf. Gold-leaved trees rise all around beyond them.
Ways lead north to a brook, east to the margin of the wood, west under a
woven arch and south toward the vast trunk of yet another great tree.
Even the wind seems to step softly in this place.

1334.name: At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest

north.description: To the north lies At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest.

east.description: To the east lies In The Old Forest.

south.description: To the south lies A Corner In The Radiant Forest.

west.description: To the west lies In The Radiant Forest.

1334.description:
A great gold-leaved tree has fallen across the border here, its roots
torn up out of the radiant wood and its crown sprawled east among the
dark trunks of the Old Forest. The leaves on this side of the line still
shine like new coin, while those beyond it have curled brown and dead.
The margin of the forest runs north and south, and west the golden trees
stand close and calm. A smell of wet bark and torn earth hangs about the
upturned roots.

1335.name: At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest

north.description: To the north lies At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest.

east.description: To the east lies In The Radiant Forest.

south.description: To the south lies A Corner In The Radiant Forest.

west.description: To the west lies In The Old Forest.

1335.description:
To the west stands a wall of dark firs, the first trees of the Old
Forest, so close-set that their lower branches have died grey and
brittle in the gloom. The soft moss underfoot gives way to a crust of
brown needles right at the boundary. A cold breath of air comes out of
the firs, smelling of resin and old rot. The golden margin leads north
and south, and east the radiant trees open invitingly.

1336.name: In The Radiant Forest

south.description: To the south lies In The Radiant Forest.

west.description: To the west lies At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest.

1336.description:
Where an old tree fell some years ago, a crowd of young saplings has
sprung up to fight for the light, each one straight and slim with a
crown of tender gold leaves. The trunk of the fallen giant still lies
among them, soft with rot and bright with orange fungus. A path leads
west to the edge of the wood, where dark firs stand beyond, and south
into a hollow of drifted leaves. The saplings sway together in the
slightest breeze.

1337.name: At A Great Tree

north.description: To the north lies In The Radiant Forest.

east.description: To the east lies In The Radiant Forest.

south.description: To the south lies In The Radiant Forest.

west.description: To the west lies In The Radiant Forest.

up.description: To the up lies Stairs On A Humongous Tree.

1337.description:
Lanterns of pale glass hang from the lowest boughs of the colossal tree
that rises here, and though no flame burns in any of them, still they
glow. A stair spirals up the trunk toward the high dwellings of
Elvandar, but its foot lies behind a door of living bark that has closed
over the opening like a healed wound. Ways lead north between banks of
fern, east past a carved stone, south toward a mossy spring and west
among young trees.

1338.name: In The Radiant Forest

east.description: To the east lies In The Radiant Forest.

west.description: To the west lies At A Great Tree.

1338.description:
A waist-high stone stands beside the path here, pale and smooth, with a
single rune carved deep into its face and filled with something that
glints like gold. Moss has crept up its sides but leaves the rune clear.
The path runs east to a warm, thyme-covered bank and west toward the
glass lanterns of a great tree. The leaves overhead are so thick that
the light comes through in shades of green and amber.

extra_descs.stone rune waystone:
The rune is a simple shape, a straight line crossed by a curve like a
drawn bow, and the gold in its grooves is not paint but sap that has
dried hard and bright. Elves set such stones to mark the ways to their
trees.

1339.name: In The Radiant Forest

north.description: To the north lies In The Radiant Forest.

east.description: To the east lies At A Great Tree.

west.description: To the west lies In The Radiant Forest.

1339.description:
A sunny bank rises here, covered with wild thyme and small purple
flowers that release a warm, peppery scent when crushed. The trees stand
back from it a little, and the light lies on the bank like honey in a
dish. East the cleft trunk of a great tree looms over the roots, north a
path leads to a woven arch, and west the way continues under silver
boughs. It is warm here, warmer than anywhere else in the wood.

1340.name: At A Great Tree

north.description: To the north lies In The Radiant Forest.

east.description: To the east lies In The Radiant Forest.

south.description: To the south lies In The Radiant Forest.

west.description: To the west lies In The Radiant Forest.

up.description: To the up lies Stairs On A Humongous Tree.

1340.description:
The great tree here has split near its base into two vast trunks that
lean apart and then grow together again far overhead, leaving a tall
cleft between them. A stair once climbed up through the cleft toward
Elvandar, but a curtain of ivy and wild rose has grown over its lower
steps, so thick and thorny that the way up is closed. Paths lead off
north, east, south and west among the roots. Petals from the wild roses
lie scattered on the moss.

1341.name: In The Radiant Forest

south.description: To the south lies In The Radiant Forest.

1341.description:
The trees close in on three sides of this small glade, leaving only the
way south open. White anemones carpet the ground so thickly that there
is hardly room to set a foot between them. At the far end someone has
bent a row of young saplings together and bound their tops with grass,
making a living bower just tall enough to sit beneath. Light falls
through the leaves in soft gold shafts that barely move.

1342.name: In The Radiant Forest

north.description: To the north lies In The Radiant Forest.

east.description: To the east lies In The Radiant Forest.

1342.description:
The ground dips into a broad hollow here, and the wind has filled it
knee-deep with fallen leaves, gold on top and brown and soft beneath.
Wading through them raises a dry, sweet smell like old parchment. The
way climbs out north among young saplings and east toward a mossy
boulder where a spring rises. The leaves shift and settle behind you,
hiding your tracks almost at once.

1343.name: In The Radiant Forest

east.description: To the east lies In The Radiant Forest.

south.description: To the south lies The Edge Of The Radiant Forest.

west.description: To the west lies In The Radiant Forest.

1343.description:
A boulder furred with green moss squats among the roots here, and from a
crack at its foot a spring wells up and spills away in a thread of
bright water. Several faint paths meet beside it, as though everyone who
passes stops to drink. One runs east along an avenue of tall trunks,
another west into a leaf-filled hollow, and a third south toward the
dark line of the forest's edge. The water tastes cold and faintly of
stone.

1344.name: In The Radiant Forest

east.description: To the east lies In The Radiant Forest.

west.description: To the west lies In The Radiant Forest.

1344.description:
Two rows of tall, straight trees stand here as evenly spaced as the
pillars of a temple, their silver trunks rising without a branch for
twenty feet before they break into crowns of pale gold. Leaves drift
down between them so slowly that they seem to hang in the air. The
avenue runs east toward a still pool and west deeper into the wood. Your
footsteps make no sound at all on the deep leaf litter.

1345.name: In The Radiant Forest

north.description: To the north lies In The Radiant Forest.

south.description: To the south lies The Edge Of The Radiant Forest.

west.description: To the west lies In The Radiant Forest.

1345.description:
A still pool lies in a hollow among the roots, so clear that the gold of
the canopy seems to float on its surface like fallen leaves. Its banks
are soft with moss and starred with tiny white flowers. A narrow glade
opens to the north, the trees thin toward the forest's edge to the
south, and a path of flattened grass leads west between the trunks. The
light gathers on the water here and lingers long after it should have
faded.

1346.name: A Corner In The Radiant Forest

north.description: To the north lies At The Edge Of The Radiant Forest.

east.description: To the east lies The Edge Of The Radiant Forest.

south.description: To the south lies In The Old Forest.

1346.description:
A slender pillar of white stone stands at this corner of the radiant
wood, cracked and leaning, with a single leaf carved near its top. The
Old Forest crowds up to it from the south and the west, a dark mass of
yew and oak whose shadows stop at the foot of the pillar as if they dare
go no further. Along the bright margin the way runs north and east.
Bindweed has wound its pale trumpets around the base of the stone.

extra_descs.pillar white stone leaf carving:
The leaf is carved with such care that every vein shows, and beneath it
runs a line of flowing elven script, too weathered to read. The stone is
faintly warm to the touch, even in shadow.

1347.name: The Edge Of The Radiant Forest

1347.description:
A huge, hollow oak of the Old Forest leans over the border from the
south, its black limbs reaching into the light like a hand stretched
toward a fire. Beneath it a ring of grey toadstools has sprung up on the
very line where gold leaves give way to brown. The edge runs east and
west, and north a path winds back among the radiant trees toward a mossy
spring. The air grows colder with every step toward the oak.

1348.name: The Edge Of The Radiant Forest

east.description: To the east lies The Edge Of The Radiant Forest.

1348.description:
A shallow stream slips out from under the golden trees here and runs
south into the Old Forest, and you can watch its water change as it
goes, bright and chattering on this side, dark and silent beyond. A line
of stepping stones crosses it just short of the boundary. Ferns crowd
both banks, green and lush here and blackened further on. The forest's
edge continues east and west along the border.

1349.name: The Edge Of The Radiant Forest

1349.description:
Brambles heavy with blackberries tangle along the southern edge of the
golden wood, and a gap has been trampled through them where some large
beast has pushed its way south into the Old Forest. Beyond the gap the
ground drops into a gloom of roots and nettles. The edge runs on east to
a corner of the wood and west beneath arching boughs, while north the
radiant trees open around a still pool. Birdsong drifts down from the
canopy, untroubled by the darkness so close by.

1350.name: A Corner In The Radiant Forest

1350.description:
This is the last corner of the radiant wood, and the Old Forest presses
against it from the east and the south alike, its gnarled trunks wrapped
in ivy and its floor lost in shadow. A thicket of holly grows along the
boundary, dark leaves glossy against the pale gold overhead. Cold mist
seeps between the stems and thins away to nothing a few paces inside the
light. The bright margin of the forest leads north and west from here.

1801.name: The Meadow Thrithing

1801.description:
The Meadow Thrithing begins here where the stony slopes give way to
grass, its long blades brushing your knees and rippling away in silver
waves. West, the land rises toward the foot of the mountains, scattered
with grey boulders that have tumbled from the heights. The meadow
spreads east and south, bright with buttercups. A cold wind comes down
off the slopes and sets the grass hissing.

1802.name: The Meadow Thrithing

1802.description:
A lone hawthorn stands in the long grass here, bent almost double by the
wind, its thorns hung with tufts of wool and coarse horsehair. Around it
the grass has been trampled into a ring where wild horses come to
scratch themselves against the trunk. The meadow stretches east, south
and west, rolling gently over low swells of ground. Beyond the grass the
mountains stand grey and close against the sky.

1803.name: The Meadow Thrithing

1803.description:
Poppies grow among the grass here in such numbers that the meadow looks
splashed with red paint. The ground rises into a low hummock crowned by
an ant hill as large as a beehive, and from its top you can see the
grass rolling on and on. The meadow runs east toward a glint of water,
south across a shallow dip and west toward a wind-bent thorn. The dry
chirring of crickets fills the air.

1804.description:
The grass grows lush and dark here as the ground slopes toward the Long
Lake, and the air smells of water and wet earth. Clumps of rushes rise
among the grass, and the soil gives softly underfoot. East, the meadow
ends at the lakeshore, where the water glitters beyond a fringe of
reeds. The grassland stretches away south and west, and the wind brings
the cool breath of the lake across it.

1805.name: By The Shore Of The Long Lake

south.description: To the south lies By The Shore Of The Long Lake.

west.description: To the west lies The Meadow Thrithing.

1805.description:
The meadow comes down to the Long Lake here in a gentle slope of short
turf, ending at a narrow beach of grey shingle. The lake stretches away
so far that its farther shore is only a faint blue line, and small waves
come in with a steady hush. An old rowing boat lies upturned on the
shingle, its planks grey and split. The shore runs south among the
reeds, and west the long grass of the meadow rises.

1806.name: The Meadow Thrithing

1806.description:
The Meadow Thrithing opens here beside the end of the plains road, which
lies just west across a strip of stony ground. Wheel ruts and hoof marks
have pressed a faint track into the grass, fading as it heads out into
the meadow. The grass runs north toward the mountain slopes, and east
and south it rolls away in long silver swells. The wind smells of grass
and distant rain.

1807.name: The Meadow Thrithing

1807.description:
A ruined shepherd's hut stands in the grass here, little more than a
ring of knee-high stone walls with a gap for a doorway. Nettles fill the
inside. The meadow spreads around it, rolling north toward a wind-bent
thorn and away east, south and west. The mountains loom closer here,
their lower slopes dark with heather.

1808.name: The Meadow Thrithing

1808.description:
The Meadow Thrithing is at its widest here, a sea of grass that bends
and rises in waves under the wind, with nothing to break it but a few
clumps of thistle. The sky feels enormous overhead. You can wade through
the grass north, east, south or west, and in every direction it looks
much the same. Seeds and burrs cling to your clothes at every step.

1809.name: The Meadow Thrithing

1809.description:
The grass here has been grazed short by wild horses, and the turf is
dotted with daisies and clover. A great flat stone lies half sunk in the
ground, warm from the sun, with shallow grooves worn into it where
generations of shepherds have whetted their knives. East, the meadow
slopes to the reedy shore of the Long Lake, and the grass rolls on
north, south and west.

1810.name: By The Shore Of The Long Lake

1810.description:
Tall reeds rise from the shallows here, their brown heads nodding over
water so still that the sky lies on it unbroken. A path of trodden mud
runs along the shore between the reeds and the meadow, printed with the
tracks of wading birds and the hooves of horses come down to drink. The
shore leads north to a shingle beach and south toward a stand of
willows. West, the meadow grass climbs gently away from the water.

1811.description:
The meadow's edge lies close to the ruins of Townsbridge here: the road
passes beneath the burnt arch of the old coaching inn just to the north,
and west stands the shell of a great barn with its wall fallen open to
the grass. The long grass grows thick around the scattered stones. The
meadow runs east and south, away from the ruins. A smell of old ash
lingers on the air.

1812.name: The Meadow Thrithing

1812.description:
The blackened walls of Townsbridge's ruined coaching inn stand just to
the north, where the road through the plains passes beneath its arch,
and the meadow grass has crept right up to the soot-stained stones.
Nettles and willowherb grow thick along the foot of the walls. The
meadow runs east, south and west. Even the wind seems to shun the ruin,
and the grass near it barely stirs.

1813.name: The Meadow Thrithing

1813.description:
The meadow runs right up to the end of the plains road here, and the
road's stony bank lies just to the north, thick with gorse. Cart ruts
run a little way into the grass and stop. The long grass stretches east
toward a lone oak and south across the open land, and west it follows
the line of the old road. The yellow gorse flowers give off a sweet,
nutty smell in the warmth.

1814.name: The Meadow Thrithing

1814.description:
A great old oak stands alone in the meadow here, its crown spreading
wide over a circle of shade where the grass grows thin. Its lowest
branch has been worn smooth by generations of herders sitting on it, and
initials are cut deep into the bark of the trunk. The meadow stretches
north, east, south and west from the shade of the oak. Acorns crunch
underfoot.

1815.name: The Meadow Thrithing

1815.description:
The meadow dips here into a shallow bowl, sheltered from the wind, where
the grass grows lush and tall and the air lies warm and still. Wild
horses have rolled here, leaving round, flattened patches in the grass.
The ground rises gently again to the north, east, south and west.
Cornflowers grow in the bottom of the bowl, as blue as a summer sky.

1816.name: The Meadow Thrithing

north.description: To the north lies The Meadow Thrithing.

east.description: To the east lies The Meadow Thrithing.

west.description: To the west lies The Meadow Thrithing.

1816.description:
An old boundary ditch crosses the meadow here, so overgrown that you see
it only when you are about to step into it. Along its bank grows a line
of crooked crab-apple trees, their small sour fruit scattered in the
grass. The meadow continues north, east, south and west, and the ditch
runs off into the grass on either hand. Long ago, someone thought this
land was worth dividing.

1817.name: The Meadow Thrithing

1817.description:
Meadowsweet grows in creamy drifts here, its heavy scent rising from the
damp ground near the lake. A broken post leans in the grass, the last
remnant of a fence that someone once tried to build across the
Thrithing. East, willows trail their fronds in the water at the lake's
edge, and the meadow runs north, south and west around you. The grass
here stays wet with dew long into the day.

1818.name: By The Shore Of The Long Lake

north.description: To the north lies By The Shore Of The Long Lake.

south.description: To the south lies By The Shore Of The Long Lake.

west.description: To the west lies The Meadow Thrithing.

1818.description:
Willows lean far out over the Long Lake here, trailing their long green
fronds in the water so that each tree seems to be drinking. Beneath them
the shore is a tangle of roots and soft black mud. A small wooden jetty,
its posts slimy with weed, runs a few paces out into the lake. The
shoreline continues north among the reeds and south toward the edge of a
wood, and the meadow lies west.

1819.name: The Meadow Thrithing

1819.description:
The meadow ends here where the plains begin, and the difference is easy
to see: the lush grass of the Thrithing gives way west to shorter,
sparser growth and patches of bare earth. Old plough ridges still show
beneath the plains grass, the remains of Townsbridge's fields. The
meadow runs north, east and south. Thistles stand in ragged ranks along
the boundary.

1820.name: The Meadow Thrithing

1820.description:
A burnt-out hay wagon lies on its side in the grass here, its wheels
charred to their iron rims and its bed long since rotted through.
Brambles have grown up through the wreck and hold it in a thorny
embrace. The meadow stretches north toward the ruins of Townsbridge,
east and west across the grass, and south to the edge of the woods.
Rosehips glow red among the brambles.

1821.name: The Meadow Thrithing

north.description: To the north lies The Meadow Thrithing.

east.description: To the east lies The Meadow Thrithing.

1821.description:
Molehills scatter the meadow here in dozens of small brown heaps, and
the grass between them is short and patchy. A crooked wild pear tree
stands among them, heavy with small hard fruit. The meadow runs north
toward the end of the plains road, east toward a hidden stream and west
across open grass, while south the edge of the woods lies close. The
soil turned up by the moles is dark and rich.

1822.name: The Meadow Thrithing

1822.description:
A stream winds through the meadow here in a channel cut deep into the
soft earth, so hidden by overhanging grass that you hear it before you
see it. A flat stone has been laid across it as a bridge. The meadow
continues north, east and west, and south it runs down to the edge of
the woods. Watercress grows thick in the clear, slow water.

1823.name: The Meadow Thrithing

west.description: To the west lies The Meadow Thrithing.

1823.description:
A ring of grey standing stones, none taller than your waist, stands half
hidden in the grass here. Lichen has crusted them yellow and white, and
the grass inside the ring grows shorter and greener than the meadow
around it. The meadow stretches north, east and west, and south the
woods begin. No one has ever moved these stones, though the Thrithing
has been grazed and crossed for longer than anyone remembers.

extra_descs.stones ring standing:
There are nine stones, each marked on its inner face with a faint
spiral. Shepherds say the ring is older than Garathorm, and that a foal
born inside it will never be taken by wolves.

1824.name: The Meadow Thrithing

1824.description:
The grass grows shorter here as the meadow nears the woods, and bracken
has begun to creep out into it in bright green patches. A pair of young
birches stand alone in the open like scouts sent ahead of the forest.
South, the edge of the woods lies a short walk away, and the meadow
spreads north, east and west. The ground is dry and sandy beneath the
grass.

1825.name: The Meadow Thrithing

1825.description:
The meadow is broken here by a shallow, reedy pond, where ground water
seeps up through the grass and lies still and brown. Yellow flag irises
grow along its margin, and the mud around it is pocked with hoofprints.
East the land falls away to the lakeshore, south the white wall of the
Birch Woods begins, and the meadow runs north and west. The pond smells
of mud and crushed rushes.

1826.name: By The Shore Of The Long Lake

north.description: To the north lies By The Shore Of The Long Lake.

south.description: To the south lies At The Edge Of The Woods.

west.description: To the west lies The Meadow Thrithing.

1826.description:
The shore curves here, and the first white birches come down almost to
the water, their reflections shivering in the small waves. Flat stones
along the waterline make good places to sit, and a ring of blackened
stones shows where someone has made a fire. North the shore runs on
beneath willows, south lies the edge of the woods, and west the meadow
grass gives way to a reedy pond. Mist often gathers on the lake here,
drifting in over the stones.

1827.name: At The Edge Of The Woods

east.description: To the east lies At The Edge Of The Woods.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

1827.description:
The meadow, the woods and the plains meet here in a broad corner of
rough grass. West, the plains stretch away toward the ruins of
Townsbridge, whose broken gables can just be seen. The birches begin to
the south, the meadow lies north, and the margin of the woods runs east.
A boundary stone, leaning and half buried, marks some old division of
the land.

1828.name: At The Edge Of The Woods

north.description: To the north lies The Meadow Thrithing.

1828.description:
The edge of the woods here is a tangle of elder and dog rose, with the
white birches rising behind. Elderflowers hang in creamy plates, filling
the air with a heavy sweetness. A gap in the tangle leads south into the
woods, while north the meadow opens out and the margin runs east and
west. A few charred fence posts still stand in the grass, the remains of
an old field boundary.

1829.name: At The Edge Of The Woods

north.description: To the north lies The Meadow Thrithing.

east.description: To the east lies At The Edge Of The Woods.

west.description: To the west lies At The Edge Of The Woods.

1829.description:
A hunting blind of woven birch branches has been built low among the
bracken at the edge of the woods here, facing out over the meadow where
the horses graze. It is cleverly made and hard to spot until you are
almost on top of it. North lies the open grass, south the Birch Woods,
and the margin runs east and west. The bracken around it has been
carefully left uncut.

1830.name: At The Edge Of The Woods

north.description: To the north lies The Meadow Thrithing.

east.description: To the east lies At The Edge Of The Woods.

south.description: To the south lies The Birch Woods.

1830.description:
The stream from the meadow runs into the woods here, slipping under a
bank of roots and vanishing among the birches. Kingcups grow bright
yellow along its edge, and the ground is soft and wet. North lies the
open meadow, south the white trunks of the Birch Woods, and the margin
of the trees runs east and west. The air is cool and smells of wet moss.

1831.name: At The Edge Of The Woods

north.description: To the north lies The Meadow Thrithing.

east.description: To the east lies At The Edge Of The Woods.

south.description: To the south lies The Birch Woods.

west.description: To the west lies At The Edge Of The Woods.

1831.description:
Wild raspberry canes crowd the margin of the woods here, a thorny tangle
between the meadow grass and the first birches. An old woodcutter's
stack of birch logs, grey and furred with moss, sits at the edge of the
trees. The meadow lies north, the woods south, and the margin runs east
and west. The logs have lain here so long that saplings grow from them.

1832.name: At The Edge Of The Woods

north.description: To the north lies The Meadow Thrithing.

east.description: To the east lies At The Edge Of The Woods.

south.description: To the south lies The Birch Woods.

west.description: To the west lies At The Edge Of The Woods.

1832.description:
A low bank topped with hazel and blackthorn marks the edge of the woods
here, and beyond it the birches crowd together. A narrow gap has been
worn through the hedge by the passing of many feet. North lies open
meadow, south the Birch Woods, and the bank runs east and west along the
margin. Sloes hang dusky blue on the blackthorn, bitter enough to make
your mouth pucker.

1833.name: At The Edge Of The Woods

north.description: To the north lies The Meadow Thrithing.

east.description: To the east lies At The Edge Of The Woods.

south.description: To the south lies The Birch Woods.

west.description: To the west lies At The Edge Of The Woods.

1833.description:
The long grass of the meadow breaks against the woods here like a green
sea against a white shore. A single tall birch stands out in the grass
ahead of the others, as though it had stepped forward to keep watch. The
meadow opens to the north, the Birch Woods begin to the south, and the
margin runs east and west between them. Harebells nod on a low bank
where the two meet.

1834.name: At The Edge Of The Woods

south.description: To the south lies The Birch Woods.

west.description: To the west lies At The Edge Of The Woods.

1834.description:
Here the meadow, the lake and the woods all meet. Birches crowd thick to
the south, their white trunks bright against the shadows between them,
while north the ground slopes down to the shore of the Long Lake.
Bracken grows waist-high along the margin of the trees, already turning
bronze at its tips. A trail runs west along the edge of the woods. The
cool damp of the lake hangs in the air.

1835.name: The Birch Woods

1835.description:
The Birch Woods begin here on the edge of the open plains, which stretch
away west under a wide sky, flat and grey-green. A few birches have
strayed out into the grass, small and stunted by the wind. The woods run
east and south, and north lies the margin of the meadow. Underfoot, the
plains grass and the woodland leaves mingle.

1836.name: The Birch Woods

west.description: To the west lies The Birch Woods.

1836.description:
Birch polypores bulge from many of the trunks here like grey-white
shelves, and one dead tree is so crowded with them that it looks like a
stack of plates. The woods are dim and quiet, the canopy thick overhead.
Paths lead north to the edge of the woods and east, south and west
deeper among the trees. The smell of damp wood and fungus is strong.

1837.name: The Birch Woods

north.description: To the north lies At The Edge Of The Woods.

east.description: To the east lies The Birch Woods.

south.description: To the south lies The Birch Woods.

west.description: To the west lies The Birch Woods.

1837.description:
Old birches with thick, rough-barked trunks stand here, their branches
hung with long grey lichen that sways like an old man's beard. The
ground beneath is soft with fallen leaves and the crumbled remains of
dead branches. Paths lead north to the edge of the woods, south toward a
place of cut stumps and stacked poles, and east and west among the
trees. It is quieter here than in the rest of the woods.

1838.name: The Birch Woods

north.description: To the north lies At The Edge Of The Woods.

east.description: To the east lies The Birch Woods.

south.description: To the south lies The Birch Woods.

west.description: To the west lies The Birch Woods.

1838.description:
The stream from the meadow wanders through the birches here in a bed of
brown pebbles, and the trees lean over it from both banks. Moss and
ferns grow thick along the water, and a fallen trunk makes a bridge
across it. Paths lead north toward the edge of the woods and east, south
and west through the trees. The water chuckles softly over the stones.

1839.name: The Birch Woods

north.description: To the north lies At The Edge Of The Woods.

east.description: To the east lies The Birch Woods.

south.description: To the south lies The Birch Woods.

west.description: To the west lies The Birch Woods.

1839.description:
Bracken grows shoulder-high between the birches here, its newest fronds
still unrolling from tight brown fists. A path has been beaten through
it, winding north toward the edge of the woods and dividing to run east,
south and west. The bracken hides the ground completely, and the path
feels close and green. Webs strung between the fronds glitter with dew.

1840.name: The Birch Woods

north.description: To the north lies At The Edge Of The Woods.

east.description: To the east lies The Birch Woods.

south.description: To the south lies The Birch Woods.

west.description: To the west lies The Birch Woods.

1840.description:
Somebody has tapped the birches here for their sap: small wooden spouts
have been driven into several trunks, and the bark beneath them is
stained dark and sticky. These trees are tall and old, their bark gone
rough and grey near the ground. Paths lead north toward the edge of the
woods and east, south and west among the white trunks. The air carries
the faint, sweet smell of sap.

1841.name: The Birch Woods

north.description: To the north lies At The Edge Of The Woods.

east.description: To the east lies The Birch Woods.

south.description: To the south lies The Birch Woods.

west.description: To the west lies The Birch Woods.

1841.description:
The birches here are young and slender, growing so close together that
their trunks make a pale fence on every side. Their leaves rustle
constantly, even when there seems to be no wind at all. North, the trees
thin out toward the edge of the woods and the meadow beyond, and paths
wind east, south and west among the white stems. Patches of moss glow a
vivid green in the dappled light.

1842.name: The Birch Woods

north.description: To the north lies At The Edge Of The Woods.

south.description: To the south lies The Birch Woods.

west.description: To the west lies The Birch Woods.

1842.description:
Silver birches stand close together here, their papery bark peeling in
white curls and marked with black scars like half-closed eyes. Their
small leaves let through a green, flickering light that dances over the
ground with every breath of wind. The Birch Woods grow brighter to the
north, where they thin toward the lake, and run on south and west in
pale ranks. Red-capped toadstools speckled with white grow in clusters
among the roots.

1843.name: The Birch Woods

north.description: To the north lies The Birch Woods.

east.description: To the east lies The Birch Woods.

south.description: To the south lies The Birch Woods.

1843.description:
The birches grow in a long line here along the top of an old earth bank,
as though they had been planted as a hedge long ago and left to grow
wild. Their roots grip the bank like knotted fingers. Paths lead north,
east and south along and through the line of trees. Below the bank the
ground is soft and deep with dead leaves.

1844.name: The Birch Woods

north.description: To the north lies The Birch Woods.

east.description: To the east lies The Birch Woods.

south.description: To the south lies The Birch Woods.

west.description: To the west lies The Birch Woods.

1844.description:
An old charcoal burners' hearth lies here among the birches, a round
patch of black earth where nothing grows. The rangers use the cleared
ground for archery, and a straw target hangs from a branch at the far
side, bristling with old arrow holes. Paths lead north, east, south and
west. Woodsmoke from the camp drifts through the trees.

1845.name: The Birch Woods

north.description: To the north lies The Birch Woods.

east.description: To the east lies The Birch Woods.

south.description: To the south lies The Rangers Camp.

west.description: To the west lies The Birch Woods.

1845.description:
The birches have been thinned here by careful cutting, the stumps cut
clean and low, and stacks of poles lie seasoning in neat piles. The
Rangers Camp lies just to the south, and the crackle of its fire carries
through the trees. Trails lead north, east and west through the woods.
The ground is covered with fresh chips of white wood.

1846.name: The Birch Woods

north.description: To the north lies The Birch Woods.

east.description: To the east lies The Birch Woods.

south.description: To the south lies The Birch Woods.

west.description: To the west lies The Birch Woods.

1846.description:
Here the stream spreads into a small, clear pool among the birches, its
surface spotted with fallen leaves. Reflections of the white trunks
shiver in it whenever the wind stirs. The pool drains away under a bank
of roots, and paths lead north, east, south and west around it. A flat
stone has been set at the water's edge, worn smooth by the knees of
rangers filling their water skins.

1847.name: The Birch Woods

north.description: To the north lies The Birch Woods.

east.description: To the east lies The Birch Woods.

south.description: To the south lies The Birch Woods.

west.description: To the west lies The Birch Woods.

1847.description:
A small spring rises among the birches here and spreads into a boggy
patch thick with moss and cotton grass, whose white tufts bob above the
green. Someone has laid a line of split logs across the wettest part.
Firmer ground leads north, east, south and west around the bog. The
water is brown with peat but cold and clean.

1848.name: The Birch Woods

north.description: To the north lies The Birch Woods.

east.description: To the east lies The Birch Woods.

south.description: To the south lies The Birch Woods.

west.description: To the west lies The Birch Woods.

1848.description:
The birches give way here to a small stand of dark pines, and the ground
beneath them is bare and brown with fallen needles. The change is so
abrupt that the light seems to dim, and the air smells of resin instead
of grass. Paths lead out of the pines north, east, south and west into
the brighter birch woods. Pine cones crunch underfoot.

1849.name: The Birch Woods

north.description: To the north lies The Birch Woods.

east.description: To the east lies The Birch Woods.

south.description: To the south lies The Birch Woods.

west.description: To the west lies The Birch Woods.

1849.description:
A clearing opens among the birches here, floored with soft grass and
edged with foxgloves whose purple spires stand taller than a child. A
ring of flat stones in the middle holds the ashes of many small fires,
swept neat after each one. Paths lead off north, east, south and west
between the white trunks. The air is still and warm in the shelter of
the trees.

1850.name: The Birch Woods

north.description: To the north lies The Birch Woods.

south.description: To the south lies The Birch Woods.

west.description: To the west lies The Birch Woods.

1850.description:
A birch has fallen here and rotted from the inside out, leaving only its
tough white bark lying on the ground like a long, hollow pipe. Moss and
tiny ferns have taken root along it. The trees around stand close, and
the wind in their leaves makes a sound like rain on a roof. Paths lead
north, south and west between the white trunks, over leaf litter so thin
that the black earth shows through.

1851.name: The Birch Woods

north.description: To the north lies The Birch Woods.

east.description: To the east lies The Birch Woods.

1851.description:
The Birch Woods end against a steep rocky bank here, its face hung with
ferns and dripping with water from a spring somewhere above. The water
collects in a basin of moss at the foot of the bank before trickling
away. Ways lead north and east through the trees. The rock is cold and
slick, and green with liverwort.

1852.name: The Birch Woods

north.description: To the north lies The Birch Woods.

east.description: To the east lies The Rangers Camp.

west.description: To the west lies The Birch Woods.

1852.description:
A well-trodden path leads east from here into the Rangers Camp, where a
fire burns in a ring of stones beneath the grey crag. Birch branches
have been cut and laid along the path's muddiest stretches. North lies a
patch of blackened earth where charcoal was once burned, and west the
woods grow thicker. The smell of woodsmoke and cooking drifts from the
camp.

1853.name: The Rangers Camp

north.description: To the north lies The Birch Woods.

east.description: To the east lies The Birch Woods.

west.description: To the west lies The Birch Woods.

up.description: To the up lies Climbing The Mountain.

1853.description:
The rangers of the Long Lake have made their camp in a clearing among
the birches, at the foot of a grey crag that rises sheer above the
trees. Lean-tos of birch poles and bark stand around a large fire pit
ringed with stones, and racks for drying hides and fish stand nearby. A
rope ladder hangs down the face of the crag, and above it a narrow path
climbs up the mountain. Trails lead north, east and west into the woods.

extra_descs.map deerskin hide frame:
A deerskin stretched on a frame has been painted with a map of the
country around: the meadow, the lake, the birch woods and the road to
Townsbridge. Red marks show where bears and wolves have been seen, and a
black cross has been drawn over the burnt village.

1854.name: The Birch Woods

north.description: To the north lies The Birch Woods.

east.description: To the east lies The Birch Woods.

west.description: To the west lies The Rangers Camp.

1854.description:
The smell of woodsmoke drifts through the birches here from the Rangers
Camp just to the west, and the ground is trodden bare along a well-used
path. Several of the trunks have been notched with the rangers' leaf
mark. The path leads west to the camp, while other trails run north
toward a woodland pool and east deeper into the woods. The crag that
rises behind the camp shows grey through the leaves.

1855.name: The Birch Woods

north.description: To the north lies The Birch Woods.

east.description: To the east lies The Birch Woods.

west.description: To the west lies The Birch Woods.

1855.description:
The birches grow tall and widely spaced here, with soft grass between
them and the occasional mossy stump. Their crowns sway far overhead, and
the wind among them sounds like the sea. A trail leads north toward a
boggy spring, and others run east and west through the white trunks.
Through the trees you can make out the grey crag that rises above the
Rangers Camp.

1856.name: The Birch Woods

north.description: To the north lies The Birch Woods.

east.description: To the east lies The Birch Woods.

west.description: To the west lies The Birch Woods.

1856.description:
A great grey boulder sits among the birches here, as big as a cottage
and split down the middle by a crack you could squeeze into. Birch
seedlings have rooted in the crack and in every pocket of soil on its
top. Trails lead north into a stand of dark pines and east and west
through the woods. Moss and lichen paint the boulder in patches of
green, grey and orange.

1857.name: The Birch Woods

north.description: To the north lies The Birch Woods.

east.description: To the east lies The Birch Woods.

west.description: To the west lies The Birch Woods.

1857.description:
A ranger's mark has been cut into a birch trunk here, a leaf inside a
circle, the cuts darkened and swollen with age. Beneath it a narrow
trail runs east and west through the woods, packed hard by careful feet.
To the north the trees open a little around a clearing. The bark of the
marked tree has healed in thick black ridges around the cuts, like lips
closed over a secret.

1858.name: The Birch Woods

north.description: To the north lies The Birch Woods.

west.description: To the west lies The Birch Woods.

1858.description:
The birches grow in a thick, tangled clump here, many trunks springing
from a single great stool where an old tree was coppiced long ago.
Beyond them the woods end in a thicket of holly and bramble too dense to
pass. The only ways out lie north and west through the white trunks.
Bramble runners catch at your ankles, and the blackberries on them are
small and sour.

2300.name: The Dusty Road

east.description: To the east lies The Dusty Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Edge of the Forest.

2300.description:
The Dusty Road earns its name at once: a broad track of pale, powdery
earth that coats boots and hems in fine grey dust. Low stone walls line
both sides, enclosing fields of stubble and tall sunflowers. Cart ruts
have baked as hard as pottery in the sun. West, the golden trees of the
Radiant Forest stand like a bright wall, and the road runs on east under
an open sky.

2301.name: The Dusty Road

east.description: To the east lies The Dusty Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Dusty Road.

2301.description:
A dead oak stands beside the road here, white and leafless, its bare
branches reaching out over the dust like the arms of a beggar. A rope
swing hangs from its lowest limb, stirring gently in the hot wind.
Little whirls of dust spin up across the fields and collapse. The road
runs straight on east between dry ditches, and west toward the shining
edge of the forest.

2302.name: The Dusty Road

north.description: To the north lies The Dusty Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Dusty Road.

2302.description:
The Dusty Road turns north here at a corner marked by a stunted thorn
tree, its branches hung with faded rags tied there for luck. A hedge of
wild roses runs along the bend, and dust lies in soft drifts against its
roots. North, the road heads toward the smoke of a small village, and
west it runs back toward the forest. The sky feels huge and empty after
the shelter of the trees.

2303.name: The Dusty Road

east.description: To the east lies The Dusty Road.

south.description: To the south lies The Dusty Road.

2303.description:
The road bends east here around a field of tall maize whose dry leaves
rattle in every breath of wind. An old well stands at the roadside under
a sagging wooden hood, its mouth boarded over and weighted with stones.
Small bare footprints run and skip across the dust. The road runs east
toward the first cottages and back south to the corner by the thorn
tree.

2304.name: The Dusty Road

east.description: To the east lies Outside A Small Village.

west.description: To the west lies The Dusty Road.

2304.description:
The road runs straight toward a cluster of thatched roofs and
whitewashed walls a little way east. In a paddock beside it, washing
lines strung between posts flap with sheets and shirts. Far beyond the
rooftops a darker smudge of woodland marks the country around Salem's
Lot, brooding even in the sunshine. West, the road bends back past the
boarded well.

2305.name: Outside A Small Village

east.description: To the east lies The Dusty Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Dusty Road.

2305.description:
A low gate of grey wood stands open across the road at the edge of the
village, hung between two posts carved with simple suns. Braids of
garlic and sprigs of rowan are nailed above it, a custom kept here
without anyone quite saying why. The dust of the road has been swept
back from the gateway in neat curves. East, the Dusty Road runs on
between the first cottages, and west it leaves the village for the open
fields.

2306.name: The Dusty Road

north.description: To the north lies Inside A Small House.

east.description: To the east lies The Town Square.

south.description: To the south lies Inside A Small House.

west.description: To the west lies Outside A Small Village.

2306.description:
The Dusty Road runs between two small houses here, each with a stout
door, iron-bolted shutters and a tiny herb garden before it. Their doors
open straight onto the road, north and south, and their thresholds are
scrubbed white. Hollyhocks lean against the whitewashed walls. East, the
road widens into the village's little square, and west it leads out to
the gate.

2307.name: Inside A Small House

south.description: To the south lies The Dusty Road.

2307.description:
This small house is a single room under a low, smoke-darkened ceiling,
with a box bed built into one wall and a hearth of rounded river stones
in another. A rag rug softens the earthen floor, and a table and two
stools stand beneath the only window. A heavy bar leans beside the door,
ready to drop into iron brackets at nightfall. The door south leads back
out to the Dusty Road.

2308.name: Inside A Small House

north.description: To the north lies The Dusty Road.

2308.description:
A great wooden loom fills most of this one-roomed cottage, a half-
finished length of blue cloth stretched across its frame. Baskets of
carded wool are stacked by the hearth, and a spinning wheel waits beside
a rocking chair worn pale on its arms. A line of salt has been poured
along the sill of the only window, unbroken from end to end. The door
opens north onto the Dusty Road.

2309.name: The Town Square

north.description: To the north lies A Side Street.

east.description: To the east lies Outside A Small Village.

south.description: To the south lies A Short Path.

west.description: To the west lies The Dusty Road.

2309.description:
The town square is little more than a widening of the road around an old
stone pillar topped with a carved sun, its base ringed by a bench
polished by years of gossip. Low cottages with brightly painted doors
face it on every side. A side street runs north between gardens and a
short path leads south toward a larger house, while the Dusty Road
carries on east out of the village and west toward its gate.

extra_descs.pillar sun carving bench:
The sun carved atop the pillar has a face, round-cheeked and smiling,
worn soft by the weather. A ring of fresh chalk circles the pillar's
base, as though someone redraws it every evening.

2310.name: A Short Path

north.description: To the north lies The Town Square.

west.description: To the west lies Inside The Elder's House.

2310.description:
A short path of scrubbed flagstones leads from the town square to the
door of the largest house in the village, between low hedges of clipped
box. A brass bell hangs from a bracket beside the door, its rope tied
off neatly, for callers to announce themselves. A rowan tree shades the
path, its berries scattered red across the stones. The square lies just
north, and the elder's door opens to the west.

2311.name: Inside The Elder's House

east.description: To the east lies A Short Path.

2311.description:
The elder's house is a wide, low-beamed room that serves as both home
and council chamber, with a long table and benches for a dozen
neighbours at once. Over the hearth a sun is carved into the chimney
breast and gilded, and beside it hangs a painted map of the parish, much
handled. Shelves of ledgers and tithe rolls fill one wall, and the
windows are fitted with iron bars on the inside. The door east leads out
to the short path.

extra_descs.map parish painted:
The map shows the village, its fields and the Dusty Road winding away
past the heath. Where the road runs on toward Salem's Lot the paint has
been rubbed thin by many fingers, and a careful hand has lettered in the
margin: GO BY DAY, AND COME HOME BY DAY.

2312.name: A Side Street

north.description: To the north lies Inside A Small House.

east.description: To the east lies Inside A Small House.

south.description: To the south lies The Town Square.

west.description: To the west lies In The Vegetable Garden.

2312.description:
This narrow side street is little more than a grassy lane between walls
of stacked flint. Two small cottages open off it, one north and one
east, each with a knocker shaped like a horseshoe on its door. West, a
wicket gate leads into a vegetable garden, and south the lane returns to
the town square. A rain barrel stands at the corner, green with moss.

2313.name: Inside A Small House

west.description: To the west lies A Side Street.

2313.description:
This house is a little larger than its neighbours, with a partition of
woven hurdles screening the sleeping corner from the rest. A long table
scarred by years of knife work runs beneath the window, and a dresser
leans slightly where one foot is propped on a flat stone. The hearth is
wide and deep, with an iron crane and a bread oven built into its side.
A plank door leads west onto the side street.

2314.name: Inside A Small House

south.description: To the south lies A Side Street.

2314.description:
This cottage is tiny but spotless, its walls limewashed so often that
the corners have gone soft and round. A high-backed settle stands by the
hearth, where an iron fireback is cast with a pattern of oak leaves.
Bunches of rowan berries hang over the window, and the shutters are
fitted with heavy iron bolts. Its low door gives south onto the side
street.

2315.name: In The Vegetable Garden

east.description: To the east lies A Side Street.

2315.description:
Neat beds of cabbages, leeks, beans on poles and fat orange pumpkins
fill this walled garden, each one edged with boards and weeded with
care. Garlic grows in a long row against the sunny wall, far more of it
than one small village could ever eat. The sun lies warm on the beds,
and the soil smells rich and dark. A wicket gate in the wall leads east
onto the side street.

2316.name: Outside A Small Village

east.description: To the east lies The Dusty Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Town Square.

2316.description:
The last cottage of the village stands here, with a lean-to woodshed and
a chopping block scarred by many winters. Wood smoke curls from its
chimney into the still air. A rough wooden sign beside the road warns
travellers to be within walls by nightfall. Beyond it the Dusty Road
runs out east across open fields toward darker country, and west it
returns to the little town square.

extra_descs.sign wooden warning:
The sign is painted in careful letters: TRAVELLERS, BE WITHIN WALLS BY
DARK. Underneath, in a shakier hand, someone has added: AND OPEN TO NO
ONE AFTER.

2317.name: The Dusty Road

east.description: To the east lies The Dusty Road.

west.description: To the west lies Outside A Small Village.

2317.description:
Beyond the village the Dusty Road runs on across a wide, bare heath, the
dust darker here and gritty underfoot. Stunted pines lean away from the
wind, and the fields give way to gorse and heather. The breeze carries a
faint chill, though the sun is bright. East, the road winds on toward
the distant woods, and west the thatched roofs of the village sit snug
behind their walls.

2318.name: The Dusty Road

north.description: To the north lies The Dusty Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Dusty Road.

2318.description:
The heath gives out against a long wall of grey fieldstone, and the
Dusty Road turns sharply north to follow it. Old flagstones show through
the dust here, laid by some long-forgotten road-builder and heaved apart
by frost. A rusted iron ring is set into the wall at the corner, perhaps
for tethering horses in busier days. West, the road runs back across the
heather toward the village, its thatch just visible above the gorse.

2319.name: The Dusty Road

east.description: To the east lies The Dusty Road.

south.description: To the south lies The Dusty Road.

2319.description:
A wayside post stands at this bend, crowned with a disc of beaten tin
cut in the shape of a sun and dulled by rain. Someone still tends it: a
fresh braid of garlic hangs from a nail, and pebbles have been laid in a
careful ring around its foot. The Dusty Road swings east here between
low walls, and runs back south along the fieldstone wall to the corner.
The wind off the heath sets the garlic swinging.

2320.name: The Dusty Road

east.description: To the east lies The Dusty Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Dusty Road.

2320.description:
The road runs straight between walls of piled stone, past the shell of a
farmhouse whose roof has fallen in upon its own rafters. Its fields have
gone to thistle and dock, and a plough lies rusting in the furrow where
it was last left. No smoke rises anywhere in sight. East, the road
carries on toward a line of tall elms, and west it bends back toward the
sun-post.

2321.name: The Dusty Road

east.description: To the east lies The Dusty Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Dusty Road.

2321.description:
A squat milestone of red sandstone leans at the roadside, its face cut
with letters that someone has tried hard to chisel away. Tall elms begin
here, planted in a row along the verge long ago, and their roots have
lifted the edge of the road into ridges. The dust lies thinner in their
shade. The Dusty Road runs on east beneath the elms and back west past
the ruined farm.

extra_descs.milestone sandstone letters:
Most of the lettering has been hacked away, but the deep-cut numeral II
survives, and beneath it the ghost of an S and an L. The chisel scars
are old and weathered smooth, as though someone long ago wished
travellers not to know how near Salem's Lot lay.

2322.name: The Dusty Road

north.description: To the north lies The Dusty Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Dusty Road.

2322.description:
An old gibbet stands at this corner of the road, a tall black post with
an arm from which an empty iron cage hangs on a chain. The cage creaks
when the wind moves it, and the grass beneath has never grown back.
Whoever last hung there is long forgotten, though the ground below is
still strewn with salt. The road turns north here under the last of the
elms and runs back west along their line.

2323.name: The Dusty Road

east.description: To the east lies The Dusty Road.

south.description: To the south lies The Dusty Road.

2323.description:
A low wall of mossy stone encloses a small graveyard beside the road,
entered by a roofed lychgate whose timbers have gone silver with age.
Inside, the headstones lean at tired angles, and several graves are
caged over with iron grilles, as if to keep something in rather than
out. The lychgate is shut fast, its latch bound with knotted twine. The
Dusty Road bends east past the graveyard wall and runs back south toward
the gibbet.

2324.name: The Dusty Road

north.description: To the north lies The Dusty Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Dusty Road.

2324.description:
A stone cottage stands close by the road here, its shutters nailed fast
and a crude sun daubed across its door in whitewash that has run in the
rain. The garden before it is a tangle of nettles grown higher than the
gate. Beyond its roof the dark woods have drawn much nearer. The road
turns north past the cottage wall, and west it leads back toward the
graveyard.

2325.name: The Dusty Road

east.description: To the east lies The Dusty Road.

south.description: To the south lies The Dusty Road.

2325.description:
Here the Dusty Road becomes a street, paved again with flags and lined
by narrow houses of grey stone that share their walls. Every door is
shut and every window shuttered, though a few window boxes still hold
the dry brown stalks of geraniums, as if their owners meant to come
back. A cast-iron pump stands at the kerb with its handle chained down.
The street runs east between the houses and back south past the nailed
cottage.

2326.name: The Dusty Road

north.description: To the north lies The Dusty Road.

east.description: To the east lies The Dusty Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Dusty Road.

2326.description:
The houses end at the foot of a steep, scrub-covered ridge, and the road
divides. North, a branch of it plunges into the black mouth of a tunnel
cut through the rock, its arch built of dressed stone and blotched with
lichen. A cold draught breathes out of the dark. East, the main road
runs toward a long, low building of tarred timber that straddles the
way, and west lies the shuttered street.

2327.name: The Dusty Road

east.description: To the east lies The Dusty Road.
