south.description: To the south lies Town Line.

west.description: To the west lies The Dusty Road.

2327.description:
A long tollhouse of tarred black timber straddles the road here, and the
Dusty Road runs east into it through a pair of great doors propped open
with stones. South, a narrow lane once led toward Town Line and Salem's
Lot, but a gate of iron bars has been set across it and chained, and
bunches of withered garlic hang from every crossbar. Brambles choke the
lane beyond the bars. West, the road returns to the fork beneath the
ridge.

2342.name: The Dusty Road

north.description: To the north lies The Dusty Road.

south.description: To the south lies The Dusty Road.

2342.description:
Daylight from the tunnel mouth to the south reaches a little way along
the walls and then fails. The tunnel is broad enough for a wagon, its
walls of fitted grey blocks sweating with damp, and old cart ruts run
deep into the stone floor. Empty niches for lamps are set into the walls
at intervals, black with the soot of flames long since gone out. The way
runs on north into darkness.

2343.name: The Dusty Road

north.description: To the north lies The Dusty Road.

south.description: To the south lies The Dusty Road.

2343.description:
Deep inside the tunnel the darkness is almost complete, and every
footstep comes back doubled from the curved roof. Water drips steadily
from a crack overhead into a shallow pool worn in the floor. A refuge
has been cut into one wall, a narrow alcove where a walker could press
back to let a cart go by, and its stone bench is green with slime. The
tunnel runs on north and back south toward the faint grey of daylight.

2344.name: The Dusty Road

north.description: To the north lies Entrance To The Wild Valley.

south.description: To the south lies The Dusty Road.

2344.description:
The air stirs here, drawn along the tunnel by a draught from ahead that
smells of wild grass and, faintly, of old ashes. The stone of the walls
is streaked with long black scorch marks, as though a blast of fire had
once roared through from the far end. The cart ruts stop short a few
paces on, as if no wagon has gone further in living memory. A dim light
shows to the north where the tunnel opens out, and southward the passage
runs back into the dark.

2345.name: Entrance To The Wild Valley

east.description: To the east lies Wild Valley.

south.description: To the south lies The Dusty Road.

2345.description:
The tunnel ends in a high vaulted chamber, once a guardroom, where stone
benches line the walls beneath arrow slits that let in thin blades of
daylight. East, a massive gate of iron bars closes the way out into the
Wild Valley, its lock rusted solid and its bars scorched black and
warped, and words are cut deep into the lintel above it. Through the
bars you glimpse green slopes and broken crags. The tunnel leads back
south into darkness.

extra_descs.words lintel letters carving:
Letters a hand high are cut into the stone above the gate: THE VALLEY IS
NOT YOURS. Beneath them, scratched much smaller and in haste, someone
has added: NOR OURS.

2346.name: The Dusty Road

east.description: To the east lies The Dusty Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Dusty Road.

2346.description:
The road runs on beneath the roof of the tollhouse, a long gallery of
tarred planks where daylight leaks in through the cracks in thin bright
lines. A toll window with a rusted grille looks out from a booth on one
side, and a board above it still lists the old charges in flaking paint.
Straw and dust have drifted against the walls. The gallery runs on east
into gloom, and back west to the great doors and the daylight.

extra_descs.board charges tolls list paint:
The flaking list reads: A CART, TWO PENCE. HORSE AND RIDER, ONE PENNY.
SHEEP AND SWINE, BY THE SCORE. At the bottom a later hand has added in
red paint: NONE AFTER DARK, AT ANY PRICE.

2347.name: The Dusty Road

south.description: To the south lies Town Line.

west.description: To the west lies The Dusty Road.

2347.description:
The tollhouse gallery comes to an end here, and the road meets a second
pair of great doors set in the south wall. They are shut fast, barred
with a beam of oak as thick as a man's waist and nailed across with
planks, beyond which the road would run on to Town Line. Sun signs have
been gouged into the wood with a knife, dozens of them, some crossed out
and cut again. The gallery leads back west toward the daylight.

3060.name: The Great Field Of Garathorm

extra_descs.countryside path: Larks rise out of the grass ahead of your footsteps. On a clear day you can see three church spires and the smoke of four villages.

3060.description:
A path runs through a wide dirt path through the lush, green, fresh
Garathorm countryside. Visible is to the horizon to the north, east, and
west; the busy city of Garathorm lies to the south. All around is healthy
green grass and an occasional large oak tree. The sun feels wonderful on
your face and a pleasant wind blows through your hair. Birds chirp
quietly to themselves and you can smell the faint scent of flowers and
freshly cut grass. You feel like you could lie down in the grass and
stay here forever, surrounded by powerful beauty in all directions. The
path you are on continues north through the field and south back to
Garathorm. The cobblestones are worn smooth by countless feet. Vendors
and pedestrians bustle past.

north.description: You see more of the path through the Great Field.

south.description: To the south lies Turning Point In The King's Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Great Chessboard Of Garathorm.

3061.name: The Great Field Of Garathorm

extra_descs.countryside path: East across the field, a banner marks the Newbie Hall, where the city trains its hopefuls before the world gets a turn at them.

3061.description:
A path runs through a wide dirt path through the lush, green, fresh
Garathorm countryside. Visible is to the horizon to the north, east, and
west; the busy city of Garathorm lies to the south. All around is healthy
green grass and an occasional large oak tree. The sun feels wonderful on
your face and a pleasant wind blows through your hair. Birds chirp
quietly to themselves and you can smell the faint scent of flowers and
freshly cut grass. You feel like you could lie down in the grass and
stay here forever, surrounded by powerful beauty in all directions.
There is a strange structure on the eastern side of the path. A small
dirt path splits off of the main path and leads off to the west. Vendors
and pedestrians bustle past. The smell of smoke and humanity hangs in
the air.

north.description: To the north lies The Garden.

south.description: You see more of the Field.

west.description: To the west lies Entrance to the wine yard.

east.description: To the east lies The Entrance To The Newbie Zone.

15066.name: Road Through The Plains

extra_descs.sign weathered:
The sign reads TOWNSBRIDGE, with an arrow pointing down the road.
Someone has painted a crude skull over the name, and beneath it, in
smaller and shakier letters, TURN BACK.

east.description: The building to the east is merely a shell of what it once probably was.  The walls are blackened as if they had been exposed to fire at some point in the past...

south.description: The stench from the south is almost overpowering now... it seems that the source wouldn't be too far from here.

west.description: A small quiet cottage stands on the west side of the road, apparently untouched by the desecration and destruction that appears to have hit this small village.

15066.description:
The road leaves Garathorm through the Eastern Gatehouse, whose grey
towers rise just to the west, and runs out across the plains toward the
ruins of Townsbridge. A weathered sign stands at the roadside. East, the
road leads to the blackened shell of a burnt shop, the first building of
the dead village. South, a track leads to a pit from which a foul smell
drifts. Wildflowers bloom along the verges as though nothing were wrong.

15071.name: Road Through The Plains
15071.description:
Beside the road stands the burned-out shell of a small shop, its roof
gone and its walls charred black, two of them burnt down to half their
height. Through the gaps you can see the scorched stump of a counter and
heaps of ash where goods once stood. Weeds and wildflowers have begun to
creep in over the blackened sill. The road runs on east across the
plains and back west toward the city gate, while open grassland falls
away south.

east.description: To the east lies Road Through The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: You can see the dirt road to the west.

3220.name: Road Through The Plains

east.description: To the east lies End Of The Plains Road.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies Road Through The Plains.

3220.description:
The road runs right through the gutted shell of what was once
Townsbridge's coaching inn, passing beneath a broad carriage arch whose
stones are still streaked with soot. Charred beams lie where the upper
floor fell in, and a row of empty stalls lines one wall. West, the road
leads through the blackened wall of a burnt shop, east it climbs toward
the hills at the end of the plains road, and a doorway south opens into
another ruin. A painted sign still hangs above the arch, burnt past
reading.

15068.name: Road Through the Plains
15068.description:
The road runs here right through the gutted shell of a house that once
straddled it, in at one gaping doorway and out at the other, under the
charred beams of what is left of the roof. Furniture lies smashed and
flung against the walls as if a whirlwind had raged through, yet
strangely no dust or cobweb lies on any of it. A side door opens east
onto the grassland and another west into a neighbouring ruin. The road
leads on north into the hills, and south to the twin towers of the
Northern Gatehouse.

north.description: To the north lies Road Through The Plains.

east.description: You can see the dirt road through the doorway to the east.

south.description: To the south lies The Northern Gatehouse.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

15062.name: Road Through The Plains
15062.description:
The overgrown track dips into a fold between grassy hills, where broom
and bramble crowd so close that you must push them aside. To the east
the ground climbs to a bare crest with wide views over the plains, and
to the west a deserted cottage sits half hidden in nettles. The track
runs back north toward the King's Road and drops south toward the town
gates. A scarecrow in faded rags leans over a forgotten garden plot.

north.description: The trail continues northwards.

east.description: The trail appears to continue to the east.

south.description: To the south lies Road Through the Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

15061.name: Road Through The Plains
15061.description:
A faint track leaves the King's Road here and wanders south across
rolling, scrubby hills, so little used that grass and thistle have
almost swallowed it. The paved road lies only a few strides away to the
north, yet the noise of its traffic already sounds far off. On either
hand stand low cottages of fieldstone, empty and silent, their doors
hanging open to the east and west. The wind moves through the long grass
with a dry whisper.

north.description: The travel upon the King's Road can be heard off to the north.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: The trail continues southwards.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

203500.name: End Of The King's Road

east.description: To the east lies On The King's Road.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

203500.description:
The King's Road ends here as abruptly as a sentence broken off, its last
paving stones finished with a carved kerb as though the builders meant
to come back. West, beyond the kerb, open grassland rolls away toward a
flat and distant horizon. To the south stands the long, empty front of
an old roadside inn with its door gaping, and east the paved road runs
back toward the Turning Point In The King's Road.

extra_descs.kerb kerbstone carving:
The kerbstones are carved with a running pattern of oak leaves, and the
last of them bears a crown above the words HERE ENDS THE KING'S ROAD.
Beneath, a traveller has scratched AND HERE BEGINS THE WALKING.

203501.name: On The King's Road

east.description: To the east lies Turning Point In The King's Road.

west.description: To the west lies End Of The King's Road.

203501.description:
The King's Road runs on here as wide and smooth as ever, its great
fitted paving stones laid so true that a cart rolls along them without a
jolt. Yet few wheels come this way now, and grass has begun to push up
along the seams. Thick undergrowth crowds the verges on either side.
East lies the Turning Point In The King's Road, and west the paving runs
a short way further to its end.

15000.name: Turning Point In The King's Road
15000.description:
The area opens at the beginning of the actual King's Road. The road is
wide enough for several horses to ride along side by side with room to
spare. The stones which make up the road have been put into place with
such skill that the road seems to be perfectly smooth and perfectly
straight. You spot a small trail leading to the south through the
undergrowth which surrounds the road at this point. A traveller passes
by and waves cheerfully at you. Buildings crowd together on all sides.
The sounds of city life echo around.

north.description: To the north lies The Great Field Of Garathorm.

east.description: The King's Road continues in a straight line to the east towards a grand castle.

south.description: A small overgrown trail leads through the undergrowth to the south.

west.description: To the west lies On The King's Road.

8100.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies End Of The King's Road.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8100.description:
The paving of the King's Road gives out just to the east, and from here
the open plains take over, rolling away beneath a wide sky in long
swells of grass and clover. A path trodden by the inn's servants long
ago still leads south to the kitchen door, though the grass has almost
swallowed it. North and west there is nothing but grassland as far as
the eye can follow.

8101.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8101.description:
Tall grass rises to your waist here, silver-green and ceaselessly
moving, and it is hard to keep any sense of where you have come from.
East and west look so alike that you might be walking in circles. A lone
hawthorn grows on a hummock, bent sideways by the wind. Northward the
grass runs on, and south it slopes gently toward the end of the King's
Road.

8102.name: The Plains

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8102.description:
A shallow pond lies in a fold of the plains here, ringed with reeds and
so still that it mirrors the drifting clouds. The prints of deer and
cattle crowd its muddy edges. Beyond it the land rises into a long, low
ridge of tangled thorn that no path crosses, and the only ways on lie
west and south through the grass.

8103.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8103.description:
An old drove road crosses the plains here, a broad strip where the grass
grows shorter and greener, trampled for generations by herds bound for
the markets of Garathorm. A squat marker stone stands beside it, half
sunk in the turf. The drove road fades away east toward the end of the
King's Road and west into the grass, and the open plains run on north
and south.

extra_descs.marker stone notches:
The stone is cut with a simple picture of a cow and a row of notches, a
drover's tally of the days left to market. The notches end at seven, and
beside the seventh someone has carved a tiny smiling face.

8104.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8104.description:
A lone oak stands in the grass here, split down the middle by some old
stroke of lightning, one half dead and silver-grey and the other still
in leaf. The ground beneath it is bare and trampled, a favourite resting
place for beasts seeking shade. Grassland runs out north, south, east
and west, each way much like the others.

8105.name: The Plains

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8105.description:
A roofless sheepfold of piled fieldstone stands here, its walls tumbled
in places and its gateway choked with brambles. Tufts of greasy wool
still cling to the stones where sheep once rubbed against them, though
no shepherd has penned a flock here in years. The plains stretch away
east, west and south under the open sky.

8106.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8106.description:
The grass is shorter here, cropped close by grazing beasts and dotted
with yellow cowslips and the white stars of daisies. A low roof of sod
shows just to the south, where the shepherd's hut lies half hidden in a
dip. The plains roll on north, east and west in gentle swells, broken
only by the odd thorn bush.

8107.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8107.description:
A tall cairn of fist-sized stones stands beside a faint path here,
raised stone by stone by travellers who each add one as they pass, for
luck on the road. Scraps of ribbon have been tucked between the stones,
faded now to the colour of dry grass. Faint paths lead away from the
cairn north, south, east and west, as though it were the hub of a great
wheel.

8108.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8108.description:
A shallow gully winds across the plains here, cut by a stream that runs
only after heavy rain, and its dry bed is paved with smooth, pale
pebbles. Willow scrub grows along its banks. It is easy enough to cross
and go on north or south, while the gully itself leads east and west
through the grass.

8109.name: The Plains

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8109.description:
The ground lifts into a gentle swell here, and from its crown the plains
lie spread out like a rumpled green blanket. Far off, a smudge of
chimney smoke marks where Garathorm must stand, and a grey line of
mountains rides the horizon. The grass slopes away south and west toward
lower ground.

8110.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

8110.description:
A broken cartwheel lies half sunk in the turf here, its spokes jutting
up through the grass like the ribs of some long-dead beast. Thistles
grow thick around it, purple-headed and humming with bees in the summer.
The plains stretch away north and east, while beyond them the land falls
into dense scrub that nobody has any reason to cross.

8111.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

8111.description:
Badgers have heaped mounds of pale earth among the grass here, and well-
worn runs lead away from the mouths of their setts. The ground is uneven
and riddled with holes, treacherous going for any horse. The plains run
north and south along a straggling line of hawthorns, and east toward a
tall cairn of stones.

8112.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8112.description:
A leaning post of grey wood stands in the grass here, crowned with the
bleached skull of an ox. Herders set up such posts to mark the edge of
safe grazing, and beyond it the grass grows taller and wilder. The
plains run on north, east and south, and west toward a country where the
grass seems never to end.

8113.name: The Plains

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

8113.description:
A ring of blackened stones marks an old campfire here, where some
traveller once spent a night out on the open plains. The grass has grown
back around it thick and lush, sprinkled with scarlet poppies. The
plains run on east and south, with nothing to break the view but the
slow march of the clouds.

8114.name: The Plains

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Never Ending Plains.

8114.description:
Here the ordinary plains give way to something vaster. West, the grass
grows tall and unbroken, rippling away toward a horizon that never seems
to come any nearer, and travellers call that country the Never Ending
Plains. Few who enter it keep a straight course for long. East,
friendlier grassland leads back toward the herders' skull post.

8115.name: The Never Ending Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Never Ending Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Never Ending Plains.

8115.description:
The sun-bleached wreck of a covered wagon lies on its side in the grass
here, its canvas long gone and its iron hoops arching up like a row of
empty doorways. Someone has scratched a tally of days into its
tailboard, neat at first and then ragged, stopping at sixty-three.
Trampled ways lead north and west through the grass.

8116.name: The Never Ending Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Never Ending Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Never Ending Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Never Ending Plains.

8116.description:
The bleached bones of a horse lie in a hollow among the grass here,
still half held together by dried sinew, with the rotted leather of a
saddle beneath its ribs. Of its rider there is no sign at all. The grass
runs north and south, and to the west it stretches on with a sameness
that makes the eyes ache.

8117.name: The Never Ending Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Never Ending Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Never Ending Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Never Ending Plains.

8117.description:
Grass taller than a man surrounds you on every side here, swaying in
long, slow waves that hiss like surf on a beach. Every way looks the
same, and walking west only seems to bring you back to this same
trampled spot. Paths of a sort are pressed north and south through the
stems, and east the grass thins toward the more ordinary plains.

8118.name: The Never Ending Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Never Ending Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Never Ending Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Never Ending Plains.

8118.description:
The grass grows in great tussocks here, and between them the ground is
soft and springy underfoot. Wander north or west and the plains only
fold you back among the same tussocks and the same crushed stems. The
way south seems the one sure path out. The wind has a voice in this
place, a low and endless sigh.

8119.name: The Never Ending Plains

east.description: To the east lies The Never Ending Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Never Ending Plains.

8119.description:
The grass parts here around a shallow pool of brackish water, ringed by
a crust of white salt and churned by the cloven prints of some heavy
beast. The water tastes bitter, but it may be the only water for miles.
The grass stretches on east and west, as endless as ever.

8120.name: The Never Ending Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Never Ending Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Never Ending Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Never Ending Plains.

8120.description:
A wide swathe of grass has been trampled flat here, as though a great
herd passed this way not long ago, and the earth is churned and pocked
with heavy hoofprints. Flies drone over the drying dung. The trail of
the herd runs north, the grass rises again to the east, and westward it
closes into another dizzying sameness.

8121.name: The Never Ending Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Never Ending Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Never Ending Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Never Ending Plains.

8121.description:
Wildflowers grow in a sudden blaze of colour here, blue cornflowers,
yellow ragwort and the white lace of yarrow, so thick that the plain
seems to have been painted. Their scent hangs heavy and sweet in the
still air. The flowers run on north and south, but to the west the grass
swallows them again.

8122.name: The Never Ending Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Never Ending Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Never Ending Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Never Ending Plains.

8122.description:
A lone standing stone rises out of the grass here, twice the height of a
man and leaning a little, its sides worn by the wind into soft ripples.
Travellers lost on these plains often steer by it, only to find it
behind them again an hour later. The grass runs north and south past its
foot, and west it rolls on without a mark.

extra_descs.standing stone words:
Low on the stone, half hidden by grass, someone has cut the words I HAVE
PASSED THIS STONE FOUR TIMES. Beneath them, in a different hand, is the
single word FIVE.

8123.name: The Never Ending Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Never Ending Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Never Ending Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Never Ending Plains.

8123.description:
The plains lift into a broad, low dome here, and from its top the grass
can be seen stretching away to a horizon as flat as a ruled line. Not a
tree, not a roof, not a wisp of smoke breaks it anywhere. Northward the
land only seems to repeat itself, but a way leads south toward a leaning
stone and another west into deeper grass.

8124.name: The Never Ending Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Never Ending Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Never Ending Plains.

8124.description:
Something huge has slept here: the grass is crushed flat in a hollow the
size of a cart, and the ground around it is littered with gnawed bones
and the splintered staves of a wooden chest. The stink of sweat and old
meat lingers in the air. A trampled way leads north, while west the
grass only circles back upon itself.

8125.name: The Never Ending Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Never Ending Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Never Ending Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Never Ending Plains.

8125.description:
Grass and sky are all there is here, the one gold-green and endless, the
other pale and empty. A faint trail, perhaps made by wandering beasts,
bends through the stems from north to south, and another branches off
west. Your own footprints vanish behind you almost as soon as you make
them.

8126.name: The Never Ending Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Never Ending Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Never Ending Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Never Ending Plains.

8126.description:
A deep hollow sinks into the plains here, sheltered from the wind, and
at its bottom the grass grows thick and dark around a seep of muddy
water. The air is close and heavy with the smell of wet earth. Ways
climb out of the hollow north and south, and west the grass rolls on
beyond its lip.

8127.name: The Never Ending Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Never Ending Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Never Ending Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Never Ending Plains.

8127.description:
The wind blows steadily here and never seems to tire, combing the grass
flat in long silver streaks. A ragged strip of red cloth is tied to a
stake driven into the ground, a marker left by someone who hoped to find
this place again. North, the grass closes back in on itself, while east
and south it opens a little.

8128.name: The Never Ending Plains

east.description: To the east lies The Never Ending Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Never Ending Plains.

8128.description:
A line of ancient paving stones breaks through the grass here, tilted
and cracked, the first sign of some road older than any map. The turf
rises and falls over them so that they appear and vanish again as you
walk. The old stones lead west, and the grass runs back east into the
plains.

8129.name: The Never Ending Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Ruined Road.

east.description: To the east lies The Never Ending Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Never Ending Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Never Ending Plains.

8129.description:
The grass thins around the end of an old road here, whose broken paving
heads off north between two toppled pillars of carved stone. South and
west the plains swirl on in their endless sameness, but the road at
least promises somewhere to go. East, the grass leads back toward the
scattered paving stones.

extra_descs.pillars toppled carved figures:
Both pillars lie on their sides, each carved with a band of marching
figures in crested helmets and long cloaks. Their faces have been worn
away by the wind, but their spears all point the same way, up the road.

8130.name: The Ruined Road

north.description: To the north lies The Ruined Road.

south.description: To the south lies The Never Ending Plains.

8130.description:
The Ruined Road runs north here, its great paving slabs heaved and
cracked by the roots of grass and thorn. Here and there a slab still
bears the deep grooves of chariot wheels from some forgotten age, and
low walls of tumbled stone line the way. South, the road fades out among
the Never Ending Plains.

8131.name: The Ruined Road

north.description: To the north lies The Ruined Highway.

south.description: To the south lies The Ruined Road.

8131.description:
The road broadens as it runs north, and beside it stands the shell of a
roadside shrine, a roofless box of fitted stone with an empty plinth
inside. Thorn bushes have rooted in its corners, and the plinth is
scored with the marks of tools, as though its figure was prised away.
South, the road narrows back toward the plains.

8132.name: The Ruined Highway

north.description: To the north lies The Ruined Road.

south.description: To the south lies The Ruined Road.

8132.description:
Here the old road becomes a highway broad enough for four wagons
abreast, raised on an embankment above the grass and edged with kerbs of
dressed stone. Statues once lined it in pairs; now only their feet
remain, standing on their plinths, enormous and sandalled. The highway
runs north toward a distant shape of walls and towers, and south it
narrows into the ruined road.

8133.name: The Ruined Road

north.description: To the north lies Outside the Gate of Kashmir.

south.description: To the south lies The Ruined Highway.

8133.description:
The highway narrows back into a ruined road as it climbs toward a great
gate, whose twin towers loom just to the north. Rubble from fallen
outworks lies scattered across the paving, half buried under grass and
wild thyme. South, the broad highway runs back toward the plains, its
line of empty plinths dwindling into the distance.

8134.name: Outside the Gate of Kashmir

east.description: To the east lies Inside The Western Gate Of Mishrak.

south.description: To the south lies The Ruined Road.

8134.description:
The Gate of Kashmir rises here, two massive towers of weathered yellow
stone joined by an arch tall enough for a siege tower to pass beneath.
Its bronze-sheathed doors stand shut and barred, green with age, and no
sound comes from the city of Mishrak beyond them. The way east lies
through those doors, but they will not open. South, the ruined road
leads back toward the plains.

extra_descs.doors bronze gate:
The doors are sheathed in bronze plates, each embossed with a rayed sun,
and they are barred from within. Long ago someone hammered on them hard
enough to dent the metal, and no one ever answered.

15065.name: The Plains
15065.description:
The rutted dirt track crosses open grassland here between two abandoned
houses, their shutters nailed tight and their thatch black with rot. The
house to the north still has its roof, but the one to the east stands
dark and silent, and even the wind seems to hush beside it. A sour smell
of decay drifts up from the south, where the track continues. West, the
tall grass rolls away toward the empty plains.

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: You can hear a wailing sound coming from the house to the east.

south.description: The dirt road continues towards the south where a horrible smell permeates the air.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8150.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

8150.description:
Low, grassy mounds lie in rows here, each about the length of a man,
with nothing to mark them but an occasional stick driven into the earth.
These are older graves than those in the pit to the north, dug with more
care and long since grown over. The plains run east from here, flat and
empty. Even on the brightest day the place feels cold.

8151.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8151.description:
This was the village alehouse, and its trestle tables still stand in
rows, though every bench has been flung over and the shelf behind the
bar has been swept bare. A dark stain spreads across the floorboards
before the cold hearth, scrubbed at long ago and never quite removed.
Doors lead out south to the dirt road, west to a small path and east
into an overgrown yard, and an inner door opens north into the smithy.

15064.name: The Plains

extra_descs.signpost sign board:
The board once read WELCOME TO TOWNSBRIDGE in cheerful green letters.
Someone has gouged a line through the first word, and beneath it carved
a long row of small crosses, too many to count at a glance.

north.description: An trail leads into the heavy undergrowth to the north.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: The dirt road continues through the village to the south.

west.description: A house stands a short distance off the west side of the road, its door hanging ajar.

15064.description:
A small path leaves the dirt road here and wanders in among the houses
of the village, its ruts grown over with plantain and clover. A
weathered signpost leans at the corner, its painted board split by
frost. The open door of an empty alehouse lies to the east and a wrecked
house gapes to the west, while the path climbs north onto a grassy rise
and runs south back to the dirt road.

15063.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: The undergrowth begins to open up to the south and you can see what appears to be a small village to the south.  It is very quiet, almost too quiet.

west.description: The overgrown trail continues to the northwest.

15063.description:
A low grassy rise lifts this corner of the village a little above its
rooftops, and on its crown stands a timber frame from which the village
bell once hung. The bell is gone, and only a rotted rope still dangles
from the crossbeam, stirring in the wind. Beyond the trees the pale
towers of Welmar's Castle can be seen. The chapel lies north, the smithy
east, a small path leads south among the houses, and an overgrown trail
runs west into the woods.

8154.name: The Plains

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies Road Through The Plains.

8154.description:
The village chapel is a single bare room, its benches overturned and its
little altar of fieldstone split clean across. A carved wooden sheaf of
wheat, the sign of Helver, still hangs crookedly on the wall behind it.
Leaves have drifted in through the empty windows to gather in the
corners. A door opens west onto an overgrown trail, another south onto a
grassy rise, and a third east into the bakehouse.

extra_descs.sheaf wheat carving helver:
The carving is plain country work, a sheaf bound with a carved cord and
worn smooth where hands have touched it in passing. A long iron nail has
been driven through its centre, hard and deliberate, pinning it to the
wall.

8155.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8155.description:
This was the village smithy, and the great anvil still stands on its
stump in the middle of the floor, red with rust. The forge is cold and
choked with old ash, its leather bellows rotted to rags, and the tool
rack on the wall hangs empty. Wide double doors open west onto a grassy
rise, while doorways lead north to the bakehouse, east to the weaver's
house and south to the alehouse.

8156.name: The Plains

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8156.description:
A domed bread oven of clay and brick takes up the whole of one wall in
this bakehouse, its mouth black and cold. The long kneading trough
beneath the window is furred with grey mould, and the flour bins along
the walls have been gnawed through and stand empty. Doorways lead west
into the chapel, south into the smithy and east into the next house
along.

8157.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies On The King's Road.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8157.description:
A gap between the houses of the King's Road leads straight into a vast
old tithe barn standing at the edge of the plains, its roof held up on
oak posts as thick as trees. Hay is heaped high in the bays, and the mud
nests of swallows crust the beams overhead. Great doors stand open to
the north and south, and lower doors in the side walls lead east and
west into the byres and sheds beyond. Dust hangs glittering in the
shafts of light from the doorways.

8158.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8158.description:
A great wooden loom fills most of this room, its warp threads long since
rotted and hanging in grey tatters like old cobwebs. A cradle lies
tipped on its side beside the cold hearth, and a spinning wheel stands
with its spokes snapped. Doorways open north and east into further
rooms, and west into the smithy next door, while a back door leads south
into a weedy yard.

8159.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8159.description:
An overgrown yard lies between the empty houses of the village here, the
grass knee-high around a well whose wooden cover has rotted through.
Nettles have swallowed what was once a vegetable garden, though a few
cabbages gone wild still show among them. Doorways stand open to the
north and west, the dark, shuttered house looms to the south, and the
rank grass runs on east between the buildings.

15069.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies Road Through The Plains.

west.description: You can see the dirt road through the doorway to the west.

15069.description:
This house of Townsbridge is dark even by day, its shutters nailed fast
from the inside and its air colder than any weather can explain. Broken
chairs are heaped against the walls, and long scratches score the
plaster as though something once tried to claw its way through it.
Doorways lead north to an overgrown yard, east into another dark room,
and south through a scorched gap into a burnt-out shop, while the front
door opens west onto the dirt road.

8161.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies Road Through The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8161.description:
This cottage on the edge of Townsbridge kept half its roof when the
village burned, and charred rafters still hold up a sagging mat of
thatch over one end of the room. Beneath it lie the remains of a
family's life: a toppled dresser, a cold hearth, a stool scorched black.
A doorway north opens onto the grassland, a passage south leads toward
the road through the village, and a low doorway west gives onto a room
so dark that nothing inside can be seen. The air tastes of soot.

8162.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8162.description:
Open grassland stretches away all around, flat and wind-combed, with
nothing taller than a thistle to break it. North stands the low stone
shelter of the shepherds, and south the blackened gable of a ruined
cottage rises out of the grass, the first of the burnt houses of
Townsbridge. The plains run on west beneath a wide, pale sky. The wind
carries a faint, stale smell of old burning.

8163.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8163.description:
Shepherds have built this low shelter of fieldstone and turf where the
farmland gives way to the open plains, and it is snug against the wind,
if not against the smell of sheep. Hurdles of woven hazel lean against
one wall, and a hearth of blackened stones holds the ashes of an old
fire. Doors lead north into the byre, west into a neighbouring shed and
south out onto the grassland. Tufts of greasy wool cling to every rough
edge of the stone.

8164.name: The Plains

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8164.description:
This long cattle byre has been built onto the end of the tithe barn, its
stalls divided by worn wooden rails and its floor of beaten earth
sloping toward a drain. Iron tethering rings are set into the wall at
the height of a cow's head, and the place smells of dung and old straw,
though the stalls stand empty. A door west leads back into the barn, and
another south opens toward a low stone shelter. Small high windows let
in a pale, dusty light.

8165.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8165.description:
This little stone hut is a shepherd's shelter, with a roof of sod, a
single bunk of planks and a hearth no wider than a bucket. Its walls
have slumped and split, and gaps open in all four of them onto the
grassland to the north, south, east and west. Someone has kept the
hearth swept and stacked a little dry kindling beside it, though there
is no other sign of who.

8166.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8166.description:
The back of the old inn rises just to the east, a long wall of
whitewashed stone gone grey and blotched with lichen, with a kitchen
door hanging open in it. A rubbish midden behind the inn has long since
grassed over into a low green mound, studded with shards of broken
crockery. To the west a small hut stands alone in the grass, and the
plains run on north and south.

8167.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8167.description:
The back of the inn turns a corner around this patch of grass, with a
storeroom door to the east and the wash-house door to the south, both
ajar and dark within. A rusted iron ring for tethering a horse is set
into the wall between them. West, a lonely hut squats in the grass, and
north the plains run along the back of the inn.

8168.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8168.description:
The inn's kitchen is a big, smoke-darkened room built around an open
hearth so wide that a man could stand upright in it, its spit and pot-
hooks still in place above the ashes. A long table runs down the middle,
warped now and split along its grain. Doors open north and west onto the
grassland behind the inn, while the common room lies east and a
storeroom south.

8169.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8169.description:
Shelves rise to the ceiling in this storeroom, still lined with
stoneware crocks and jars, though most are cracked and all are empty.
Rows of iron hooks for hams and flitches of bacon hang bare from the
beams, and something has gnawed a hole through the bottom of the flour
bin. A back door opens west onto the plains, and doorways lead north to
the kitchen, east to the stable and south to the wash-house.

8170.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8170.description:
This was the inn's wash-house, with a great copper boiler set in brick
in one corner and a stone sink beneath a pump that has long run dry. A
mangle with rollers of pale wood stands rusting by the wall, and empty
laundry lines still sag across the room. A back door opens west onto the
open plains, and doorways lead north to a storeroom, east to the coach
house and south to the hay barn.

8171.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies End Of The King's Road.

east.description: To the east lies Road Through The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8171.description:
This long, low common room was once the first welcome of the inn at the
end of the King's Road, but its fire has been cold for years. Tables and
settles stand beneath a grey fur of dust, and the inn's painted sign, a
lantern on a blue field, hangs askew above the hearth. Doors lead out
north onto the road's end and east onto an overgrown trail, while inner
doorways open west to the kitchen and south to the stables.

8172.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies Road Through The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8172.description:
A row of wooden stalls runs down one side of this stable, their mangers
still holding a little hay gone black and brittle with age. Harness pegs
line the walls, all empty, and the smell of horse has long since faded
into one of damp and mice. A wide door east opens onto an overgrown
trail, and doorways lead north to the common room, west to a storeroom
and south into the coach house.

8173.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies Road Through the Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8173.description:
An old coach stands propped on blocks in this coach house, its wheels
gone and its doors hanging open on a seat slashed to the stuffing.
Cobwebs hang in heavy grey sheets from the rafters, and the floor is
printed with the tracks of bare feet. A gap knocked through the wall to
the east leads into a wrecked house, and doorways open north to the
stable, west to the wash-house and south into a hay barn.

8174.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies Road Through the Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8174.description:
Old hay is heaped high against the walls of this barn, sour and grey on
top and still faintly sweet beneath. A deep hollow has been pressed into
the largest heap, as though something heavy sleeps there, and the straw
around it is scattered with gnawed bones. A side door opens east into a
wrecked house, and doorways lead north to the coach house and west to
the wash-house.

8181.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies Road Through The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

8181.description:
This small cottage stood closest to the road, and though its thatch is
gone, a few charred rafters still span the walls and a lean-to of rotten
planks shelters one corner. A table lies overturned there beside a
broken spinning wheel. The doorway north opens onto the road, and a gap
in the east wall looks out toward the pit, from which a dreadful smell
drifts in. The walls are scored with long scratches that no tool made.

15067.name: The Plains
15067.description:
The dirt road ends at the edge of a great pit, and here the smell of
decay becomes almost unbearable. The pit is a mass grave, its sides
crumbling into a jumble of bones, skulls and rotting shrouds, and some
of the bodies look far too fresh for a village that has stood empty for
years. Rank grass grows tall and dark around its rim. A narrow track
leads back north to the road, an empty house stands to the west, and
open plains stretch away east and south.

north.description: Just near the north edge of the pit a small and narrow trail leads away.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8183.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies Road Through The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8183.description:
This is the back of Townsbridge, where the gardens and yards of the
village once ran down to the fields. North stands the blackened shell of
a burnt shop, and east the walls of a great barn. West the ground falls
away toward a pit, and the stench rising from it is enough to make your
eyes water. The plains run south, open and empty under the sky.

8184.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8184.description:
The plains are flat and featureless here, the grass beaten down along a
faint trail that runs from the ruined village toward the south. A sour,
rotten smell drifts on the wind from somewhere close by, and a few small
bones lie bleached among the thistles. The plains continue north toward
the ruins, east toward an abandoned field and west across empty grass.
Nothing grows here taller than your knee.

8185.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8185.description:
An old well stands alone in the open here, its stone ring still sound
but its windlass gone and its little roof fallen in. A dropped pebble
falls a long way before a faint splash comes back up. Whatever farmstead
once stood beside it has vanished, leaving only the well. The plains run
north, east, south and west around it, flat and windswept.

8186.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies Road Through The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Meadow Thrithing.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8186.description:
This was once Townsbridge's great barn, and its stone walls still stand
to the eaves, though the roof has fallen in at one end and its timbers
lie blackened across the floor. The east wall has collapsed outward,
opening the barn to the long grass of the meadow. A doorway north leads
to the road through the village, and others open south and west onto the
plains. Charred grain lies drifted in the corners, black and hard as
gravel.

8187.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Meadow Thrithing.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8187.description:
A scarecrow's cross stands crooked in an abandoned field here, its rags
long since rotted away, its arms still spread as if to warn off birds
that stopped coming years ago. Coarse grass and docks have swallowed the
crop rows. North rise the walls of a burnt barn, east the lush grass of
the meadow begins, and the plains run south and west. The wind moves
through the grass with a dry, whispering sound.

8188.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies At The Edge Of The Woods.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8188.description:
A rusted plough lies abandoned in the grass here, its share still buried
in the earth where it stopped mid-furrow, as though the ploughman simply
walked away. Grass has grown up through its frame. East the land rises
to the edge of the woods, and the plains stretch north, south and west.
Yarrow and ragwort grow everywhere, the flowers of land that no one
tends.

8189.name: The Plains

north.description: To the north lies The Plains.

east.description: To the east lies The Birch Woods.

west.description: To the west lies The Plains.

8189.description:
The plains meet the birch woods here, and the first white trunks stand
just to the east, bright against the grey-green grass. A sheepfold of
piled stones has half collapsed nearby, its gate gone and its walls
sliding into the turf. The plains stretch north and west, empty and
quiet. The grass here is short and tough, cropped close by the wind.

8200.name: On The King's Road

north.description: To the north lies On The King's Road.

east.description: To the east lies On The King's Road.

south.description: To the south lies The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies On The King's Road Outside The Castle.

8200.description:
The King's Road runs wide and well paved here, lined with tall, narrow
houses of plastered timber whose window boxes spill with flowers. West,
the road leads on toward the moat and graceful towers of Welmar's
Castle, and east it carries on out of the castle town. A gap between the
houses opens south onto the plains. A crooked lane wanders off north
among the chimneys, only to bend round on itself and bring you back to
this same spot.

8201.name: On The King's Road

east.description: To the east lies On The King's Road.

west.description: To the west lies On The King's Road.

8201.description:
Here the King's Road narrows between the last houses of the castle town,
and the paving gives way to older, rounder cobbles. A horse trough of
carved stone stands against one wall beneath a bronze spout shaped like
a lion's head. East, the road passes under the long timber roof of a
covered market, its shadowed mouth hung with lanterns. West, the road
leads back toward the castle and the busier streets.

8202.name: A Slight Bend In The Old Road

east.description: To the east lies A Slight Bend In The Old Road.

west.description: To the west lies An Old Road.

8202.description:
The old road bends gently here, and someone has taken care of it: the
potholes are packed with gravel and the ditches on either side are
freshly dug. A split-rail fence runs along a pasture where the grass is
cropped short, and the smell of woodsmoke drifts from somewhere ahead.
The road curves on east toward the village and runs back west across the
open pasture.

8203.name: A Slight Bend In The Old Road

north.description: To the north lies The Entrance To Hommlet.

west.description: To the west lies A Slight Bend In The Old Road.

8203.description:
At this second bend the old road swings north toward Hommlet, whose
thatched roofs and church tower show above a hedge of hazel. A wayside
shrine stands at the turning, a little roofed box on a post holding a
carved wooden figure with a sheaf of wheat in its arms. Someone has
tucked fresh wildflowers along the shrine's ledge. West, the road runs
back along the pasture fence.

extra_descs.shrine wayside figure carving:
The little figure is crudely carved but lovingly painted: a robed farmer
holding a sheaf of wheat to his chest. The villagers say it is Helver,
who keeps Hommlet's fields and the travellers bound for them.

8204.name: The Entrance To Hommlet

north.description: To the north lies Modest Farmhouse And Barn.

east.description: To the east lies A Bend In The Road.

south.description: To the south lies A Slight Bend In The Old Road.

8204.description:
A painted board on a post welcomes travellers to Hommlet in neat
letters, and the road becomes a proper village lane of packed earth and
gravel. North stands a modest farmhouse joined to its barn under a
single long roof of thatch. The lane continues east between hedges
toward a bend, and back south the old road leaves the village behind.
The verges here are scratched bare by roaming hens.

8205.name: Modest Farmhouse And Barn

south.description: To the south lies The Entrance To Hommlet.

down.description: To the down lies Store Room.

8205.description:
House and barn share one roof here, divided only by a low wooden
partition, so that the warmth of the stalls seeps into the living room.
The floor is beaten earth strewn with clean straw, and a plain table and
benches stand near a hearth of fieldstone. A trapdoor in the floor leads
down to the store room, but it has been nailed shut and weighted with a
heavy grain chest. The door south opens onto the village lane.

8206.name: A Bend In The Road

north.description: To the north lies The Prosperous Farm House.

east.description: To the east lies On The Caravan Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Entrance To Hommlet.

8206.description:
The village lane bends here around the corner of a dry-stone wall topped
with moss and yellow stonecrop. North, behind a neat gate, stands a
large and prosperous farmhouse with glazed windows and a slate roof, a
rare luxury so far from Garathorm. East the lane meets the broad Caravan
Road, rutted deep by the wheels of trading wagons, and west it leads
back to the village entrance.

8208.name: The Prosperous Farm House

south.description: To the south lies A Bend In The Road.

8208.description:
This farmhouse is plainly the home of a family that has done well: the
floor is of polished boards, the walls are plastered and limewashed, and
real glass glints in the windows. A carved dresser displays rows of
painted plates, and a long oak table could seat a dozen hungry
farmhands. A tall clock ticks solemnly beside the hearth. The front door
leads south to the lane.

8209.name: On The Caravan Road

north.description: To the north lies The Village Square.

east.description: To the east lies The Well-Kept Farm.

south.description: To the south lies Another Prosperous Farmhouse.

west.description: To the west lies A Bend In The Road.

8209.description:
The Caravan Road runs through the heart of Hommlet here, broad enough
for two wagons to pass, its surface packed hard and scored with ruts. A
well-kept farm lies east behind whitewashed fences, and another
prosperous farmhouse stands south across a little garden of beans and
cabbages. North, the road opens into the village square, and west a lane
bends away between hedges.

8210.name: The Village Square

north.description: To the north lies On The Caravan Road.

east.description: To the east lies On The Old Temple Road.

south.description: To the south lies On The Caravan Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Inn Of The Welcome Wench.

8210.description:
Hommlet's village square is a broad green trodden bare in the middle,
where an ancient elm spreads its branches over a stone drinking trough.
West stands the Inn Of The Welcome Wench, a rambling building of timber
and stone with a swinging sign and smoke rising from two chimneys. East,
the Old Temple Road leads in beneath a long covered walk of timber, and
the Caravan Road crosses the square north and south. A notice board
beside the trough is crowded with village news.

extra_descs.notice board notices:
Pinned notices offer a reward for a lost brown cow, call for strong
hands at the mill, and warn that robbers have been seen on the Caravan
Road toward the Black Woods.

8211.name: The Well-Kept Farm

west.description: To the west lies On The Caravan Road.

8211.description:
The kitchen is the heart of this well-kept farmhouse, flagged with stone
scrubbed almost white and warmed by a wide inglenook where a kettle sits
on the hob. Smoked hams and flitches of bacon hang from hooks in the
beams, and a butter churn stands ready in the corner. Everything is in
its place, from the row of polished boots by the door to the sampler
stitched with the farm's name above the fire. The door west leads back
out to the Caravan Road.

8212.name: Another Prosperous Farmhouse

north.description: To the north lies On The Caravan Road.

8212.description:
This farmhouse rivals its neighbour for comfort and makes a point of it:
a bright woven carpet from some city market covers the floor of the
front room, and pewter plates line a dresser carved with sheaves and
sickles. A great stuffed pike glowers from a glass case above the
fireplace, and a cushioned settle faces the hearth. Through the small,
deep windows you can see a garden of beans and cabbages. The front door
opens north onto the Caravan Road.

8213.name: On The Caravan Road

north.description: To the north lies On The Caravan Road.

east.description: To the east lies The Shope Of The Weaver.

south.description: To the south lies The Village Square.

west.description: To the west lies The Village Hall.

8213.description:
North of the square the Caravan Road is lined with the village's
workshops and public buildings. East, a weaver's shop has its shutters
painted with a loom and shuttle, and west stands the village hall, a
tall timber building with a bell hanging in a little cote on its roof.
The road continues north toward the river and runs south into the
village square.

8214.name: On The Old Temple Road

north.description: To the north lies The Smithy.

east.description: To the east lies On The Old Temple Road.

south.description: To the south lies The End Of The Path.

west.description: To the west lies The Village Square.

8214.description:
The Old Temple Road begins here beneath a long covered walk of timber,
roofed with shingles and open between its posts like a cloister.
Lanterns hang from the crossbeams, and the boards underfoot ring hollow.
North, the glow and smell of hot iron spill from the wide doorway of a
smithy, while to the south a gap between the posts gives onto a footpath
leading off into the trees. The covered walk runs on east, and west it
opens onto the village square.

8215.name: The Inn Of The Welcome Wench

north.description: To the north lies The Private Dining Room.

east.description: To the east lies The Village Square.

south.description: To the south lies The Kitchen Of The Welcome Wench.

west.description: To the west lies The Bar Of The Welcome Wench.

up.description: To the up lies The Top Of The Stairs.

down.description: To the down lies The Secret Store Room.

8215.description:
The common room of the Welcome Wench is long and low, with smoke-
darkened beams, scrubbed floorboards and a stone fireplace big enough to
roast an ox. Trestle tables and benches stand ready for the evening
crowd. The bar opens to the west, an archway south leads to the kitchen,
and a stout door in the north wall closes off a private dining room,
while the front door gives east onto the village square. A staircase
climbs toward the guest rooms, but a rope is stretched across its foot,
and a trapdoor half hidden under a rag rug is bolted fast.

8216.name: The Private Dining Room

south.description: To the south lies The Inn Of The Welcome Wench.

8216.description:
This small, panelled room is kept for guests who can pay for privacy,
and it shows: the oak table is polished to a mirror, the chairs are
cushioned in faded red velvet, and a pair of brass candlesticks stands
ready at either end. A narrow window of thick bottle-glass lets in a
greenish, wavering light. Painted hunting scenes hang on the walls, and
a small fire is laid ready in the grate. The door south leads back to
the common room.

8217.name: The Kitchen Of The Welcome Wench

north.description: To the north lies The Inn Of The Welcome Wench.

up.description: To the up lies Gundigoot's Quarters.

down.description: To the down lies The Store Room.

8217.description:
Heat rolls out of the great hearth that fills one wall of the kitchen,
where iron spits and a blackened cauldron hang over a bed of glowing
coals. Copper pans gleam on their hooks, a long table is dusted with
flour for the day's bread, and strings of onions and garlic dangle from
the beams. A narrow stair climbs steeply to Gundigoot's own quarters,
its door at the top locked fast, and a cellar hatch in the floor is held
shut by a heavy padlock. The way north leads back to the common room.

8218.name: The Bar Of The Welcome Wench

east.description: To the east lies The Inn Of The Welcome Wench.

8218.description:
A long counter of dark oak, worn pale along its edge by countless
elbows, runs the length of the bar, and behind it great casks of ale and
cider rest on their sides in wooden cradles. Pewter tankards hang from
hooks along a beam, each marked with the name or sign of a regular. The
floor is strewn with sawdust that smells of spilled beer. An archway
east opens back into the common room.

extra_descs.tankards hooks beam:
The tankards bear scratched names and signs: a plough, a horseshoe, a
fish, a pair of dice. One hook has a black ribbon tied around it, and no
tankard hangs there.

8226.name: On The Caravan Road

north.description: To the north lies On The Bridge Over The River.

south.description: To the south lies On The Caravan Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Cottage Of The Tailor.

8226.description:
Here the Caravan Road runs between cottages with deep thatch and tidy
kitchen gardens, and a pump with a long iron handle stands on a
flagstone by the verge. West, a cottage with a tailor's shears painted
on its door leans over the road. North, the road dips toward the river
and a stone bridge, and south it leads back past the workshops to the
village square.

8227.name: The Shope Of The Weaver

west.description: To the west lies On The Caravan Road.

8227.description:
A great wooden loom fills most of the weaver's shop, its warp threads
strung tight and a length of half-finished blue cloth wound on its beam.
Skeins of dyed yarn hang from poles across the ceiling, madder red, woad
blue and weld yellow, and the whole shop reeks cheerfully of lanolin and
dye. A spinning wheel waits by the hearth. The shop door gives west onto
the Caravan Road.

8228.name: The Village Hall

east.description: To the east lies On The Caravan Road.

8228.description:
Hommlet's village hall is a single tall room under a roof of open
timbers, where the villagers gather to settle disputes, hold feasts and
hear the news. Long trestle tables are stacked against the walls, and a
raised platform at one end holds the elder's chair and a table draped in
green cloth. A bell rope from the cote on the roof dangles beside the
door, its end worn smooth by many hands. Tall double doors open east
onto the Caravan Road.

8229.name: On The Bridge Over The River

north.description: To the north lies Caravan Road Meeting River Road.

south.description: To the south lies On The Caravan Road.

8229.description:
A sturdy bridge of three stone arches carries the Caravan Road over the
river, its parapets worn smooth by the elbows of idlers. Below, the
water runs broad and brown between reedy banks, and further along the
bank the great wheel of the mill turns slowly in its race. North, the
road passes under the timber roof where it meets the River Road, and
south it climbs back into the village.

8230.name: The Cottage Of The Tailor

east.description: To the east lies On The Caravan Road.

8230.description:
The tailor's cottage is crowded with the tools of the trade: a long
cutting table scored with chalk lines, a wooden dummy wearing a half-
made coat, and pigeonholes stuffed with remnants of every colour. A
bright window lets the light fall full on the table, and the room smells
of wool and beeswax. Pins glint between the floorboards where years of
them have fallen. The door east opens onto the Caravan Road.

8231.name: On The Caravan Road

north.description: To the north lies On The Caravan Road.

south.description: To the south lies On The Caravan Road.

8231.description:
The last houses of Hommlet fall behind here, and the churchyard wall
runs beside the road, its coping furred with moss and overhung by dark
yews. Beyond the wall, old gravestones lean at odd angles in the long
grass. A worn mounting block stands by the verge for riders setting out.
The road heads north out of the village between open fields, and back
south toward the church gate.

8232.name: Caravan Road Meeting River Road

north.description: To the north lies On The Caravan Road.

east.description: To the east lies On The River Road.

south.description: To the south lies On The Bridge Over The River.

west.description: To the west lies On The River Road.

8232.description:
The Caravan Road and the River Road meet beneath a great market roof of
oak shingles, raised on stout posts and walled with planks against the
wind off the river. A merchant's beam-scale hangs from the central tie-
beam, and lanterns on chains light the trodden flagstones even at
midday. Wide openings lead east and west along the River Road, north
toward the church and south onto the bridge.

8233.name: On The Caravan Road

north.description: To the north lies On The Caravan Road.

east.description: To the east lies The Great Hall Of The Church Of Helver.

south.description: To the south lies Caravan Road Meeting River Road.

8233.description:
The Church of Helver dominates this part of the road, a long building of
honey-coloured stone with a square tower and tall arched windows. A
lychgate with a mossy shingle roof opens east onto the path to its great
hall, and the churchyard lawn is neatly scythed. North, the road carries
on out of the village, and south it runs under the market roof at the
meeting of the roads.

8234.name: On The River Road

north.description: To the north lies The Trading Post.

east.description: To the east lies The Eastern End Of The River Road.

west.description: To the west lies Caravan Road Meeting River Road.

8234.description:
The River Road runs along the bank here, with the water sliding past
just beyond a low wall of stone. North stands the trading post, a big
timber building with a wide porch and hitching rails, its sign showing a
pair of clasped hands. The road continues east past the last houses of
the village, and west it passes under the market roof where it meets the
Caravan Road.

8235.name: On The River Road

east.description: To the east lies Caravan Road Meeting River Road.

south.description: To the south lies The Money Changer's Shop.

west.description: To the west lies The End Of River Road.

8235.description:
West of the market roof the River Road is lined with the better sort of
shops, their fronts freshly painted and their doorsteps scrubbed. South,
a narrow stone building with barred windows and a brass sign of a
balance marks the money changer's shop, which stands with its back to
the river. The road runs on west to its end among the craftsmen's homes,
and east beneath the great shingled roof where the two roads meet.

8236.name: The Great Hall Of The Church Of Helver

north.description: To the north lies The Small Antechamber.

west.description: To the west lies On The Caravan Road.

8236.description:
The great hall of the Church of Helver is long and high, its roof held
up by dark oak beams carved with sheaves of wheat and climbing vines.
Rows of plain wooden pews face a carved screen at the far end, and
sunlight falls through tall windows of greenish glass onto a floor of
worn flagstones. A doorway in the screen leads north into a small
antechamber, and the great doors open west onto the Caravan Road.

8237.name: The Small Antechamber

north.description: To the north lies The Altar And Sanctuary.

east.description: To the east lies The Vestry.

south.description: To the south lies The Great Hall Of The Church Of Helver.

west.description: To the west lies The Study And Audience Chamber.

8237.description:
This small, square chamber is panelled in dark wood and lit by a single
bronze lamp hanging on a chain. Three doors open from it: a tall carved
door north into the sanctuary, a plain one east into the vestry, and a
heavy iron-banded door west into the study where the priests receive
visitors. An archway leads south back into the great hall. A faint smell
of incense hangs in the still air.

8238.name: The Altar And Sanctuary

south.description: To the south lies The Small Antechamber.

8238.description:
The sanctuary is the holiest place in Hommlet, a hushed room of pale
stone under a vaulted ceiling painted with golden wheat on a deep blue
ground. A great altar of white marble stands upon three steps, carved
with a sheaf and a rising sun, the signs of Helver. Tall candles burn in
iron stands around it, and their light trembles on the walls. The only
door leads south, back into the antechamber.

extra_descs.altar marble sheaf sun:
Words are carved along the front of the altar: AS THE SEED, SO THE
HARVEST. The marble is worn smooth at one corner where generations of
worshippers have touched it for luck.

8239.name: The Vestry

west.description: To the west lies The Small Antechamber.

up.description: To the up lies The Upper Hall.

8239.description:
Tall wardrobes of carved oak line the walls of this narrow room, where
the priests of Helver robe themselves for worship. A washstand with a
copper basin stands beneath a small window, and a clean scent of
lavender and starch hangs about the room. A narrow stair climbs up
toward the upper hall, but a locked oak door bars it at the top. The
door west opens back into the antechamber.

8240.name: The Study And Audience Chamber

east.description: To the east lies The Small Antechamber.

down.description: To the down lies The Sacred Trophies Gallery.

8240.description:
Here the priests of Helver hear the troubles of the villagers, in a
comfortable room with a broad desk, high-backed chairs and shelves of
leather-bound books. A tapestry of a harvest festival hangs on one wall,
and a small hearth keeps the room warm. In a corner, steps lead down
toward the gallery of sacred trophies, but they end at an iron-bound
door that is locked fast. The door east leads back to the antechamber.

8245.name: The Money Changer's Shop

north.description: To the north lies On The River Road.

8245.description:
A stout counter divides this narrow shop, topped by a brass grille
through which coins pass to and fro. Behind it an iron-bound strongbox
is bolted to the floor, and a pair of fine scales stands under a bell of
glass. Charts of coinage from distant lands are pinned to the panelled
walls, showing the faces of kings and strange beasts. The only door,
heavy and studded with iron, opens north onto the River Road.

extra_descs.charts coinage coins:
The charts show the coins of Garathorm, New Thalos and Port Halyon side
by side, with their weights and their worth in silver. A few are marked
with a red cross, the sign of a known forgery.

8246.name: The End Of River Road

north.description: To the north lies The Cabinet Maker's House.

east.description: To the east lies On The River Road.

south.description: To the south lies The Potter's Cottage.

west.description: To the west lies The Brewery.

8246.description:
The River Road ends in a little square of cobbles where the village's
craftsmen live and work. North, a tall house with a workshop of fresh-
cut timber smells of sawdust and varnish, and south a potter's cottage
has a squat brick kiln smoking behind it. West stands the brewery, a big
stone building fragrant with malt and hops. East, the road leads back
toward the money changer's and the market roof.

8247.name: The Cabinet Maker's House

south.description: To the south lies The End Of River Road.

8247.description:
The cabinet maker's house is half home and half workshop, and fragrant
curls of wood shaving drift into every corner of both. A heavy workbench
with an iron vice runs beneath the window, and racks of seasoning planks
lean against the wall. The living quarters are furnished with the
master's own work, a dresser with doors carved like lace and a settle
with roses on its back. A wide door leads south onto the little square.

8248.name: The Brewery

east.description: To the east lies The End Of River Road.

8248.description:
The brewery is a lofty hall of stone filled with the thick, sweet smell
of boiling malt. Great copper vats sit on brick hearths along one wall,
and fat oak casks are racked to the rafters along the other. The floor
is wet and sticky underfoot, and steam drifts through the light from the
high windows. The door east opens onto the square at the end of the
River Road.

8249.name: The Potter's Cottage
