north.description: To the north lies The End Of River Road.

8249.description:
The potter's cottage is warm from the kiln built against its back wall,
and a fine red dust lies over every surface. A kick-wheel stands in the
middle of the floor, its seat polished by years of use, beside a trough
of wet clay covered with damp sacking. Smears of glaze decorate the
doorframe where the potter wipes his hands. A low door leads north onto
the cobbles at the end of the road.

8250.name: The Trading Post

north.description: To the north lies The Stable.

south.description: To the south lies On The River Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Traders' Room.

8250.description:
The trading post is a single great room of rough timber, with a long
counter across one end and empty shelves behind it rising to the
rafters. The floor is scuffed by the boots of every trader who passes
through Hommlet, and the room smells of leather, tallow and pipe smoke.
A door north leads to the stable, another west to the traders' room, and
the wide front doors open south onto the River Road.

8251.name: The Eastern End Of The River Road

north.description: To the north lies The Teamster's Cottage.

east.description: To the east lies The House Of The Dairy Farmer.

south.description: To the south lies The Mill And Attached Home.

west.description: To the west lies On The River Road.

8251.description:
The River Road ends here in a small yard of beaten earth where three
homes stand close together. North is a teamster's cottage with a wagon
shed beside it, and east a dairy farmer's house with a cool stone dairy
built against its wall. South stands the mill, its great wheel turning
in the race beside the river. West, the road runs back along the
riverbank toward the village.

8252.name: The Teamster's Cottage

south.description: To the south lies The Eastern End Of The River Road.

8252.description:
The teamster's cottage is plain and cluttered, its single room smelling
of axle grease, horses and stale beer. Empty harness pegs line the wall
by the door, and a narrow cot is pushed against the opposite wall. Above
it someone has drawn a map of the roads in charcoal on the plaster, with
distances scrawled along each line. Its one door lets out south onto the
yard.

extra_descs.map charcoal roads plaster:
The map shows Hommlet in the middle, with lines running off toward
Garathorm, the mountains and the Black Woods. Beside the Black Woods the
teamster has drawn a heavy cross and written NOT FOR ANY PRICE.

8253.name: The House Of The Dairy Farmer

west.description: To the west lies The Eastern End Of The River Road.

8253.description:
The dairy farmer's house is cool and spotless, its stone floor scrubbed
pale and its walls lined with slatted wooden racks for ripening cheeses.
A great stone sink sits beneath the window, beside a scoured wooden
butter churn as tall as a child. The whole house smells of milk, butter
and cut grass. The door west opens back onto the yard at the end of the
River Road.

8254.name: The Mill And Attached Home

north.description: To the north lies The Eastern End Of The River Road.

8254.description:
The mill and the miller's home share one roof here, and the whole
building trembles gently with the turning of the great wheel outside.
Through an open archway the millstones grind in their wooden casing,
filling the air with a fine white dust that settles on everything. The
living quarters are warm and floury, with a table, a dresser and a
cradle by the fire. A door north lets out onto the yard where the River
Road ends.

8255.name: The Traders' Room

east.description: To the east lies The Trading Post.

8255.description:
This snug chamber is where traders strike their bargains in private,
around a heavy round table scarred by the edges of countless coins.
Cushioned benches line the walls, and a small barred window lets in a
little grey light. A slate fixed to the wall is chalked with the latest
prices for wool, salt, iron and barley. The door east opens back into
the trading post.

8256.name: The Stable

south.description: To the south lies The Trading Post.

8256.description:
The stable behind the trading post is long and low, with a row of roomy
stalls along one wall and hay racks fixed above the mangers. The cobbled
floor slopes toward a drain, and the air is thick with the warm smells
of horse, hay and leather. Wooden pegs for saddles and harness line the
opposite wall. The only door leads south into the trading post.

8257.name: The Smithy

south.description: To the south lies On The Old Temple Road.

8257.description:
The smithy is hot and dim, lit by the red glow of a forge whose great
leather bellows hang from a beam beside it. An anvil worn bright on its
face stands on a stump of oak, and racks of tongs and hammers line the
sooty walls. Horseshoes are nailed above the door for luck, their points
turned upward. The doorway south leads back out to the covered walk of
the Old Temple Road.

8258.name: On The Old Temple Road

north.description: To the north lies The Village Elder's Compound.

east.description: To the east lies On The Old Temple Road.

south.description: To the south lies The Wheel-Wright's Shop.

west.description: To the west lies On The Old Temple Road.

8258.description:
The covered walk of the Old Temple Road is wider here, and benches have
been built between its posts where travellers can rest out of the
weather. North, a gate in a high wall of whitewashed stone leads into
the village elder's compound, and south a wheelwright's shop has a
cartwheel painted on its door. Light falls in bars between the posts
across the worn boards. The walk runs on east and back west toward the
smithy and the square.

8259.name: The End Of The Path

north.description: To the north lies On The Old Temple Road.

south.description: To the south lies The Druid's Cottage.

8259.description:
The footpath from the village ends here in a quiet clearing ringed by
oaks and hollies. A round cottage with a mossy turf roof stands on the
southern side, a thread of smoke rising from a hole at its peak and
bunches of drying herbs hanging beneath its eaves. Mistletoe grows in
pale clumps high in the oaks. North, the path leads back through the
trees to the covered walk of Hommlet's Old Temple Road.

8260.name: The Druid's Cottage

north.description: To the north lies The End Of The Path.

8260.description:
The single round room of the cottage is warm and dim, lit by a fire of
applewood in a ring of stones at its centre. Herbs, roots and dried
flowers hang in hundreds of bunches from the rafters, filling the air
with a dusty green scent, and shelves of clay jars line the curving
wall. A sleeping pallet heaped with fleeces lies against one side, and a
sprig of mistletoe is fixed above the door. The doorway north leads back
out to the clearing.

extra_descs.jars shelves clay:
Each jar is marked with a scratched symbol rather than a word: a leaf, a
moon, an eye, a drop of water. One, set apart on a high shelf, is marked
with a skull and sealed with black wax.

8261.name: The Village Elder's Compound

south.description: To the south lies On The Old Temple Road.

8261.description:
The village elder's compound is entered through a long, dim hall hung
with the faded banners of Hommlet's oldest families. A carved chair of
black oak stands at the head of the hall beside a brass-bound chest
where the village records are kept. Rushes cover the floor, and a fire
of apple wood crackles in a deep hearth. The door south leads back out
to the covered walk.

8262.name: On The Old Temple Road

north.description: To the north lies The House Of The Stonemason.

east.description: To the east lies On The Old Temple Road.

south.description: To the south lies The House Of The Carpenter.

west.description: To the west lies On The Old Temple Road.

8262.description:
Here the covered walk passes between the homes of two builders, each a
boast of its owner's craft. North stands a house of beautifully dressed
stone with carved lintels, the stonemason's, and south a timber-framed
house with an overhanging upper storey, the carpenter's. The posts of
the walk here are carved with leaves and faces, the fruit of a long and
friendly rivalry. The walk continues east and back west.

extra_descs.posts carvings faces:
Each post is carved with a different face: a laughing man, a scowling
woman, a sleepy ox. One is plainly a caricature of the carpenter, and
the next, in return, of the stonemason.

8263.name: The Wheel-Wright's Shop

north.description: To the north lies On The Old Temple Road.

8263.description:
Wheels in every stage of making fill this lofty shop: bare elm hubs
stacked against the wall, felloes of ash clamped to a bending jig, and a
finished cartwheel standing in the wheel pit to await its iron tyre. A
great round tyring plate of stone lies near the back, blackened by the
fires used to heat the iron. The floor is ankle-deep in curled shavings
that crackle underfoot. The doorway north opens back onto the covered
walk of the Old Temple Road.

8265.name: The House Of The Stonemason

south.description: To the south lies On The Old Temple Road.

8265.description:
The stonemason's house is cool and solid, its walls of close-fitted
ashlar and its floor laid in a chequer of red and grey flags. The mantel
over the hearth is a single slab carved with a twisting vine, and every
window has a carved stone sill. A heavy stone bench by the window is
pitted with chisel marks and dusted white. The door south opens onto the
covered walk.

8266.name: On The Old Temple Road

east.description: To the east lies On The Old Temple Road.

west.description: To the west lies On The Old Temple Road.

8266.description:
Beyond the builders' houses the covered walk grows older and plainer,
its posts grey with age and its roof patched with newer boards. Gaps
between the posts look out over garden plots and a reedy duck pond.
Pilgrims of long ago pressed coins into the cracks of the posts for
luck, and their green edges still show. The walk continues east toward a
crossing and back west past the builders' houses.

8267.name: The House Of The Carpenter

north.description: To the north lies On The Old Temple Road.

8267.description:
The carpenter's house is as much workshop as home, and its ground floor
smells richly of oak shavings, glue and linseed oil. A long workbench
scarred by years of chisels runs beneath the window, with saws, planes
and augers hung in neat rows on pegs above it. Every stick of furniture
is the carpenter's own work, from the carved settle by the hearth to the
spindle-backed chairs. A grinning wooden face on the mantel looks
suspiciously like the stonemason across the way. The door north leads
out to the covered walk.

extra_descs.face carving mantel:
It is the stonemason to the life, from his heavy jaw to the chip of
granite caught in his beard, carved with a great deal of affection and
not a little malice.

8268.name: On The King's Road

east.description: To the east lies On The King's Road.

west.description: To the west lies On The King's Road.

8268.description:
The King's Road runs beneath a long market roof here, a gallery of oak
posts and rafters blackened by lamp smoke. Empty stalls with folding
wooden shutters line both walls, each painted with a faded trade sign: a
loaf, a boot, a fish, a key. Lanterns on iron hooks shed a yellow light
over flagstones worn into shallow grooves by cartwheels. The covered way
continues east, and its open mouth lets in the daylight from the west.

8269.name: On The King's Road

east.description: To the east lies On The King's Road.

west.description: To the west lies On The King's Road.

8269.description:
The timber gallery gives way to a vaulted passage of dressed stone,
where the road runs beneath the old toll house of the castle town. A
barred window in one wall looks into the empty toll room, and the ledge
below it is worn smooth by generations of coins. Water drips from the
vault into a channel cut along the floor, and the air is cool and smells
of wet stone. The passage runs on east and back west into the market.

8270.name: On The King's Road

east.description: To the east lies An Intersection In The King's Road.

west.description: To the west lies On The King's Road.

8270.description:
This is the deep arch of an old gate through the castle town's outer
wall, so long that lamps burn in niches along its sides. Grooves for a
portcullis score the stonework overhead, though the portcullis itself is
long gone, and the walls are carved with the initials of bored guards.
Daylight and the smell of grass come in through the arch to the east,
where the road meets a crossing in open country. West, the passage leads
back beneath the toll house.

8271.name: An Intersection In The King's Road

north.description: To the north lies An Old Road.

east.description: To the east lies The Edge of the Forest.

south.description: To the south lies Rolling Foothills.

west.description: To the west lies On The King's Road.

8271.description:
Four ways meet here in open, grassy country beneath a wide sky. The
King's Road runs on east toward the edge of a forest whose leaves shine
a pale, lingering gold, and back west through the arch of the castle
town's wall. An old road, grass-grown between its stones, heads north
toward a squat roofed building. South, a track toward the rolling
foothills is closed by a rusted iron gate chained between two stone
posts, and brambles choke the way beyond.

8272.name: An Old Road

north.description: To the north lies An Old Road.

south.description: To the south lies An Intersection In The King's Road.

8272.description:
The old road passes straight through a roofed hall of rough stone, an
ancient waystation built over the way so that drovers could shelter
their beasts from the weather. Its roof of stone slabs still holds,
though daylight leaks between them in thin bright lines. Iron rings for
tethering are set into both walls, and a stone manger runs the length of
one side. The road leaves the hall north through a sagging doorway and
south toward the crossroads.

8273.name: An Old Road

east.description: To the east lies An Old Road.

south.description: To the south lies An Old Road.

8273.description:
Out in the open again, the old road bends around a lone standing stone
taller than a man, its face patterned with lichen in rings of grey and
orange. Thistles and tall grass have crept across the paving, and only
the line of the kerbstones shows where the road once ran. It turns east
toward a stream and a roofed bridge, and runs back south into the
shelter of the old waystation.

extra_descs.standing stone lichen spirals:
The stone is older than the road, and the road builders bent their way
around it rather than move it. Faint spirals are cut into its face
beneath the lichen, worn almost smooth by rain.

8274.name: An Old Road

east.description: To the east lies An Old Road.

west.description: To the west lies An Old Road.

8274.description:
The old road crosses a stream here inside a covered bridge, a long box
of weathered planks under a shingled roof. Light falls in stripes
through the gaps between the boards, and water chuckles somewhere
beneath the floor. Carters have carved their marks and the names of
sweethearts into the beams along the walls. The bridge opens east onto
the road beyond and west toward the standing stone.

8275.name: An Old Road

east.description: To the east lies A Slight Bend In The Old Road.

west.description: To the west lies An Old Road.

8275.description:
The old road runs straight and level across rough pasture, its stones
heaved and tilted by the roots of an elder bush growing in the verge. A
milestone leans beside the way, its numbers long since weathered away.
East, the road goes on toward a bend and the first farm fences of a
village, and to the west the roofed bridge squats over its stream. The
wind hisses through dry seed-heads on either side.

8276.name: On The Old Temple Road

east.description: To the east lies An Intersection In The Old Temple Road.

west.description: To the west lies On The Old Temple Road.

8276.description:
The covered walk runs between high hawthorn hedges here at the edge of
the village, and its boards give way to packed earth trodden hard. A
wooden collecting box for the upkeep of the walk is fixed to one post,
its slot worn smooth. Light filters dimly through the hedges, heavy with
the scent of may blossom. The walk leads on east to a crossing and back
west into the village.

8277.name: An Intersection In The Old Temple Road

north.description: To the north lies On A Road Crossing The Plains.

south.description: To the south lies The Overgrown Path.

west.description: To the west lies On The Old Temple Road.

8277.description:
The covered walk ends in a square, roofed pavilion where three ways
meet, its timber pillars painted long ago in red and gold now faded to
rust and straw. A worn stone set in the middle of the floor marks where
the old temple road once began. North, a doorway leads into a long
shelter built over a road across the plains, and south an archway opens
onto an overgrown path winding into the woods. West, the walk leads back
toward Hommlet.

8278.name: On A Road Crossing The Plains

south.description: To the south lies An Intersection In The Old Temple Road.

8278.description:
This long shelter of weathered timber was built over the road where it
sets out across the plains, a place for travellers to wait out the rain.
Its far doors are nailed shut and blocked by a heap of fallen roof
beams, so the road beyond can only be glimpsed through gaps in the
planking: grass, rolling away for miles. A row of rotting benches lines
one wall. Your way lies back south, to the pavilion.

8300.name: On The Caravan Road

north.description: To the north lies On The Caravan Road.

south.description: To the south lies On The Caravan Road.

8300.description:
Apple orchards line both sides of the Caravan Road here, their gnarled
old trees propped with forked poles where the branches sag. A low press-
shed with a mossy roof stands among the trees, and the air smells
faintly of cider. The road is paved with flat stones set in neat
courses, the work of careful hands. It runs north between the orchards
and south back toward the village.

8301.name: On The Caravan Road

north.description: To the north lies On The Caravan Road.

south.description: To the south lies On The Caravan Road.

8301.description:
Hay meadows spread away from the road on either hand, dotted with tall
ricks thatched against the rain. A stone culvert carries a ditch beneath
the road, and the water gurgles through it into a reed-lined channel.
Poppies and cornflowers grow thick along the ditch bank. The Caravan
Road runs straight on north, and south it passes into the shade of the
orchards.

8302.name: On The Caravan Road

north.description: To the north lies The Road Crossing.

south.description: To the south lies On The Caravan Road.

8302.description:
A spring rises beside the road here and has been piped into a long stone
basin, where travellers and their beasts can drink. Someone has carved a
cup and a horseshoe into the stone above the spout. The fields grow
rougher from here on, with gorse creeping in from the verges, and a
crossroads with a tall signpost lies just to the north. South, the road
runs back among the hay meadows of Hommlet.

8303.name: The Road Crossing

north.description: To the north lies On The Caravan Road.

east.description: To the east lies Along The Road To Nowhere.

south.description: To the south lies On The Caravan Road.

west.description: To the west lies On A Dirt Road.

8303.description:
A tall signpost stands where four roads cross, its arms pointing every
which way and its post studded with the nails of old notices. The
Caravan Road runs on north toward the dark line of distant woods, and
south back to Hommlet. West, a dirt road wanders off toward the faint
blue shapes of mountains. To the east a short paved road ends abruptly
at a carved archway set into the side of a grassy hill.

extra_descs.signpost arms post:
Three of the arms read HOMMLET, MOUNTAINS and BLACK WOODS in fading
paint. The fourth, pointing at the hill, has been painted over so often
that it is blank, and someone has chalked NOWHERE across it.

8488.name: On The Caravan Road

north.description: To the north lies On The Caravan Road.

south.description: To the south lies The Road Crossing.

8488.description:
Just beyond the crossroads a drovers' pond lies beside the road, a broad
muddy pool with a cobbled ramp where herds are watered. The ground all
around is churned by countless hooves and dried into hard ridges. The
Caravan Road climbs gently north into emptier country, and the signpost
at the crossing can be seen a short way back to the south.

8489.name: On The Caravan Road

north.description: To the north lies On The Caravan Road.

south.description: To the south lies On The Caravan Road.

8489.description:
A long dry-stone wall keeps company with the road here, snaking over the
rolling downs as far as the eye can follow. The turf beyond it is
cropped short by sheep, and a shepherd's hut with a roof of sods stands
empty in a fold of the land. Tufts of wool cling to the wall's rough
stones. The road runs on north and back south toward the drovers' pond.

8490.name: On The Caravan Road

north.description: To the north lies On The Caravan Road.

south.description: To the south lies On The Caravan Road.

8490.description:
A stout milestone of red sandstone stands at the roadside, carved on
both faces with distances and the sign of a wagon wheel. The Caravan
Road is paved with heavy flags here, cambered so that rain runs off into
deep ditches on either side. Open grassland stretches away under a huge
sky, broken only by a few wind-bent thorn trees. The road carries on
north and runs back south toward Hommlet.

extra_descs.milestone sandstone wheel:
One face reads HOMMLET IV and the other BLACK WOODS IX. Beneath the
carved wagon wheel some traveller has scratched a short warning: KEEP
TOGETHER.

8491.name: On The Caravan Road

north.description: To the north lies On The Caravan Road.

south.description: To the south lies On The Caravan Road.

8491.description:
The road crosses a stretch of boggy ground on a raised causeway of
packed stone, with black water lying among the reeds on either side.
Cotton grass nods in the wind, and the air smells of peat and rot.
Wooden posts painted white at their tops mark the edges of the causeway
for travellers caught out in fog. The way continues north and back south
onto firmer ground.

8492.name: On The Caravan Road

north.description: To the north lies On The Caravan Road.

south.description: To the south lies On The Caravan Road.

8492.description:
On a low rise beside the road stands an old gibbet of weathered timber,
its iron cage empty and creaking in the wind. It was raised long ago as
a warning to robbers, and the grass beneath it grows rank and dark. The
Caravan Road hurries past, running north over the rise and south toward
the causeway and the bog.

8493.name: On The Caravan Road

north.description: To the north lies On The Caravan Road.

south.description: To the south lies On The Caravan Road.

8493.description:
The blackened ruin of a roadside inn stands here, nothing left of it but
a tall stone chimney and a ring of charred beams sunk in nettles. A
painted sign still hangs from a bracket on the chimney, too scorched to
read. Whatever happened here, no one has come back to rebuild. The road
runs north past the ruin and back south toward the gibbet on its rise.

8494.name: On The Caravan Road

north.description: To the north lies On The Caravan Road.

south.description: To the south lies On The Caravan Road.

8494.description:
A trader's wagon lies wrecked in the ditch here, tipped on its side with
two wheels smashed and its canvas cover rotted to rags. Brambles have
grown up through its floorboards, and it was stripped of anything worth
taking long ago. The paving of the road is cracked and patched in
places, and weeds push up between the stones. The Caravan Road goes on
north and back south past the burned inn.

8495.name: On The Caravan Road

north.description: To the north lies On The Caravan Road.

south.description: To the south lies On The Caravan Road.

8495.description:
A long, grass-covered barrow lies beside the road, a mound as long as a
barn with a dark stone doorway at one end sealed by a great slab. The
road builders gave it a wide berth, and travellers still hurry past it.
Heather grows thick on the slopes of the barrow, and the wind seems
colder here. The way leads north and south along the old caravan route.

extra_descs.barrow mound slab doorway:
The slab across the doorway is carved with a worn figure of a sleeping
warrior, his arms folded over a sword. Small stones have been piled at
its foot, as if to keep whatever lies within asleep.

8496.name: On The Caravan Road

north.description: To the north lies On The Caravan Road.

south.description: To the south lies On The Caravan Road.

8496.description:
The road crests a low ridge here, and from the top the land can be seen
falling away toward an unbroken mass of dark forest far ahead: the Black
Woods. Gorse blazes yellow along the verges, and the wind hums through
the heather. Behind, the country rolls back toward the distant smoke of
Hommlet. The road continues north off the ridge and south toward the
barrow.

8497.name: On The Caravan Road

north.description: To the north lies On The Caravan Road.

south.description: To the south lies On The Caravan Road.

8497.description:
A ruined watchtower stands beside the road, a stump of round stone wall
with an iron beacon basket rusting on top of it. Once a fire lit here
would have warned Hommlet of trouble on the road. The paving is
overgrown with moss now, and tall bracken presses in from the verges.
North, the road nears the edge of the forest, and south it climbs back
toward the ridge.

8498.name: On The Caravan Road

south.description: To the south lies On The Caravan Road.

west.description: To the west lies On The Caravan Road.

8498.description:
The Caravan Road turns west here to skirt the forest, and a tall cairn
of piled stones marks the turning. Travellers add a stone for luck as
they pass, and the heap now stands taller than a rider on horseback.
Dark trees stand close beyond a strip of rough grass, and the smell of
leaf mould drifts from them. South, the road runs back across the open
downs.

8499.name: On The Caravan Road

east.description: To the east lies On The Caravan Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Outskirts Of The Woods.

8499.description:
The paving gives out here, and the Caravan Road becomes a rutted track
running west into the outskirts of the woods. Birch and young oak crowd
the verges, and the light is already dimmer beneath their spreading
branches. A broken cart axle has been driven into the ground as a post,
with a strip of red cloth knotted round it as a marker. East, the road
runs back to the cairn at the turning.

8501.name: End Of The Plains Road

north.description: To the north lies Foot Of The Mountains.

east.description: To the east lies The Meadow Thrithing.

south.description: To the south lies The Meadow Thrithing.

west.description: To the west lies Road Through The Plains.

8501.description:
The plains road comes to an end here at the foot of rising hills, its
last few yards marked by a squat milestone so worn it might be any old
stone. North the ground climbs steeply toward the mountains, while east
and south the long grass of the Meadow Thrithing spreads away, rippling
silver in the wind. West the road runs back toward the burnt village of
Townsbridge. Heather and gorse grow in clumps along the stony bank.

extra_descs.milestone stone:
Scraping away the lichen reveals the word GARATHORM and a number too
worn to read. On the other face, cut much more recently, is a leaf
inside a circle, the mark the rangers of the Long Lake use to show the
way to their camp.

8502.name: Foot Of The Mountains

north.description: To the north lies At The Plateau Before The Mountains.

east.description: To the east lies The Meadow Thrithing.

south.description: To the south lies End Of The Plains Road.

west.description: To the west lies A Small Path Along The Mountains.

8502.description:
The land begins to climb in earnest here, rough grass giving way to
scree and outcrops of grey rock at the foot of the mountains. An old
drystone wall runs along the slope, and set into it is a stout plank
door, weathered silver, that opens west onto a small path along the
mountains. North a steep track climbs toward a high plateau, east the
meadow grass rolls away, and south lies the end of the plains road. The
wind here has a cold edge to it.

8503.name: A Small Path Along The Mountains

east.description: To the east lies Foot Of The Mountains.

west.description: To the west lies At The Old Mine.

8503.description:
A small path picks its way along the foot of the mountains here,
squeezed between a slope of loose scree and a tumble of boulders furred
with lichen. The peaks rise steep and grey above, their summits often
lost in cloud, and a cold wind spills down from them. East, a weathered
plank gate in a dry-stone wall leads back to the Foot Of The Mountains,
and west the path ends at the timbered mouth of an old mine.

8504.name: At The Old Mine

north.description: To the north lies Into The Mine.

east.description: To the east lies A Small Path Along The Mountains.

8504.description:
A long shed of rough timber has been built against the mountainside over
the mouth of the old mine, and inside it is dim, cold and dusty. A
rusted winch stands bolted to the floor beside a row of ore carts whose
wheels have seized solid, and broken picks hang forgotten on pegs. In
the rock face to the north a heavy door of iron-bound planks closes the
way into the mine. The shed's open end lets out east onto the mountain
path.

8505.name: At The Plateau Before The Mountains

south.description: To the south lies Foot Of The Mountains.

up.description: To the up lies On The Cliffside.

8505.description:
A windswept plateau of bare rock and thin, wiry grass spreads out here
before the mountains, which rise in a sheer grey cliff close at hand.
Cracks in the cliff face have been worn into a rough ladder of handholds
and ledges that climbs up toward the cliffside high above. A cairn of
piled stones marks the start of the climb. Far below, the meadow and the
dark line of the woods lie spread out like a map, and the track leads
back south down the slope.

extra_descs.cairn stones:
Every stone in the cairn was carried up by a climber, and many bear
scratched initials or tiny charms tied on with string. It is said to
bring luck to add a stone before the climb.

8573.name: Into The Mine

north.description: To the north lies Into the Mine.

south.description: To the south lies At The Old Mine.

8573.description:
Beyond the door the mine runs straight into the mountain, a tunnel
shored with timbers black with age and so low that a tall man must
stoop. The air is cold and smells of wet stone, with something sour and
rotten beneath it. A short way north the tunnel is closed by a grille of
thick iron bars, chained and padlocked, with only darkness beyond.
Behind you to the south, the door leads back out to the mine shed.

extra_descs.grille bars chain padlock slate:
The bars are old, but the chain is new and heavy, and its padlock is the
size of a fist. A slate hangs from the grille with KEEP OUT scratched
into it, and beneath, in smaller and shakier letters, someone has added
THE DEAD ARE DIGGING.

8600.name: The Small Path

east.description: To the east lies The Animal Path.

8600.description:
The small path ends in a sunny dell where someone once kept a garden,
fenced with woven hazel hurdles that have half collapsed. Rosemary, sage
and thyme have run wild and spread far beyond the hurdles, and the warm
air is heavy with their scent. A flat stone serves as a seat beside a
tiny spring. The only way out is east, back to the animal path.

8601.name: The Edge of the Forest

east.description: To the east lies The King's Road.

west.description: To the west lies An Intersection In The King's Road.

8601.description:
Here the King's Road leaves open grassland and passes between two
enormous golden trees that stand on either side of it like gateposts,
their roots heaving the first paving stones of the forest road. Beyond
them the wood glows, every leaf holding the light as if reluctant to let
it go. East, the road runs on beneath the shining canopy, and west it
leads out into open country toward a crossing and the castle town's
wall.

8602.name: The King's Road

east.description: To the east lies The King's Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Edge of the Forest.

8602.description:
A barrier pole painted in bands of red and white stands raised on its
post beside the road here, where the king's foresters can lower it to
stop wagons if they choose. A little sentry box of planks stands beside
it, and a board nailed to its side forbids fires, felling and hunting in
the royal wood without warrant. The golden trees grow thicker going
east, and west the light of open country shows at the forest's edge.

8603.name: The King's Road

east.description: To the east lies The King's Road.

west.description: To the west lies The King's Road.

8603.description:
The trees stand back from the road here around a wide glade of short
grass starred with yellow flowers. Light pools in it like water in a
bowl, and the foresters say that even on moonless nights a soft gold
glow lingers here long after sunset. A single golden oak grows in the
middle of the glade, its lowest boughs sweeping the grass. The King's
Road crosses the glade east to west.

8604.name: The King's Road

east.description: To the east lies The King's Road.

west.description: To the west lies The King's Road.

8604.description:
The stump of an old stone watchtower stands beside the road here, ivy-
clad and roofless, its stair long since fallen so that no one can climb
it. Golden saplings have taken root in its empty windows, and their
leaves shine out of the grey stone like candle flames. Crowns and
initials have been scratched into the stones at its base. The King's
Road runs past its foot, east past a row of little cairns and west
through the trees.

8605.name: The King's Road

east.description: To the east lies The King's Road.

west.description: To the west lies The King's Road.

8605.description:
Dozens of little cairns of pebbles line the verge along this stretch of
the King's Road, each built by some traveller in thanks for a safe
passage through the forest. Golden leaves have drifted against them and
half buried the smallest. The trees here are very old and very tall,
their pale trunks rising straight as columns. The road runs on east and
west through their light.

8606.name: The King's Road

east.description: To the east lies The King's Road.

west.description: To the west lies The King's Road.

8606.description:
A forester's lodge stands back from the road here in a clearing of its
own, a snug house of golden-brown logs with a crown carved over its door
and antlers nailed to its gable. Its shutters are closed and its door is
locked, though a thread of smoke sometimes rises from the chimney. A
rain barrel and a chopping block stand by the porch. The King's Road
runs on east toward a bend and west between the shining trees.

8607.name: The King's Road

north.description: To the north lies The King's road.

south.description: To the south lies In The Old Forest.

west.description: To the west lies The King's Road.

8607.description:
The King's Road turns north here at a sharp bend, banked with pale stone
where the wheels of heavy wagons have swung wide over the years. On the
outer side of the bend the golden trees end at a ditch, and beyond it
the dark ranks of the Old Forest begin, with a gap in the ditch letting
a path slip off south among them. West, the road runs straight back
through the shining wood.

8608.name: The King's road

north.description: To the north lies The King's Road.

east.description: To the east lies On The Trail Of Shadows.

south.description: To the south lies The King's Road.

8608.description:
The King's Road runs north and south here along the edge of a darker
wood, and the golden trees grow thin and pale on its eastern side. East,
a narrow way slips off between black trunks into the gloom of the Trail
of Shadows, and even at midday the air that breathes out of it is cold.
An iron bracket on a post holds a lantern cage, empty and rusted, as if
someone once thought a light here worth the trouble.

8609.name: The King's Road

north.description: To the north lies The Animal Path.

east.description: To the east lies The King's Road.

south.description: To the south lies The King's road.

8609.description:
The King's Road turns here at a bend shaded by a vast golden lime, its
heart-shaped leaves glowing like lamps. Set into a niche in the roadside
bank is a little shrine of carved stone, a stag with a sun between its
antlers, hung about with faded ribbons. The air beneath the lime is
sweet and drowsy. The road runs on east and south, and a deer track
slips away north into the bracken.

extra_descs.shrine stag niche carving:
The little stag is carved from pale stone with great care, every tine of
its antlers sharp, and the sun between them is inlaid with a disc of
yellow glass. Foresters say the white stag of the Radiant Forest shows
itself only to those who leave the woods as they found them.

8610.name: The King's Road

east.description: To the east lies The King's Road.

west.description: To the west lies The King's Road.

8610.description:
The paving dips through a shallow hollow here, where a spring wells up
beside the road and is led away beneath it through a stone culvert. Moss
grows thick and bright around the spring, studded with tiny white
flowers, and the golden trees above lean together into an arch. The
water is clear and very cold. The King's Road runs on east and climbs
gently west toward a bend.

8611.name: The King's Road

east.description: To the east lies The King's Road.

west.description: To the west lies The King's Road.

8611.description:
A milestone capped with a carved crown stands at the roadside here, its
face giving the leagues back to Garathorm in letters picked out in faded
red. On one side of the road the golden trees stand tall and bright, but
on the other their gold gives way within a stone's throw to the dark,
crowding trees of an older wood. The road runs on east toward a crossing
and west into a hollow.

8612.name: The King's Road

north.description: To the north lies The Trail.

east.description: To the east lies The King's Road.

south.description: To the south lies On The Trail Of Shadows.

west.description: To the west lies The King's Road.

8612.description:
A trail crosses the King's Road here, and the two halves of it could
hardly be less alike. North it wanders off cheerfully into a wood of oak
and gold, while south it plunges into a wall of dark, close-grown trees
where the light dies within a few paces: the Trail of Shadows. A post at
its mouth bears a board painted with the foresters' crown and a single
word, WARE. The road runs on east toward a bridge and west beneath the
golden boughs.

8613.name: The King's Road

east.description: To the east lies A Bridge On The King's Road.

west.description: To the west lies The King's Road.

down.description: To the down lies A Small Rocky Path.

8613.description:
Just short of the bridge, the bank beside the King's Road falls away
steeply toward the stream, and a small rocky path leads down from the
roadside, zigzagging between boulders and hazel toward a wooded hollow
below. Ferns spill over the edge of the paving. The trees in the hollow
are a plain, sober green, untouched by the gold that lines the road. The
road runs east onto the bridge and west deeper into the golden wood.

8614.name: A Bridge On The King's Road

east.description: To the east lies The King's Road.

west.description: To the west lies The King's Road.

8614.description:
The King's Road crosses a deep, rocky stream here on a bridge of a
single high arch, built of the same pale stone as the road and wide
enough for two wagons to pass. Golden trees lean out over the water from
both banks, and their fallen leaves ride the current below like flecks
of gilt. A crowned shield is carved on the keystone of each parapet. The
road runs on east and west among the trees.

extra_descs.shield crowned carving keystone parapet:
The shield bears a crown above a single open eye, the old sign of the
king's foresters. Beneath it are cut the words THE ROAD IS THE KING'S
PEACE, and travellers have rubbed the crown bright for luck.

8615.name: The King's Road

north.description: To the north lies The Path.

east.description: To the east lies The King's Road.

south.description: To the south lies On The Muddy Path.

west.description: To the west lies A Bridge On The King's Road.

8615.description:
A muddy track leaves the King's Road here, sliding off south between the
golden trunks toward rough hill country, its ruts brimming with brown
water. Beside it a weathered post bears a board with a single word,
MARSHES, and a painted hand pointing the way with what looks like
reluctance. North, a footpath enters the trees. The road itself runs
west onto a stone bridge and on east beneath the shining leaves.

8616.name: The King's Road

east.description: To the east lies The King's Road.

west.description: To the west lies The King's Road.

8616.description:
The King's Road runs straight and level here, its pale stones swept
clean and its verges trimmed back by the foresters' billhooks. A stone
bench carved with a crown stands at the roadside for weary travellers,
its seat dusted with fallen gold leaves. The leaves drift slowly even on
windless days, turning over and over like spun coins. The road continues
east toward a crossing and west toward a bridge.

8617.name: The King's Road

north.description: To the north lies The King's Road.

east.description: To the east lies The King's Road.

south.description: To the south lies The Path of Light.

west.description: To the west lies The King's Road.

8617.description:
Beneath the golden trees the King's Road is crossed here by two lesser
ways. South, the Path of Light slips off between a pair of ancient
trunks whose leaves glow brighter than any around them, and a narrower
arm of the road strikes off north. The broad paving itself runs on east
toward the forest's edge and west deeper into the wood. A stone basin at
the roadside holds rainwater that has caught the gold of the leaves
above.

8618.name: The King's Road

north.description: To the north lies The King's Road.

south.description: To the south lies The King's Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Path.

8618.description:
This arm of the King's Road is older and narrower than the main way, its
paving stones small, rounded and furred with moss along the joints. The
golden trees still line it, but oaks have crept in among them, and their
darker leaves make a patchwork of the light. A footpath leaves the road
westward through a gap in the bracken. The road runs on north and back
south to the crossing.

8619.name: The King's Road

south.description: To the south lies The King's Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Lost Path.

8619.description:
The paving of the King's Road simply stops here, as though its builders
laid one last stone and walked away. Beyond it a heap of dressed blocks,
never set, has sunk into the moss beneath a great golden beech. A faint
track, hardly more than a parting of the ferns, wanders off west among
the trees and is soon lost to sight. The only clear way is back south
along the road.

8620.name: The King's Road

east.description: To the east lies The Edge of the Forest.

west.description: To the west lies The King's Road.

8620.description:
The King's Road runs through the Radiant Forest here on wide, pale
paving stones, kept clear of roots by the king's foresters. The trees on
either side are tall and slender, their leaves a pale gold that seems to
drink the light and give it back, so that even the shadows are soft and
warm. East, the trees thin toward the edge of the forest, and west the
road runs on deeper among the shining trunks.

8621.name: The Edge of the Forest

east.description: To the east lies The Dusty Road.

west.description: To the west lies The King's Road.

8621.description:
Here the Radiant Forest comes to an end, its last golden trees standing
like sentinels at the edge of open, sun-baked farmland. A weathered
boundary stone carved with a crown marks the limit of the royal
woodland. Beyond it the paving of the King's Road gives way to a pale
dirt road that runs off east, raising little puffs of dust in the
breeze. West, the road leads back beneath the shining leaves.

8622.name: The Animal Path

north.description: To the north lies The Animal Path.

south.description: To the south lies The King's Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Small Path.

8622.description:
The animal path drops into a ditch at the edge of the King's Road and
climbs out again over a fallen log, worn smooth on top by the passage of
many hooves and paws. Golden leaves from the roadside trees drift into
the bracken here. A small path, neater than the game trail, leads off
west, and the animal path wanders north into the wood. South lies the
road.

8623.name: The Animal Path

north.description: To the north lies The Overgrown Path.

east.description: To the east lies The Animal Path.

south.description: To the south lies The Animal Path.

8623.description:
The animal path skirts a grey beech whose trunk has been shredded in
long, parallel furrows, the torn bark hanging in strips and the pale
wood beneath still weeping sap. The ground at its foot is torn open and
strewn with rotten wood where something dug for grubs. A musky, animal
smell hangs in the air. North, the path meets an old overgrown road;
east and south it wanders on through the undergrowth.

8624.name: The Overgrown Path

north.description: To the north lies An Intersection In The Old Temple Road.

east.description: To the east lies The Animal Path.

south.description: To the south lies The Animal Path.

8624.description:
South of the pavilion the old temple road becomes an overgrown path, its
paving stones heaved apart by roots and buried under moss. Bracken and
young ash crowd in from both sides, and the canopy closes overhead.
Animal trails branch off east and south, narrow ways pressed through the
undergrowth by deer and boar. North, the painted archway of the pavilion
shows through the leaves.

8625.name: The Animal Path

north.description: To the north lies The Narrow Path.

east.description: To the east lies The Animal Path.

south.description: To the south lies The Animal Path.

west.description: To the west lies The Overgrown Path.

8625.description:
Several game trails meet here in a little clearing trampled flat, where
the earth is pocked with hoofprints and the bark of a young beech has
been rubbed raw by antlers. A narrow path climbs north between hazel
thickets, game trails wander off east and south through the bracken, and
the old overgrown path lies to the west. The light is green and dappled,
and the wood smells of crushed fern.

8626.name: The Animal Path

north.description: To the north lies The Animal Path.

south.description: To the south lies The Trail.

west.description: To the west lies The Animal Path.

8626.description:
This is a deer track rather than a path, a narrow groove through head-
high bracken that closes behind you as you pass. Slots of cloven hooves
are pressed into every soft patch, and tufts of reddish hair cling to a
low branch where something rubbed past. The fronds leave your clothes
dusted with brown spores. The track runs north toward a trampled
clearing, west through the bracken, and south to a wider trail.

8627.name: The Trail

north.description: To the north lies The Animal Path.

east.description: To the east lies The Trail.

south.description: To the south lies The King's Road.

8627.description:
The trail passes through an old charcoal burners' clearing, where a wide
ring of earth is still black and nothing grows but a few thin grasses. A
turf hut has slumped into a low green mound at its edge. The smell of
old smoke lingers in the soil after rain. North, an animal path slips
away into the bracken, east the trail runs on among the oaks, and south
it leads to the King's Road.

8628.name: The Trail

north.description: To the north lies The Trail.

south.description: To the south lies The King's Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Trail.

8628.description:
The trail leaves the King's Road behind and winds north between oaks and
golden ash trees, its earth packed hard by the boots of foresters. A
neat stack of cut logs stands beside it, roofed with bark and waiting to
be carted away, and sawdust still lies pale on the ground around it. A
side trail branches west through the bracken, and south the paving of
the road shows bright between the trunks.

8629.name: The Trail

north.description: To the north lies The Animal Path.

east.description: To the east lies The Ravine Path.

south.description: To the south lies The Trail.

down.description: To the down lies A Badger Borrow.

8629.description:
Beneath a great old oak at this fork, the earth has been dug into a
sprawling badger sett, its spoil heaps of yellow sand scattered with old
bedding and scraps of bone. One entrance is wide enough for a person to
crawl down into, a dark mouth between two roots. The trail runs on north
as a narrower animal track, and east a path heads off toward the sound
of rushing water. South, the trail returns toward the King's Road.

8630.name: The Animal Path

north.description: To the north lies The Animal Path.

east.description: To the east lies The Ravine Path.

south.description: To the south lies The Trail.

west.description: To the west lies The Animal Path.

8630.description:
This animal path is a well-worn groove through the undergrowth, so
deeply trodden that the roots on either side stand out like steps. A mud
wallow beside it is churned and pitted, and the rank stink of boar hangs
over it. The trail runs north toward a rocky slope and west toward a
trampled clearing. A path leads east along the rim of a ravine, and a
wider trail heads away south.

8631.name: The Animal Path

south.description: To the south lies The Animal Path.

west.description: To the west lies The Narrow Path.

down.description: To the down lies The Stone Ledge.

8631.description:
The animal trail runs along the top of a steep, rocky slope here, where
the ground falls away sharply through a tangle of roots and boulders. A
goat track zigzags down the slope to a ledge of grey stone, beyond which
the trees of another forest stretch away into the haze. The wind rising
from below smells of pine resin. Westward the trail meets the narrow
path through the hazels, and south it wanders back among the bracken.

8632.name: The Narrow Path

north.description: To the north lies The Narrow Path.

east.description: To the east lies The Animal Path.

south.description: To the south lies The Animal Path.

8632.description:
The narrow path squeezes between two great hazel thickets, so close that
their branches brush both shoulders at once. The ground rises gently,
and the soil is sandy and dry underfoot. Empty nutshells crunch
underfoot where squirrels have feasted. An animal trail breaks off east
through a gap in the thicket, while the narrow path continues north and
returns south to the trampled clearing.

8633.name: The Narrow Path

east.description: To the east lies The Narrow Path.

south.description: To the south lies The Narrow Path.

8633.description:
The narrow path turns east here along the lip of a sandy bank riddled
with old burrows. Silver birches grow along the bank, their papery bark
peeling in curls. Through a gap in the trees a dark mass of enormous
grey trees can be seen somewhere beyond, looming over the rest of the
wood. The path runs on east and back south through the hazels.

8634.name: The Narrow Path

north.description: To the north lies The Narrow Path.

west.description: To the west lies The Narrow Path.

8634.description:
The path runs through a stand of tall beeches here, their smooth grey
trunks rising like pillars to a canopy of copper leaves. The ground
beneath them is bare but for a thick carpet of beech mast that crackles
underfoot. A fallen beech lies rotting nearby, sprouting shelves of
orange fungus. The path bends north toward darker trees and runs back
west along the sandy bank.

8635.name: The Narrow Path

north.description: To the north lies Outside A Large Grove.

south.description: To the south lies The Narrow Path.

west.description: To the west lies The Trail.

8635.description:
The narrow path reaches a fork here, where the beeches give way to
older, darker trees whose branches are hung with grey lichen like old
lace. North, the path leads toward a huge grove whose towering grey
trees rise above the rest of the forest, and an unnatural hush seems to
flow from that way. A trail branches west into a tangle of undergrowth,
and the path runs back south among the beeches.

8636.name: The Trail

east.description: To the east lies The Narrow Path.

8636.description:
The trail peters out in a tangle of blackthorn and dog rose, so dense
that there is no going further. An old hunter's hide of woven branches
is built into the thicket, its peephole looking out over a little glade
where deer come to graze. Sloes hang dark and bitter on the blackthorn.
The only way back is east, to the fork in the narrow path.

8637.name: Outside A Large Grove

north.description: To the north lies The Entrance To The Shadow Grove.

south.description: To the south lies The Narrow Path.

8637.description:
A wall of giant grey trees stands before you, the edge of a grove so
vast and dark that the woods around it seem small. Their trunks are
smooth as stone, and the shadows between them are thick even though the
light out here is ordinary daylight. A faint path leads north between
two of the greatest trunks into the gloom, and a sense of watchful power
hangs in the air. South, the narrow path offers a way back to friendlier
woods.

8638.name: The Ravine Path

north.description: To the north lies The Ravine Path.

8638.description:
The ravine path ends at a jutting shelf of rock, where the stream leaps
out over a lip of stone and falls in a long white plume into a deep
green pool far below. A seat has been cut into the rock at the edge of
the shelf, worn smooth by those who come to watch. Mist rises from the
falls and beads every leaf with water. The only way on is back north
along the rim.

8639.name: The Ravine Path

north.description: To the north lies The Ravine Path.

south.description: To the south lies The Ravine Path.

west.description: To the west lies The Trail.

8639.description:
The path runs along the very rim of the ravine here, so close to the
edge that someone has driven iron pegs into the rock and strung a rope
between them as a rail. Far below, the stream boils white through a
chute of black stone. Hart's-tongue ferns sprout from every crack, and
the air is damp with spray. The rim path runs north toward a bridge and
south along the gorge, and a trail leads west into the trees.

8640.name: The Ravine Path

east.description: To the east lies A Small Bridge.

south.description: To the south lies The Ravine Path.

west.description: To the west lies The Animal Path.

8640.description:
The path follows the rim of a narrow ravine here, where a stream tumbles
over mossy rocks far below the ferny edge. Alders lean out over the
drop, their roots clinging to the crumbling bank. The rush of the water
fills the air with a cool, constant noise. East, a small wooden bridge
crosses the ravine, and the path also runs south along its rim and west
back to the animal trail.

8641.name: A Small Bridge

east.description: To the east lies The Forest Trail.

west.description: To the west lies The Ravine Path.

8641.description:
A small bridge of split logs, railed with knotted rope, spans the ravine
here and sways a little with every step. Far below, the stream foams
white between the rocks, and ferns drip from the walls of the gorge.
Moss has grown thick on the logs, and they are slick with spray. The
bridge leads east to a broad forest trail and west back to the ravine
path.

8642.name: The Forest Trail

east.description: To the east lies The Forest Trail.

south.description: To the south lies The Forest Trail.

8642.description:
The trail crests a low rise crowned by a ring of silver birches, and
from here the trees beyond are noticeably brighter, many of them hung
with leaves of a soft, glowing gold. Sunlight clings to those branches
long after it has left the others. The trail slopes away east toward the
golden trees and runs back south to the fork beyond the bridge.

8643.name: The Forest Trail

north.description: To the north lies The Forest Trail.

east.description: To the east lies The Forest Trail.

south.description: To the south lies The Forest Trail.

west.description: To the west lies A Small Bridge.

8643.description:
Beyond the ravine a broad forest trail winds among oaks and sweet
chestnuts, and here and there a tree with leaves of pale gold glows
among the green. Spiny chestnut husks lie split open along the path.
Trails part three ways here, north over a gentle rise, east toward the
King's Road and south deeper into the wood, while the log bridge lies
back to the west.

8644.name: The Forest Trail

east.description: To the east lies The King's Road.

south.description: To the south lies The Forest Trail.

west.description: To the west lies The Forest Trail.

8644.description:
Golden leaves drift across the trail here, blown from the trees of the
Radiant Forest that crowd ever closer. The light has a warm, honeyed
quality, as though the afternoon had decided to stay. Even the moss on
the stones is tinged with gold. East, the trail meets the broad paved
way of the King's Road, while other paths lead south into the wood and
west toward the log bridge.

8645.name: The Forest Trail

north.description: To the north lies The Forest Trail.

east.description: To the east lies The Forest Trail.

8645.description:
The forest trail follows the foot of a long, mossy bank here, where
beech roots twist out of the earth like the coils of great grey
serpents. A trickle of water seeps from the bank and keeps the path soft
and dark. Primroses grow in the damp along its foot. North, the trail
climbs toward a fork among the chestnuts, and east it runs on to a small
clearing where four paths cross.

8646.name: The Forest Trail

north.description: To the north lies The Forest Trail.

east.description: To the east lies The Lost Path.

south.description: To the south lies The Path.

west.description: To the west lies The Forest Trail.

8646.description:
Four paths cross in a small clearing here, around a squat post of oak
that bears an arrow carved for each of them, though the cuts have
weathered almost smooth. Hornbeams with grey, twisted trunks ring the
clearing, and woodpeckers have riddled a dead limb of one with neat
round holes. The forest trail runs north toward the brighter trees and
west along a mossy bank, a lesser path heads south, and a faint way
wanders off east.

8647.name: The Path

east.description: To the east lies The King's Road.

south.description: To the south lies The King's Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Path.

8647.description:
A forester's shelter stands beside the path here, a lean-to of poles
roofed with bark and sods, with a ring of blackened stones before it
where many fires have burned. The golden trees grow thickly again on
this side of the holly, and their light falls warm across the trodden
earth. The path forks: east to the old arm of the King's Road and south
to the main road, while west it ducks back into the holly.

8648.name: The Path

north.description: To the north lies The Forest Trail.

east.description: To the east lies The Path.

8648.description:
The path bends here through a thicket of holly, its dark, glossy leaves
so dense that the light beneath them is green and dim. Dead leaves
crackle underfoot, and a mossy log lies along the edge of the way,
hollowed by rot. Here and there a scarlet berry glows among the leaves.
North, the path opens onto a clearing where trails cross, and east it
winds on through the holly toward the King's Road.

8649.name: The Lost Path

east.description: To the east lies The King's Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Forest Trail.

8649.description:
It is easy to see how this path earned its name, for it fades in and out
of the ferns and in places vanishes altogether beneath drifts of leaves.
Old blazes cut into the bark of the trees have healed into faint scars,
and someone has tied strips of faded red cloth to the branches to mark
the way. East, the end of the paved road shows between the trunks, and
west the path struggles on toward a broader trail.

8650.name: The Path of Light

north.description: To the north lies The King's Road.

south.description: To the south lies The Path of Light.

8650.description:
The Path of Light begins between two ancient golden trees whose boughs
meet overhead in an arch, and passing beneath them is like stepping into
a warm room. A narrow way of white pebbles runs on south, edged with
moss, and the leaves above glow so brightly that the path seems lit from
within. Even the air tastes faintly of honey. North, the King's Road
lies just beyond the arch.

8651.name: The Path of Light

north.description: To the north lies The Path of Light.

south.description: To the south lies The Path of Light.

8651.description:
The pebbled path runs straight between slender golden trees, their bark
pale as birch and their leaves stirring and whispering of their own
accord. Shafts of light fall across the way at the same low slant
whatever the hour, so that morning and evening look much alike here. A
small stone marker carved with a sun stands at the path's edge. The path
runs on north and south.

8652.name: The Path of Light

north.description: To the north lies The Path of Light.

east.description: To the east lies The Path of Light.

8652.description:
The path turns east beside a still, round pool whose water mirrors the
golden canopy so perfectly that it seems to hold a second forest beneath
its surface. Flat stones have been set around its rim for sitting, and
their tops are worn smooth. Fallen leaves float on the water without
sinking, slowly turning. North, the pebbled path leads back toward the
King's Road.

8653.name: The Path of Light

east.description: To the east lies The Path of Light.

west.description: To the west lies The Path of Light.

8653.description:
Here the golden trees grow close on either side, their trunks wrapped in
a pale, silvery bark that seems to give off a faint light of its own.
The white pebbles of the path are swept clean, though no one is ever
seen sweeping them. Tiny gold flowers, no bigger than a fingernail, grow
in the moss along the edges. The path runs east toward a crossing and
west to the still pool.

8654.name: The Path of Light

north.description: To the north lies The Small Trail.

east.description: To the east lies The Path of Light.

south.description: To the south lies The Path of Light.

west.description: To the west lies The Path of Light.

8654.description:
Four ways meet at the heart of the Path of Light, around a standing
stone of yellow crystal taller than a man. Light gathers inside the
stone and glows there softly, brightening when clouds pass over as if to
make up for the hidden sun. A small trail slips away north between the
trees, the pebbled path runs east and west, and another branch of it
leads south beneath the golden boughs.

extra_descs.stone crystal standing yellow:
The stone is clear yellow quartz, warm as a hand, and deep inside it
hang specks of gold like motes in a sunbeam. Pilgrims have pressed their
palms against it so often that one face is polished to a mirror.

8655.name: The Small Trail

south.description: To the south lies The Path of Light.

8655.description:
The small trail winds away from the crystal stone and ends in a tiny
glade, hardly bigger than a room, walled in by golden saplings. A bower
has been woven from living branches at its far side, the stems bent and
tied until they have grown into a leafy roof over a seat of moss. It is
very quiet here, and the light is soft and green-gold. The only way back
is south.

8656.name: The Path of Light

south.description: To the south lies The Path of Light.

west.description: To the west lies The Path of Light.

8656.description:
The path bends south here around a golden tree so old that its trunk has
split into three, each part as thick as an ordinary oak, the three
leaning apart like dancers. Its fallen leaves lie heaped against the
roots in a glittering drift that crunches softly underfoot. The pebbles
run west toward the crystal stone and south deeper into the radiant
wood.

8657.name: The Path of Light

north.description: To the north lies The Path of Light.

east.description: To the east lies The Path of Light.

south.description: To the south lies The Path of Light.

west.description: To the west lies The Path of Light.

8657.description:
The Path of Light opens here into a round paved space where the ways
meet, and in its centre the stones form a great mosaic of a rising sun
in white and gold. The glow of the paving is strongest at the sun's
heart. Ways lead north and west, both bending toward the same glade,
while east the path runs on between tall trees and south it curves
around a gold-leaved trunk. Leaves that fall on the mosaic never seem to
stay there long.

extra_descs.mosaic sun stones:
Thousands of tiny stones make up the sun, each set by hand. Its rays
point down every path that leaves this place, and one ray, longer than
the rest, points toward a part of the forest where no path runs at all.

8658.name: The Path of Light

north.description: To the north lies The Path of Light.

east.description: To the east lies The Path of Light.

south.description: To the south lies The Path of Light.

west.description: To the west lies The Path of Light.

8658.description:
Another crossing of pale paths opens here within a ring of golden trees
planted at even spaces, like the pillars of a round hall with the sky
for its roof. The ground inside the ring is carpeted with short, fine
grass that never seems to need cutting. Ways lead north and west among
the trees, east toward a brighter glow, and south along the pebbled
path.

8659.name: The Path of Light

west.description: To the west lies The Path of Light.

8659.description:
The path ends in the brightest place in all the forest, a sunken glade
where the light lies so thick and golden that it is like wading through
warm water. Nothing casts a shadow here, not even you. A spring rises in
the middle of the glade and spills over a lip of white stone into a
pebbled runnel. The only way out is west, back to the ring of trees.

8660.name: The Path of Light

north.description: To the north lies The Path of Light.

east.description: To the east lies The Path of Light.

8660.description:
The Path of Light bends here, its paving of pale, close-fitted stones
curving from north to east around the foot of a tall gold-leaved tree.
Each stone holds a soft glow of its own, as though it had soaked up the
daylight and could not quite let it go. Grass grows only along the edges
of the paving, never between the stones. The trees stand back on either
side, leaving the path open to a ribbon of bright sky.

8661.name: The Path of Light

north.description: To the north lies The Path of Light.

east.description: To the east lies The Path of Light.

west.description: To the west lies The Path of Light.

8661.description:
The pebbled path runs east and west here along the foot of a gentle bank
covered in golden moss, and a branch of it climbs north toward the ring
of trees. Ferns of a pale yellow-green unfurl along the bank, and the
air is warm and still. A stone trough set into the bank catches the
water of a little rill and lets it overflow into the moss. Its trickle
is the only sound.

8662.name: The Path of Light

east.description: To the east lies The Path of Light.

west.description: To the west lies The Path of Light.

8662.description:
The golden trees thin a little here, and between their trunks you catch
the first glimpses of darker woods somewhere beyond, grey and brooding
against the glow. The path runs on east and west between low banks of
moss, its white pebbles fewer now and sunk deep into the earth. A wooden
bench, silvered with age, has been set where travellers can rest and
look back at the light.

8663.name: The Path of Light

south.description: To the south lies The Edge of the Path of Light.

west.description: To the west lies The Path of Light.

8663.description:
The path turns south here, and the gold of the forest begins to fade,
the leaves overhead paler and fewer and the light a thinner yellow. A
carved post stands at the corner, a sun at its top and beneath it a
crescent moon turned on its back like a cradle. South, the path heads
toward the edge of the bright wood, and west it returns among the
shining trees.

8664.name: The Edge of the Path of Light

north.description: To the north lies The Path of Light.

south.description: To the south lies A Trail Through A Light Forest.

8664.description:
Here the Path of Light comes to its end, the last golden trees standing
in a line like a guard of honour on either side of the pebbles. Beyond
them a narrower trail runs on south through a lighter wood of slim birch
and aspen, and on both sides of it the dark Old Forest crowds close. The
glow of the radiant trees lies at your back to the north. The air grows
cooler with every step.

8671.name: In The Old Forest

north.description: To the north lies The King's Road.

east.description: To the east lies In The Old Forest.

south.description: To the south lies In The Old Forest.

west.description: To the west lies In The Old Forest.

8671.description:
Just beyond the verge of the King's Road the Old Forest begins in
earnest, and the gold of the roadside trees can still be glimpsed
through the branches to the north. A vast thicket of blackthorn blocks
the way ahead, and paths skirt it east and west, though both wind around
it to the same hidden glade. The thorns are hung with tufts of fur and
scraps of cloth. Another way leads south between grey trunks.

8672.name: In The Old Forest

north.description: To the north lies In The Old Forest.

east.description: To the east lies In The Old Forest.

south.description: To the south lies In The Old Forest.

8672.description:
A stream has cut a deep, narrow bed through the forest floor here, and
the way crosses it on a fallen trunk furred with moss. The water is
black, quick and strangely silent, and pale roots trail into it like
fingers. Water drips from every leaf long after the rain has stopped.
Paths of a sort lead north toward the King's Road, east among dense
hollies, and south into the confusing depths of the wood.

8673.name: In The Old Forest

north.description: To the north lies In The Old Forest.

east.description: To the east lies In The Old Forest.

8673.description:
This is the deep heart of the Old Forest, where every way looks the same
and the trees seem to have been placed to confuse. Grey trunks march off
in endless ranks, their crowns woven so tightly together that sun and
sky are only guesses. Many a traveller has strayed in here from the
paths and wandered in circles for days. A way of sorts leads north, and
another east toward the Trail of Shadows.

8674.name: In The Old Forest

east.description: To the east lies On The Trail Of Shadows.

west.description: To the west lies In The Old Forest.

8674.description:
Two fallen trunks lean together over the way here like the rafters of a
roofless house, and ferns sprout thickly from the rot along their backs.
Beneath them the light is the colour of weak tea. Beetles have carved
twisting galleries in the bare wood where the bark has fallen away. The
Old Forest presses close on every side, but a way leads east toward the
Trail of Shadows and west into deeper wood.

8675.name: On The Trail Of Shadows

north.description: To the north lies On The Trail Of Shadows.

south.description: To the south lies On The Trail Of Shadows.

west.description: To the west lies In The Old Forest.

8675.description:
The trail skirts a sunken pool of black water here, its surface skinned
with a film like oil and its banks bare of any growing thing. The white
bones of a horse lie half in and half out of the water, picked clean
long ago. No reflection shows in the pool, not even of the branches
overhead. North and south the trail runs on beneath the dark trees, and
west the roots of the Old Forest reach out across the path.

8676.name: On The Trail Of Shadows

north.description: To the north lies On The Trail Of Shadows.

east.description: To the east lies In The Old Forest.

south.description: To the south lies On The Trail Of Shadows.

8676.description:
Strings of small bones, feathers and knotted hair hang from the low
branches over the trail here, turning slowly though the air hangs dead
and still. Whoever hung them meant them as a warning, or a ward, and
they click softly against each other in the gloom. The trail beneath
them is bare earth, as though few care to linger. The trail runs on
north and south, and a gap in the trees opens east into the Old Forest.

8677.name: On The Trail Of Shadows

north.description: To the north lies On The Trail Of Shadows.

south.description: To the south lies On The Trail Of Shadows.

8677.description:
Low cairns of grey stones line both sides of the trail here, each the
length of a man, and some have a stick or a broken blade thrust into the
top as a marker. These are the graves of travellers who did not finish
the Trail of Shadows, buried by those who did. Several of the cairns
have been disturbed, their stones scattered. The trail runs north
between the dark trees and south toward older, stranger country.

8678.name: On The Trail Of Shadows

north.description: To the north lies On The Trail Of Shadows.

west.description: To the west lies On The Trail Of Shadows.

8678.description:
The trail bends west here around a fallen pillar of white stone, the
first sign of the ancient city that once stood somewhere in this forest.
The pillar is fluted and finely carved, but the trees have grown over
and around it, and roots grip it like a fist. The shadows beneath the
trees seem deeper here than the leaves can account for. North, the trail
leads back past the travellers' graves.

8679.name: On The Trail Of Shadows

north.description: To the north lies In The Old Forest.

east.description: To the east lies On The Trail Of Shadows.

south.description: To the south lies On The Trail Of Shadows.

8679.description:
Under the leaf litter the trail here runs on great flagstones of the
same white stone, the paving of some forgotten road. A carved head, as
large as a cartwheel and with its nose broken away, lies on its side
among the ferns, gazing at nothing. East the trail leads back to the
fallen pillar, south it follows the old paving deeper into shadow, and
north a faint way pushes into the Old Forest.

extra_descs.head carved statue stone:
The face is calm and heavy-lidded, its hair bound in a fillet of carved
leaves. Someone has painted the eyes black, and not long ago, for the
paint still shines.

8680.name: On The Trail Of Shadows

north.description: To the north lies On The Trail Of Shadows.

east.description: To the east lies On The Trail Of Shadows.

8680.description:
Every tree in this stretch of the forest is dead, grey and leafless, yet
none has fallen, and they stand in their ranks like an army turned to
stone. Without leaves they should let in the light, but the sky above
them is a dull, sunless grey, and the shadows lie thick on the old
paving. The trail turns east here, and north it leads back past the
carved head.

8681.name: On The Trail Of Shadows

south.description: To the south lies On The Trail Of Shadows.

west.description: To the west lies On The Trail Of Shadows.

8681.description:
Low walls of white stone begin to show among the trees here, the
foundations of houses swallowed long ago by the forest, their doorways
choked with nettles. A broken archway leans over the trail, its keystone
gone, yet somehow it still stands. Somewhere ahead water drips into
stone with a slow, hollow note. The trail turns south toward the heart
of the ruins, and west it runs back among the dead trees.

8682.name: On The Trail Of Shadows

north.description: To the north lies On The Trail Of Shadows.

south.description: To the south lies The Ruined City.

8682.description:
The Trail of Shadows ends before the gate of a ruined city, where two
broken towers of white stone flank the old road, their tops snapped off
and crowned with ferns. The gate between them is long gone, and the road
passes south through the gap into a wilderness of fallen walls and black
trees. Huge iron hinge-pins still jut from the towers, rusted into red
stumps. North, the trail leads back among the foundations.

8683.name: The Ruined City

north.description: To the north lies On The Trail Of Shadows.

east.description: To the east lies The Ruined City.

west.description: To the west lies In The Ruined City.

8683.description:
Inside the broken gate a wide street of white flagstones opens out,
heaved and split by the black trees that grow straight through it.
Shells of houses line it, roofless and hollow-eyed, their upper floors
long since fallen into their cellars. The silence is so complete that
your footsteps sound like trespass. Streets lead east and west through
the ruins, and north the gap between the towers leads back out to the
trail.

8684.name: The Ruined City

south.description: To the south lies The Ruined City.

west.description: To the west lies The Ruined City.

8684.description:
A colonnade of white columns runs along this street, a dozen still
standing in a row and holding nothing but the sky. Behind them the floor
of some great hall lies open to the weather, its mosaic of black and
white tiles buckled by roots. Here and there the mosaic still shows part
of a picture: a hand, a wing, a crowned head. The street turns south
past the columns, and west it leads back toward the gate.

8685.name: The Ruined City

north.description: To the north lies The Ruined City.

south.description: To the south lies In The Ruined City.

west.description: To the west lies At The Centre Of The Ruins.

8685.description:
A great fountain basin of cracked marble stands in the middle of the
street here, empty but for drifted leaves and a black puddle of
rainwater. West, through a gap in the fallen walls, a broad open space
can be seen, and at its far side the dark bulk of a building that seems
to have resisted the forest better than the rest. The street runs north
toward the colonnade and south deeper into the ruins.

8686.name: In The Ruined City

north.description: To the north lies The Ruined City.

west.description: To the west lies In The Ruined City.

8686.description:
This narrow lane winds between the ruins of tall houses, whose walls
still stand two storeys high in places, pierced by empty windows. A
