stone stair climbs the outside of one house and ends abruptly in empty
air where the upper floor used to be. Ivy hangs in curtains over
everything. The lane runs north to the fountain and west between the
walls.

8687.name: In The Ruined City

north.description: To the north lies At The Centre Of The Ruins.

east.description: To the east lies In The Ruined City.

west.description: To the west lies In The Ruined City.

8687.description:
A toppled statue lies across this crossing of ruined streets, a robed
figure twice the height of a man, broken into three pieces at the waist
and knees. Its upturned face has been worn featureless by rain. In one
stone hand it still clutches the stub of a key. North, the streets open
into a great square at the centre of the ruins, while lanes run east and
west between crumbling walls.

8688.name: At The Centre Of The Ruins

north.description: To the north lies Entrance to the Undertombs.

east.description: To the east lies The Ruined City.

south.description: To the south lies In The Ruined City.

west.description: To the west lies In The Ruined City.

8688.description:
The streets of the ruined city meet in a great round square paved in
rings of black and white stone, with a dead tree standing at its very
centre. North rises a squat, windowless temple of black rock that guards
the entrance to the Undertombs, but its doorway is sealed by an iron
grate set deep in the stone, the lock rusted into a single lump. Cold
air breathes through the bars from the darkness beyond. Streets leave
the square east, south and west.

extra_descs.temple grate doorway black:
The temple's walls are of a black stone found nowhere else in the city,
fitted without mortar. Above the grate a line of old script is cut into
the lintel, and beneath it someone has scratched a plainer warning: WHAT
IS GIVEN TO THE DARK IS NOT GIVEN BACK.

8689.name: In The Ruined City

east.description: To the east lies The Ruined City.

south.description: To the south lies In The Ruined City.

8689.description:
A corner of the old city wall stands here, still sound enough to hold
the remains of a painted fresco on its inner face: a feast in a garden
of golden trees, the dancers faded almost to ghosts. Black trees have
rooted along the foot of the wall. Rain has washed the faces from every
one of the dancers. A street runs east toward the gate, and a lane leads
south toward a court with a well.

8690.name: In The Ruined City

north.description: To the north lies In The Ruined City.

east.description: To the east lies At The Centre Of The Ruins.

south.description: To the south lies In The Ruined City.

down.description: To the down lies The Bottom Of A Well.

8690.description:
An old well stands in this small paved court, its round stone head
carved with a band of leaves and its windlass long since rotted away.
Iron rungs set into the shaft lead down into darkness, slick with moss
but still sound. From far below comes the faint, hollow sound of
dripping water. The great square lies east, and lanes lead north and
south between the ruined walls.

8691.name: In The Ruined City

north.description: To the north lies In The Ruined City.

east.description: To the east lies In The Ruined City.

south.description: To the south lies On The Narrow Trail.

8691.description:
The ruins thin out here against the remains of the city's outer wall,
which has been breached by a great tree whose trunk now fills the gap
like a cork. Beside it a small postern gate still stands, its door gone,
and a narrow trail slips out through it to the south. Moss has turned
the stones of the wall a deep, velvety green. Lanes run north toward the
well and east toward the toppled statue.

8692.name: On The Narrow Trail

north.description: To the north lies In The Ruined City.

south.description: To the south lies The Edge Of The Forest.

8692.description:
The narrow trail squeezes between walls of bramble and blackthorn, so
tight in places that the thorns snag at every step. Behind, the white
stones of the ruined city gleam among the black trees, and ahead the
gloom begins to lift, with real daylight showing between the trunks. The
air smells of crushed leaves and, faintly, of open fields. The trail
runs north back through the postern and south toward the edge of the
forest.

8693.name: The Edge Of The Forest

north.description: To the north lies On The Narrow Trail.

south.description: To the south lies The Edge Of The Forest.

8693.description:
The trees end here at the brow of a long slope, and beyond them open
country rolls away under a wide, pale sky, fields and far-off hills hazy
with distance. A trail seems to lead on south across the slope, yet
every time it is followed it curls back through a fringe of birches to
this same spot, as though the forest is unwilling to let anyone leave
this way. North, the narrow trail returns toward the ruins.

8696.name: On The Trail Of Shadows

north.description: To the north lies The King's Road.

east.description: To the east lies In The Old Forest.

south.description: To the south lies On The Trail Of Shadows.

west.description: To the west lies The King's road.

8696.description:
Under the first black trees of the Trail of Shadows the gold of the
King's Road seems a world away, though its paving still glimmers both
north and west between the trunks. The trees here are dark-barked and
close, their branches knitted into a roof that lets through only a grey,
sourceless light. Sounds carry oddly, and your own footsteps seem to
come a moment late. East, the tangled Old Forest presses in, and south
the trail runs on into deeper shadow.

8697.name: On The Trail Of Shadows

north.description: To the north lies On The Trail Of Shadows.

east.description: To the east lies In The Old Forest.

south.description: To the south lies On The Trail Of Shadows.

8697.description:
The burnt shell of a wagon lies on its side beside the trail here, its
canvas long gone and its ribs charred black. Nobody has salvaged its
wheels or iron, which says something about how little anyone cares to
linger on the Trail of Shadows. The trail runs north toward the King's
Road and south into deeper gloom, and to the east the tangle of the Old
Forest begins.

8698.name: On The Trail Of Shadows

north.description: To the north lies On The Trail Of Shadows.

east.description: To the east lies In The Old Forest.

south.description: To the south lies On The Trail Of Shadows.

8698.description:
The trail sinks into a deep cutting here, its banks so high and so
overhung with roots that it runs like a tunnel through the earth. Water
drips from the roots onto the path, and the walls of the cutting are
slick with black mud. Crow feathers, black and glossy, are stuck in the
mud at the foot of the banks. A gap in the bank to the east lets in a
little grey light from the Old Forest, and the sunken trail runs on
north and south.

8699.name: In The Old Forest

north.description: To the north lies In The Old Forest.

south.description: To the south lies In The Old Forest.

west.description: To the west lies On The Trail Of Shadows.

8699.description:
A great boulder lies among the trees here, split cleanly in two as if by
a single blow, and an oak sapling grows from the crack between the
halves. Strangely, no moss or lichen clings to its sides, though every
other stone in the Old Forest is furred with green. Ways lead north
among the willows and south toward the smell of water, and westward the
dark Trail of Shadows runs close by.

8701.name: In The Old Forest

north.description: To the north lies In The Old Forest.

south.description: To the south lies In The Old Forest.

8701.description:
The ground grows wetter here, and the forest floor gives way to beds of
royal fern and sphagnum that quake underfoot. A low mist hangs between
the alders, never rising above knee height, and the trunks seem to stand
in milk. Every sound is muffled, as if the mist swallows it. The firmest
way follows a ridge of roots north toward drier ground and south toward
the gleam of open water.

8702.name: In The Old Forest

north.description: To the north lies In The Old Forest.

east.description: To the east lies At The Forest Lake.

8702.description:
Through a screen of alders the dark water of a lake shines east, and a
trodden way slants toward it between the roots. The trees here lean out
toward the light, their trunks bent and their bark scabbed with grey
lichen. Someone long ago carved initials into a fallen trunk beside the
way, a pair of letters inside a heart, now swollen and blurred. North,
the forest closes again in mist.

8703.name: At The Forest Lake

east.description: To the east lies The Forest Lake.

west.description: To the west lies In The Old Forest.

8703.description:
The trees give way to a narrow shore of grey shingle at the edge of a
still forest lake, its water so dark that it looks bottomless. Lily pads
float in the shallows, and dead reeds rattle in the breeze. Out on the
lake a small wooded island rises, crowned by a green mound, and a
causeway of tumbled stones runs east toward it. West, the Old Forest
waits behind the alders.

8704.name: On The Muddy Path

north.description: To the north lies The King's Road.

south.description: To the south lies On The Muddy Path.

8704.description:
Leaving the golden trees behind, the path runs out into open hill
country and turns at once to mud, a sticky brown slough that sucks at
every step. Rough grass and tussocks cover the slopes on either hand,
and the wind blows cold after the shelter of the forest. Far ahead,
beyond the folded hills, bare grey crags rise into a haze that never
seems to lift. North, the trees of the King's Road glow at the top of
the slope, and the path squelches on south.

8705.name: On The Muddy Path

north.description: To the north lies On The Muddy Path.

south.description: To the south lies On The Muddy Path.

8705.description:
A cart has been abandoned here, sunk to its axles in the mire with one
wheel snapped and its shafts pointing at the sky. Whoever owned it took
the horse and left the rest to rot, and grass now grows from the boards
of its bed. The wind hums through the gorse. The path bends around the
wreck through heather, climbing north toward the forest and running on
south over the shoulder of the hill.

8706.name: On The Muddy Path

north.description: To the north lies On The Muddy Path.

east.description: To the east lies The Dead Marshes.

south.description: To the south lies On The Muddy Path.

8706.description:
A cairn of grey stones marks a parting of the ways on the hillside, its
top stone daubed with a red warning mark. East, a stony track climbs
toward the crags, where a pale mist lies over the Dead Marshes and a
smell of stagnant water drifts on the wind. No sheep graze here, and the
grass grows long and rank around the cairn. The muddy path itself winds
on south between the hills, and north it climbs back toward the forest.

8707.name: On The Muddy Path

north.description: To the north lies On The Muddy Path.

east.description: To the east lies On The Muddy Path.

8707.description:
The path fords a peaty stream here on a line of stepping stones, each
one slick with brown slime and set just a little too far from the next.
Beyond the ford the mud is churned deep, and the path bends east around
the foot of a heather-clad hill. The stream chatters over the stones,
the only cheerful sound for miles. North, the path climbs toward the
cairn at the parting of the ways.

8708.name: On The Muddy Path

east.description: To the east lies On The Muddy Path.

west.description: To the west lies On The Muddy Path.

8708.description:
Peat has been cut from the hillside here, leaving black terraced banks
above the path and a few stacks of turves drying under a heap of stones.
The diggers have not been back in some time, and water has pooled in the
cuttings, brown as strong tea. High above, grey crags hide whatever lies
beyond them. The muddy path runs on east along the slope and west around
the flank of the hill.

8709.name: On The Muddy Path

south.description: To the south lies On The Muddy Path.

west.description: To the west lies On The Muddy Path.

8709.description:
Loose scree has spilled across the path here from the crags above, and
the mud between the stones is the colour of rust. A thin spring trickles
out of the hillside into a pool ringed with cress, the only clean water
for some distance. Hoofprints of deer are pressed into the soft ground
around it. The path turns at the spring, running west along the slope
and south between two rounded hills.

8710.name: On The Muddy Path

north.description: To the north lies On The Muddy Path.

east.description: To the east lies On The Path.

8710.description:
The muddy path comes to an end in a hollow between the hills, where a
firmer track of beaten earth strikes off east toward a dark line of
trees. An old turf dyke runs across the hollow, breached where the paths
meet, and heather grows thick along its top. After so much mud the hard
ground is a relief underfoot. North, the mire leads back toward the
spring.

8711.name: On The Path

south.description: To the south lies On The Path.

west.description: To the west lies On The Muddy Path.

8711.description:
The track passes through a belt of old pines that cap the hill, their
trunks red-barked and straight and their crowns sighing in the wind.
Needles lie deep and dry underfoot, and the air is sharp with resin. Old
axe-cuts scar a few of the trunks, long since healed over with gum. The
path turns here, running south out of the pines along a ridge and west
back to the hollow where the muddy path ends.

8712.name: On The Path

north.description: To the north lies On The Path.

south.description: To the south lies On The Path.

8712.description:
The path runs along the spine of a ridge here, open to every wind, with
the land falling away in long slopes of heather and bilberry on either
side. Ahead, beyond the hills, a vast dark sea of treetops stretches to
the horizon. Clouds race low overhead, trailing their shadows across the
slopes. North, a stand of pines crowns the next rise, and southward the
path keeps to the ridge.

8713.name: On The Path

north.description: To the north lies On The Path.

south.description: To the south lies On The Path.

8713.description:
A lone hawthorn grows beside the path on this windswept stretch of
ridge, bent so far by the gales that its crown nearly brushes the
ground. In its lee stand the tumbled walls of a shepherd's bothy,
roofless now, its hearthstone still black with old fires. Tufts of wool
snagged on the thorns flutter like small grey flags. The path follows
the ridge north and south through the heather.

8714.name: On The Path

north.description: To the north lies On The Path.

west.description: To the west lies On The Path.

8714.description:
The ridge ends at a knoll of weathered grey rock, split by frost into
great blocks that lean against one another like tired giants. The path
skirts around them and turns west, slanting off the high ground through
bracken toward the edge of the dark forest. From here the country of
hills lies spread out behind you like a rumpled blanket. North, the path
runs back along the windy spine of the ridge.

8715.name: On The Path

east.description: To the east lies On The Path.

south.description: To the south lies A Small Road In The Old Forest.

8715.description:
At the foot of the hills the path reaches the edge of the Old Forest,
where enormous trees stand shoulder to shoulder like a wall. Two moss-
grown gateposts mark where a small road once began, and it runs on south
between them into the shadow beneath the boughs. East, the path climbs
back through the bracken toward the ridge. The air from the forest is
cool and smells of leaf mould.

8716.name: A Small Road In The Old Forest

north.description: To the north lies On The Path.

south.description: To the south lies On A Small Road In The Old Forest.

8716.description:
A small road runs beneath the Old Forest here, so old that only its
kerbstones still show, two lines of mossy blocks with a carpet of leaf
mould between them. Huge oaks lean over it, their limbs bearded with
ivy, and the light beneath them is a deep green dusk even at noon.
North, daylight glimmers where the road leaves the trees for the hills,
and south it runs on into the gloom.

8717.name: On A Small Road In The Old Forest

north.description: To the north lies A Small Road In The Old Forest.

east.description: To the east lies On A Small Road In Old The Forest.

south.description: To the south lies The Meteorite.

8717.description:
The small road bends east here, but something has torn a great gap in
the forest to the south, as though a giant had walked through the trees
and snapped them at the knee. Shattered trunks lie in a long swathe, all
pointing the same way, their splintered ends blackened by fire. Young
birches have sprouted among them. North, the road runs back toward the
hills.

8718.name: The Meteorite

north.description: To the north lies On A Small Road In The Old Forest.

8718.description:
At the end of the swathe of broken trees lies a wide crater, its sides
furred with young birch and its floor strangely bare. In the middle sits
the meteorite, a great lump of black, pitted stone half buried in the
earth, with a metallic sheen where the rain has washed it. The ground
around it has run and hardened like glass, and the air smells faintly of
hot iron. The only way out is north through the fallen trees.

extra_descs.meteorite stone black lump:
The stone is warm to the touch even on cold days, and a faint hum seems
to come from somewhere deep inside it. Chisel marks around its base show
where someone tried to chip a piece away, and the broken tip of the
chisel is still lodged in it, fused to the metal.

8719.name: On A Small Road In Old The Forest

east.description: To the east lies On A Small Road In The Old Forest.

west.description: To the west lies On A Small Road In The Old Forest.

8719.description:
The road crosses a brown, slow brook here on a single arch of stone so
overgrown with moss and fern that it looks more like a natural bank than
anything built. The water slides beneath without a sound, and the trees
crowd so close on either side that their roots dip into it. Long strands
of weed stream in the current like green hair. The road runs on east
into deeper shade and west toward the bend.

8720.name: On A Small Road In The Old Forest

south.description: To the south lies On A Small Road In The Old Forest.

west.description: To the west lies On A Small Road In Old The Forest.

8720.description:
An immense hollow oak stands at this turn of the road, its trunk split
open into a dark cleft wide enough to step inside, though nothing about
it invites you to. Thick grey webs are strung across the cleft and
between the lower branches, sagging with old dead leaves. The road turns
south here, and west it runs back toward the mossy bridge. The forest is
very quiet.

8721.name: On A Small Road In The Old Forest

north.description: To the north lies On A Small Road In The Old Forest.

east.description: To the east lies On A Small Road In The Old Forest.

8721.description:
Roots as thick as a man's body have pushed through the road here,
heaving its old stones into humps and hollows that make every step a
scramble. Bracket fungus, orange and cream, climbs the nearest trunks in
shelves. Somewhere overhead a branch creaks, though no wind reaches the
ground. The road turns east, and north it leads back toward the hollow
oak.

8722.name: On A Small Road In The Old Forest

south.description: To the south lies On A Small Road In The Old Forest.

west.description: To the west lies On A Small Road In The Old Forest.

8722.description:
A forest giant has fallen beside the road here, and its upturned roots
stand taller than a house, still clutching boulders in their grip. The
hole it tore in the canopy lets a single broad shaft of sunlight fall
onto the stones, and foxgloves crowd into the light, tall and purple
against the green. The road turns south past the roots, and west it
leads back over the heaved stones.

8723.name: On A Small Road In The Old Forest

north.description: To the north lies On A Small Road In The Old Forest.

south.description: To the south lies On A Small Road In The Old Forest.

8723.description:
Ancient yews close in on both sides of the road here, their trunks
fluted and twisted and their dark foliage shutting out nearly all the
light. Long ago someone carved a face into the bark of the largest, and
the tree has grown around it so that the face seems to peer out from
deep inside the wood. The road runs on north toward a patch of sunlight
and south through the yews.

extra_descs.face carving yew bark:
The face is bearded with leaves and its mouth hangs open, as if speaking
or singing. The bark has swollen around the eyes so that they look half
shut, and someone has pressed a copper coin into the mouth, now green
with age.

8724.name: On A Small Road In The Old Forest

north.description: To the north lies On A Small Road In The Old Forest.

south.description: To the south lies The Edge Of The Old Forest.

8724.description:
The trees begin to thin here, and a grey brightness shows between the
trunks ahead where the forest comes to an end. The road's old paving
reappears from under the leaf mould, cracked and tilted but still in its
lines, and brambles reach across it from both sides. Blackberries hang
heavy on them, though none have been picked. South lies the forest's
edge, and north the road plunges back among the yews.

8725.name: The Edge Of The Old Forest

north.description: To the north lies On A Small Road In The Old Forest.

8725.description:
The Old Forest ends abruptly at the lip of a steep escarpment, and so
does the road, its last stones hanging broken over a raw scar where the
hillside has slipped away. Far below and beyond, a wide country of misty
fields and distant woods stretches away under an open sky. There is no
way across the landslip. The road leads back north into the shadow of
the trees.

8726.name: The Forest Lake

south.description: To the south lies The Small Island.

west.description: To the west lies At The Forest Lake.

8726.description:
The causeway runs out across the middle of the lake here, a spine of
flat stones barely a stride wide, with black water lapping at its edges
on either hand. Some of the stones have sunk, and you must step from one
to the next over cold, clear shallows where weed waves far below. Mist
smokes off the water in thin, curling wisps. South, the causeway turns
toward the little island and its mound, and west it leads back to the
shingle shore.

8727.name: The Small Island

north.description: To the north lies The Forest Lake.

down.description: To the down lies The Barrow Mound.

8727.description:
The small island is little more than a grassy hump in the lake, ringed
with twisted thorn trees and crowned by an ancient barrow mound.
Weathered standing stones circle the mound, and on its near side a dark
doorway framed by three great slabs opens onto a stair of worn steps
that leads down into the earth. No sound reaches the island from the
forest. North, the stepping-stone causeway leads back across the water.

extra_descs.doorway slabs lintel barrow:
The lintel slab is carved with a row of spirals and a single line of
runes too worn to read. Someone has wedged a twist of rowan into a crack
above the door, and it has long since withered.

8728.name: In The Old Forest

east.description: To the east lies In The Old Forest.

south.description: To the south lies In The Old Forest.

west.description: To the west lies In The Old Forest.

8728.description:
Behind the blackthorn lies a hidden glade, where the stump of some
unimaginably old tree spreads as wide as a cottage floor, its rings too
many to count. Moss and pale toadstools have colonised its rotten heart.
Whatever felled it left no trace of axe or saw. Paths leave the glade
east and south between grey trunks, and west a way winds back around the
thorns toward the King's Road.

8729.name: In The Old Forest

south.description: To the south lies In The Old Forest.

west.description: To the west lies In The Old Forest.

8729.description:
Webs as broad as sails are strung between the firs here, grey and heavy
with dew, and some are so thick that they blot out what little light
there is. Bundles wrapped in old silk hang among them, shrivelled and
still, and it is better not to wonder what they once were. A path ducks
beneath the lowest strands, running west toward the glade and south into
deeper gloom.

8730.name: In The Old Forest

north.description: To the north lies In The Old Forest.

west.description: To the west lies In The Old Forest.

8730.description:
Holly grows so densely here that the forest becomes a maze of dark,
prickling walls, and the light that filters through is green and cold. A
gap to the west looks promising, but it winds through the thicket in a
tight circle and delivers you back to this same patch of leaf mould.
Boot prints going round and round in the soft ground show that others
have been fooled before. North, a clearer way leads back toward the
ruined hut.

8731.name: In The Old Forest

north.description: To the north lies In The Old Forest.

east.description: To the east lies In The Old Forest.

west.description: To the west lies In The Old Forest.

8731.description:
An old pitfall gapes beside the way here, a square shaft dug by hunters
long ago, its rotten cover of branches collapsed into it. Sharpened
stakes, grey and soft with age, still bristle from the leaves that fill
its bottom. It would be easy to blunder into it in the gloom. The way
edges past it, leading north toward the glade with the great stump, east
toward the ruined hut and west to the stream.

8732.name: In The Old Forest

north.description: To the north lies In The Old Forest.

south.description: To the south lies In The Old Forest.

west.description: To the west lies In The Old Forest.

8732.description:
A trapper's hut once stood in this hollow, but only its chimney of piled
stones still stands upright, the rest a heap of rotten logs smothered in
bramble. A rusted iron hook juts from the chimney breast where a kettle
once hung. Whoever lived here left in a hurry, or did not leave at all.
Faint paths lead north toward the webbed firs, south into a tangle of
holly, and west between the grey trunks.

8733.name: In The Old Forest

north.description: To the north lies In The Old Forest.

south.description: To the south lies In The Old Forest.

west.description: To the west lies On The Trail Of Shadows.

8733.description:
The Old Forest closes in at once, a press of ancient, lichen-grey trunks
that seem to stand a little nearer each time you look away. A path of
sorts leads north between them, but it twists among the roots and
somehow returns you to where you began. Dead leaves lie ankle-deep, and
nothing stirs in them. South, the trees open a gap into deeper forest,
and west lies the dim Trail of Shadows.

8734.name: In The Old Forest

north.description: To the north lies In The Old Forest.

east.description: To the east lies In The Old Forest.

south.description: To the south lies In The Old Forest.

west.description: To the west lies On The Trail Of Shadows.

8734.description:
Paths fork and fork again in this part of the Old Forest, and the ways
north and east, though they set off in different directions, soon wind
together among the same grey trunks. A dead elm stands in the midst of
them, white and barkless, its bare limbs spread like a signpost that has
forgotten its words. South, the forest grows darker still, and west the
Trail of Shadows passes close by.

8735.name: In The Old Forest

north.description: To the north lies In The Old Forest.

south.description: To the south lies In The Old Forest.

8735.description:
Grey willows of enormous age begin to crowd among the other trees here,
their trunks split and hollow and their long leaves hissing softly
though the air is still. The ground is soft and black, and roots loop
out of it like the ribs of buried things. It is hard to shake the
feeling that the willows are listening. A narrow way threads north
between the trunks and south toward damper ground.

8736.name: The Dead Marshes

east.description: To the east lies The Dead Marshes.

south.description: To the south lies On The Muddy Path.

west.description: To the west lies On The Muddy Path.

8736.description:
The Dead Marshes lie in a high bowl among the crags, a maze of black
pools and sodden moss threaded between ribs of bare grey rock. Nothing
green grows here; the reeds are brown and broken, and the water is so
still it holds the sky like dark glass. The cold bites deeper than the
height alone can explain. A stony gully leads south off the rock toward
the lower path, the track from the cairn returns west, and the marsh
stretches on east.

8737.name: The Dead Marshes

north.description: To the north lies The Dead Marshes.

south.description: To the south lies On The Muddy Path.

west.description: To the west lies The Dead Marshes.

8737.description:
A crag of bare rock rears over the marsh here, its face streaked white
where water seeps from the cracks. Below it a long black mere lies edged
with rotting reeds, and a line of flat stones, set by some forgotten
hand, picks across the bog. Beneath the still water pale shapes seem to
drift and turn, though they are gone whenever you look straight at them.
The stones lead north and west through the marsh, and a scree slope
falls away south toward the muddy path.

8738.name: The Dead Marshes

south.description: To the south lies The Dead Marshes.

8738.description:
The marsh ends against a sheer wall of dark rock, and the last of the
bog lies in its shadow, where old grey snow survives in the crevices
long after the thaw. A ring of standing stones rises from the black
water, half drowned and leaning, their tops crusted with pale lichen.
The air is utterly still and very cold. The only way out is back south
across the stepping stones.

extra_descs.standing stones ring carvings:
The stones are carved with rows of small figures linked hand to hand,
walking into water that the carver drew as wavy lines. Whatever the
figures were walking toward has been worn away, or deliberately broken
off.

209000.name: Entrance to the wine yard

east.description: To the east lies The Great Field Of Garathorm.

west.description: To the west lies A small road in the wine yard.

209000.description:
A low wall of fieldstone marks the edge of the wine yard, broken here by
a wooden gate that hangs open on leather hinges. Beyond it rows of vines
march away over a gentle slope, each one tied to its stake and trimmed
with care. East, the open grass of the Great Field rolls away under a
wide sky, and a cart track leads west into the vineyard between the
rows. The air carries the faint sweetness of ripening grapes.

209001.name: A small road in the wine yard

north.description: To the north lies The wine field.

east.description: To the east lies Entrance to the wine yard.

west.description: To the west lies A small road in the wine yard.

209001.description:
The small road through the wine yard is little more than two wheel ruts
with a strip of clover growing between them. Vines crowd close on both
sides, their broad leaves filmed with dust, and a row of straw beehives
stands at the end of one row. A path turns north between the stakes into
the wine field, while the track carries on west toward a farmhouse and
back east to the gate.

209002.name: A small road in the wine yard

east.description: To the east lies A small road in the wine yard.

west.description: To the west lies Outside the farmhouse.

209002.description:
The cart track bends past a tumbledown shed where pruning hooks once
hung, and the vines give way to a scrubby patch of herbs gone wild.
Thyme and rosemary crush underfoot and sweeten the air with every step.
West, the roof of a farmhouse and a larger building beside it show above
a line of pear trees, and the track runs back east between the vine
rows.

209003.name: Outside the farmhouse

north.description: To the north lies Inside a large building.

east.description: To the east lies A small road in the wine yard.

west.description: To the west lies In the Kitchen.

209003.description:
A packed-earth yard spreads before a whitewashed farmhouse with a mossy
slate roof and blue shutters. To the north stands a much larger building
of dressed stone, its wide doors open and smelling of crushed grapes and
old oak. A stout door leads west into the farmhouse kitchen, where a
chimney breathes a thin thread of smoke. East, the cart track runs back
out among the vines, and a well with a wooden windlass stands in the
middle of the yard.

209004.name: In the Kitchen

east.description: To the east lies Outside the farmhouse.

up.description: To the up lies The bedroom.

209004.description:
The farmhouse kitchen is low and warm, its rafters hung with bunches of
drying herbs and long plaits of onions. A broad hearth fills one wall,
an iron pot-crane swung back over cold ashes, and a scrubbed table runs
down the middle of the room. A narrow stair climbs up toward the
bedroom, but the door at its head is barred and nailed shut. The kitchen
door opens east onto the farmyard.

209006.name: Inside a large building

south.description: To the south lies Outside the farmhouse.

down.description: To the down lies In the wine cellar.

209006.description:
This is the vineyard's pressing house, a long hall of whitewashed stone
under heavy roof beams. A great wooden wine press with a screw as thick
as a man's waist fills one end, its trough stained purple by years of
vintages. Steps lead down toward the wine cellar, but a stout iron grate
has been locked across them and the stair beyond is black and cold. The
doorway south opens onto the farmyard and the daylight.

209009.name: The wine field

north.description: To the north lies At the end of the wine field.

south.description: To the south lies A small road in the wine yard.

209009.description:
Here the vines grow thickest, row upon row of gnarled black stocks bowed
under clusters of dark grapes. The soil between them is pale and stony,
raked clean of weeds and warm to the touch where the sun has lain on it.
A scarecrow in a tattered red coat leans over the rows on its pole, arms
spread wide. The rows run on north to the far end of the field, and a
gap between the stakes leads south to the cart track.

209010.name: At the end of the wine field

south.description: To the south lies The wine field.

209010.description:
The vineyard ends against an old hawthorn hedge, so thick and thorny
that no cart could ever push through it. A stone trough from some long-
abandoned press sits at the foot of the last row, green with moss and
half filled with rainwater. From this rise the whole wine yard can be
seen sloping gently away, its rows combed as straight as the threads on
a loom. The only way out lies south, back among the vines.

9136.name: On A Dirt Road

east.description: To the east lies The Road Crossing.

west.description: To the west lies On A Dirt Road.

9136.description:
A dirt road strikes off across rough heath here, its surface pale with
dust and pocked with hoofprints. West, the road vanishes into the open
doors of an enormous old barn that straddles the way like a gatehouse.
Gorse and broom grow thick on either side, and far beyond them rise the
grey shoulders of mountains. East, the road returns to the signpost at
the crossing.

9137.name: On A Dirt Road

east.description: To the east lies On A Dirt Road.

west.description: To the west lies On A Dirt Road.

9137.description:
The dirt road runs straight through a vast tithe barn, in at one pair of
great doors and out at the other, so that carts can pass through without
unloading. Massive cruck beams arch overhead like the ribs of an
upturned ship, and light slants in through narrow slits in the stone
walls. Chaff and dust lie thick on the floor, and the sweet, dusty scent
of old hay hangs everywhere. The far doors open west onto the road, and
the near ones east toward the heath.

9138.name: On A Dirt Road

east.description: To the east lies On A Dirt Road.

west.description: To the west lies On A Dirt Road.

9138.description:
Beyond the barn the dirt road enters a long covered way built of logs
and roofed with turf, raised to keep winter drifts off the road as it
climbs toward the hills. Light falls through gaps between the logs in
pale bars, and the air inside is cold and smells of resin and damp
earth. Dark streaks on the timbers show where meltwater runs each
spring. The covered way runs on west toward a rocky spur and back east
to the barn.

9139.name: On A Dirt Road

east.description: To the east lies On A Dirt Road.

west.description: To the west lies On A Rocky Mountain Road.

9139.description:
The road burrows through a spur of rock here in a short, rough tunnel,
its walls hacked out by hand and blackened by the smoke of old torches.
Rusted iron brackets jut from the walls at intervals, and daylight
glimmers faintly at either end. Water trickles down one wall and runs
off along a gutter cut beside the road. The tunnel opens west onto a
rockier road and east into the covered way.

9140.name: On A Rocky Mountain Road

east.description: To the east lies On A Dirt Road.

west.description: To the west lies On A Rocky Mountain Trail.

9140.description:
Here the road becomes a gallery cut into the side of the mountain,
roofed by the overhanging rock and walled on its outer side with heavy
masonry. Narrow openings in that wall let in a cold, thin light and a
wind that whistles as it passes. Fallen stones lie heaped along the
inner wall where the roof has shed them. The gallery climbs west toward
a steeper trail and runs back east into the tunnel.

9141.name: On A Rocky Mountain Trail

east.description: To the east lies On A Rocky Mountain Road.

up.description: To the up lies On A Rocky Mountain Trail.

9141.description:
The gallery ends in a cramped cleft roofed over by great fallen slabs,
where the road dwindles to a trail of broken rock. Rough steps hacked
into the stone climb up through a gap between the slabs toward the open
mountainside. The walls are daubed with crude marks in red ochre, and a
foul, animal stink drifts in from above. East, the gallery leads back
along the face of the mountain.

9142.name: Along The Road To Nowhere

west.description: To the west lies The Road Crossing.

9142.description:
A carved archway opens into the side of the hill, and the paved road
runs on inside it as a broad tunnel of fine masonry, lit only by the
daylight from the arch. After some distance the stonework simply stops,
and the road ends against a face of raw rock scarred with old chisel
marks. Letters carved over the inner side of the arch break off in mid-
sentence. Whoever began this road never finished it, and the only way
out is back west to the crossroads.

extra_descs.letters carving arch inscription:
The letters are deep and handsome: THIS ROAD LEADS TO. There the carving
ends, and the next stone has been left smooth.

9700.name: Danozi Avenue

north.description: To the north lies Danozi Avenue.

east.description: To the east lies Jeweller's.

south.description: To the south lies Danozi Avenue.

9700.description:
An iron gate on the east side of the avenue leads into the Jeweller's, a
small walled yard behind a front of carved white stone. Above the gate
hangs a gilded ring as big as a cartwheel, set with a great glass stone
that flashes whenever the light strikes it. Danozi Avenue runs north and
south past the gate.

9701.name: Trade Road

east.description: To the east lies Inside the West Gate of Garathorm.

west.description: To the west lies Trade Road.

9701.description:
The Trade Road runs east here to the West Gate of Garathorm, where two
small towers built into the city wall are joined by a footbridge high
above a heavy wooden gate. Carts queue along the road waiting their turn
to pass inside, and the stones are rutted deep by their wheels. West,
the road leads back to the market cross and on to the Western Gatehouse.

9702.name: Trade Road

north.description: To the north lies Trade Road.

east.description: To the east lies Esh Road.

south.description: To the south lies The Gate Of The Inner City.

west.description: To the west lies Shokogya Street.

9702.description:
The Trade Road begins here in the shadow of Garathorm's inner wall,
where the great gate of the Inner City stands open to the south.
Merchants' houses of timber and pale stone lean over the cobbles, their
upper storeys hung with painted signs lettered in half a dozen trading
tongues. Esh Road branches off east past a row of counting-houses, and
Shokogya Street runs west beneath striped awnings. Northward the Trade
Road climbs gently toward the outer gate, its stones rutted by countless
cartwheels.

9703.name: Trade Road

east.description: To the east lies Trade Road.

west.description: To the west lies The Gate To The Inner City.

9703.description:
Here the Trade Road leaves the inner city by the Gate To The Inner City,
whose two small towers rise from the wall just to the west with a
footbridge slung between them above the gate's heavy timbers. The road
is paved with broad flagstones that slope toward deep gutters, and the
traffic of carts never seems to slacken. East, the road runs on to a
busy crossing with Pasocaoa Boulevard and Esh Road.

9704.name: Stonewalk Way

east.description: To the east lies The Southern Gatehouse.

west.description: To the west lies Stonewalk Way.

9704.description:
Iron rings for tethering horses are set into the town wall along this
stretch, and the cobbles beneath them are strewn with straw and worse.
Across the way a livery stable stands with its wide doors open,
breathing out the warm smell of hay and horse. East lies the Southern
Gatehouse, and west Stonewalk Way runs on between the wall and the
houses.

9705.name: Stonewalk Way

north.description: To the north lies Boarding House.

east.description: To the east lies Stonewalk Way.

west.description: To the west lies Stonewalk Way.

9705.description:
A tall, narrow house of grey stone on the north side of the street hangs
out a painted board that promises ROOMS AND BOARD, CLEAN BEDS, NO
BRAWLING. Its doorstep is freshly whitened and its windows are hung with
patched but tidy curtains. Across the street the town wall is pocked
with old scars where carts have scraped it. Stonewalk Way runs east
toward the gate and west along the wall.

9706.name: Stonewalk Way

east.description: To the east lies Trade Road.

west.description: To the west lies Stonewalk Way.

9706.description:
An iron fire bell hangs from a timber frame at the edge of the raised
walk here, its rope looped up out of the reach of children. A painted
board beneath it warns that anyone who rings it falsely will pay a
silver piece to the watch. East, the street opens onto the Trade Road
beneath the gate of the inner city, and west it follows the wall.

9707.name: Danozi Avenue

north.description: To the north lies Danozi Avenue.

south.description: To the south lies Danozi Avenue.

9707.description:
An apothecary's narrow shop front is hung with bunches of drying herbs,
and a great stone mortar and pestle stand on the step outside by way of
a sign. The air around its door smells of sage, camphor and something
bitter that catches in the throat. Danozi Avenue runs north toward the
Trade Road and south toward the Jeweller's gate.

9708.name: Shokogya Street

north.description: To the north lies Shokogya Street.

south.description: To the south lies Shokogya Street.

9708.description:
Cookshops crowd both sides of the street here, their counters open to
passers-by and their charcoal grills sending up fragrant smoke. The
smells of ginger, garlic and hot fat mingle beneath the striped awnings.
The street is so narrow that the awnings almost touch overhead, and it
runs on north and south.

9709.name: Stonewalk Way

north.description: To the north lies Stonewalk Way.

east.description: To the east lies Stonewalk Way.

9709.description:
A squat round tower bulges from the town wall at this corner, its arrow
slits dark and its roof of weathered shingles sagging in the middle.
Stonewalk Way bends around its foot, running north toward Danozi Avenue
and east along the wall toward the Southern Gatehouse. Moss grows thick
in the tower's shade, softening the edges of the raised stone walk.

9710.name: Stonewalk Way

east.description: To the east lies Stonewalk Way.

south.description: To the south lies Stonewalk Way.

9710.description:
A massive buttress of the inner city wall juts into the street here,
forcing Stonewalk Way to bend around it from south to east. Its lowest
stones are blackened by the braziers that pedlars have lit in its
shelter for generations. High above, the walls of Garathorm are crowned
with crenellations, and a banner stirs on its pole above the parapet.

9711.name: Stonewalk Way

east.description: To the east lies Stonewalk Way.

west.description: To the west lies Stonewalk Way.

9711.description:
The common bakehouse of the quarter stands here against the inner wall,
its great brick oven fired before dawn so that the whole street smells
of fresh bread by first light. Flour dust whitens the raised walk
outside its door, printed with the tracks of many boots. Stonewalk Way
runs east toward the Trade Road and west to where the wall's great
buttress turns it.

9712.name: Shokogya Street

north.description: To the north lies Shokogya Street.

east.description: To the east lies Grebe's Tavern.

south.description: To the south lies Shokogya Street.

9712.description:
A signboard painted with a crested water bird swings above a low door on
the east side of the street, marking Grebe's Tavern. Its bow window
glows with lamplight, and the hum of talk and the clink of tankards
spill out whenever the door swings open. The awnings of Shokogya Street
run on north and south.

9713.name: Shokogya Street

north.description: To the north lies Shokogya Street.

south.description: To the south lies Shokogya Street.

9713.description:
A lantern-maker's shop opens onto the street here, its front hung with
paper lanterns of every size, from little globes no bigger than an apple
to great drums that could light a hall. Frames of split cane are stacked
by its door, waiting for their paper. North, the street runs on toward
its corner, and south it leads back past Grebe's Tavern.

9714.name: Trade Road

north.description: To the north lies The Gate Of The Inner City.

east.description: To the east lies Stonewalk Way.

south.description: To the south lies Trade Road.

west.description: To the west lies Stonewalk Way.

9714.description:
The Trade Road meets the inner city here, running north through the Gate
Of The Inner City between two round towers hung with Garathorm's
banners. A stone pillar at the roadside is carved with the names of
distant places and the leagues to each. Stonewalk Way runs off east and
west along the foot of the wall, and south the road passes beneath a
long vaulted roof on its way to the outer gate.

extra_descs.pillar stone names leagues:
The pillar lists New Thalos, Port Halyon, Haon-Dor and the Dwarven
Kingdom, each with a tally of leagues cut beside it. At the bottom a
newer hand has carved TOWNSBRIDGE, and a later one has struck it
through.

9715.name: Pasocaoa Boulevard

north.description: To the north lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

south.description: To the south lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

west.description: To the west lies Butcher's Shop.

9715.description:
A painted wooden ox head juts from the wall above a shop door on the
west side of the boulevard, the sign of the Butcher's Shop. Sawdust
tracked out from its floor lies scattered over the paving, and the
gutter here runs faintly pink whenever the shop is washed down. Even the
scent of the lindens cannot quite cover the smell of fresh meat. The
boulevard leads on north and south.

9716.name: Pasocaoa Boulevard

north.description: To the north lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

south.description: To the south lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

9716.description:
The roots of an old linden have heaved the paving into a hump here, and
the stones have been left to tilt rather than see the tree cut back.
Behind it a chandler's shop faces the street, a gilded wooden candle
hanging over its door and the warm, greasy smell of tallow seeping from
its shutters. North lies the butcher's sign, and south the boulevard
runs straight on between its trees.

9717.name: Danozi Avenue

north.description: To the north lies Danozi Avenue.

south.description: To the south lies Danozi Avenue.

9717.description:
A joiner's workshop stands open to the street here, with a carved chair
hung on a bracket above its door by way of a sign. The rasp of saws and
the sweet smell of fresh-cut pine spill out of it, along with the
sawdust that drifts across the paving. Danozi Avenue continues north and
south between its rows of jutting houses.

9718.name: Pasocaoa Boulevard

east.description: To the east lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

west.description: To the west lies Stonewalk Way.

9718.description:
This last stretch of the boulevard is narrower and plainer than the
rest, lined with low houses of whitewashed brick whose doors open
straight onto the street. Blue tiles still frame a few of the windows,
but the grand lattices and courtyards are left behind. West, the paving
changes to the heavy grey flags of Stonewalk Way, while east the
boulevard swings round its corner.

9719.name: Stonewalk Way

north.description: To the north lies Stonewalk Way.

east.description: To the east lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

south.description: To the south lies Stonewalk Way.

9719.description:
Here Stonewalk Way earns its name, for raised walks of dressed stone run
along both sides of the street a step above the cobbles, so that folk on
foot can keep their boots out of the gutter. The houses are built of the
same grey stone, solid and plain, with deep-set windows. The street runs
north and south, and east it meets the tail of Pasocaoa Boulevard.

9720.name: Danozi Avenue

north.description: To the north lies Danozi Avenue.

south.description: To the south lies Danozi Avenue.

9720.description:
Squares numbered in white paint mark out pitches along the edges of the
paving here, where hawkers set up their trestles on market days. Between
markets the squares stand empty and the street feels oddly wide and
quiet. The noise of the Trade Road carries down from the north, and the
avenue runs south between its chestnut trees.

9721.name: Danozi Avenue

north.description: To the north lies Danozi Avenue.

east.description: To the east lies Brewery.

south.description: To the south lies Danozi Avenue.

9721.description:
The Brewery fills the east side of the avenue here, a long building of
brick with a tall chimney that breathes out sweet-smelling steam. Its
wide doors are painted with a sheaf of barley crossed with a foaming
tankard, and a ramp of planks lets barrels roll straight out into the
street. North and south the avenue runs on beneath the chestnut trees.

9722.name: Trade Road

north.description: To the north lies Esh Road.

east.description: To the east lies The Eastern Gatehouse.

south.description: To the south lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

west.description: To the west lies Trade Road.

9722.description:
The Trade Road ends its run through the outer town here at the Eastern
Gatehouse, whose squat towers loom just to the east. This is a busy
crossing: Esh Road leads north between tall merchant houses, Pasocaoa
Boulevard opens broad and straight to the south, and the Trade Road
itself stretches back west toward the inner city. A long stone trough
for watering horses stands beside the gate, and the cobbles around it
are never quite dry.

9723.name: Trade Road

north.description: To the north lies Shokogya Street.

east.description: To the east lies Trade Road.

south.description: To the south lies Danozi Avenue.

west.description: To the west lies The Western Gatehouse.

9723.description:
Four ways meet at this busy crossing, where a stone market cross stands
on a round step worn hollow by sitters. The Trade Road runs west to the
Western Gatehouse and east toward the gate of the inner city, while
Shokogya Street leads off north beneath striped awnings and Danozi
Avenue runs south. Carts jostle around the cross from every side, and
the din of wheels and voices never quite dies away.

9724.name: Stonewalk Way

east.description: To the east lies Stonewalk Way.

west.description: To the west lies Trade Road.

9724.description:
A farrier's forge opens onto the street here, its wide doorway glowing
red and its anvil ringing whenever there is a horse to be shod. The
smell of scorched hoof and coal smoke hangs over the raised walks. West,
the street opens onto the Trade Road below the gate of the inner city,
and east Stonewalk Way runs on beneath the wall.

9725.name: Stonewalk Way

east.description: To the east lies Stonewalk Way.

west.description: To the west lies Stonewalk Way.

9725.description:
Narrow houses have been built right up against the inner city wall along
this stretch, their roofs propped against its stones like tired men
leaning on a fence. Their chimneys climb the wall in a row of soot-
stained flues, and smoke drifts lazily along its face. The raised stone
walk runs on east and west, its edge rounded by generations of
footsteps.

9726.name: Pasocaoa Boulevard

north.description: To the north lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

south.description: To the south lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

west.description: To the west lies Ceran's Contracting.

9726.description:
Scaffolding of lashed poles climbs the front of a house here, and stacks
of timber, sand and roofing slate are piled in the yard beside it. A
signboard over a door on the west side shows a plumb line and a set
square, with the name Ceran's Contracting lettered neatly beneath. Fine
dust from the yard settles on everything. The boulevard runs north
beneath the last of the lindens and south toward its corner.

9727.name: Pasocaoa Boulevard

north.description: To the north lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

west.description: To the west lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

9727.description:
Pasocaoa Boulevard bends sharply here, turning west from its long
straight run. A round corner house with a conical slate roof stands in
the angle, and a stone mounting block worn into steps waits at its foot
for riders. The lindens have given out, and the paving is scored by the
wheels of carts swinging round the turn. North, the boulevard runs back
toward the Trade Road.

9728.name: Stonewalk Way

north.description: To the north lies Stonewalk Way.

south.description: To the south lies Stonewalk Way.

west.description: To the west lies Danozi Avenue.

9728.description:
Danozi Avenue begins here, opening west beneath a pair of tall chestnut
trees, while Stonewalk Way carries on north and south. A carved stone
post at the corner bears the names of both streets, the letters picked
out in flaking red paint. The houses along this stretch are built of the
same grey stone as the walks, and their doors are set deep in arched
porches.

9729.name: Danozi Avenue

east.description: To the east lies Stonewalk Way.

west.description: To the west lies Danozi Avenue.

9729.description:
Two old chestnut trees spread their branches over the start of Danozi
Avenue, and every autumn their spiny husks crunch underfoot. The avenue
runs west from here between tall houses of timber and plaster, each
storey jutting out a little further over the street than the one below.
East, the way meets the grey stones and raised walks of Stonewalk Way.

9730.name: Danozi Avenue

north.description: To the north lies Danozi Avenue.

east.description: To the east lies Danozi Avenue.

9730.description:
Lines of washing are strung between the upper windows here, sheets and
shirts flapping across the street like the sails of a becalmed ship. A
laundry at the corner breathes out steam and the sharp smell of lye, and
its gutter runs grey with soapy water. Danozi Avenue bends at this
point, running north along the edge of the town and east toward
Stonewalk Way.

9731.name: Stonewalk Way

south.description: To the south lies Stonewalk Way.

west.description: To the west lies Stonewalk Way.

9731.description:
The great wall of Garathorm's inner city rises close at hand here, so
tall that the street lies in its shadow for most of the day. Stonewalk
Way turns at this corner, running west along the foot of the wall and
south away from it. Ivy has climbed a little way up the stones before
being cut back, leaving dry brown tendrils clinging to the mortar.

9732.name: Stonewalk Way

north.description: To the north lies Stonewalk Way.

west.description: To the west lies Stonewalk Way.

9732.description:
Stonewalk Way turns a corner here, running north toward the end of
Pasocaoa Boulevard and west along the inside of the town wall. An iron
pump stands at the corner over a stone basin, green with slime where its
drips fall. A small niche in the wall above it holds a weathered carving
of a cloaked traveller, the paint long faded from its face.

9733.name: Danozi Avenue

north.description: To the north lies Danozi Avenue.

east.description: To the east lies Ship Shop.

south.description: To the south lies Danozi Avenue.

9733.description:
A ship's anchor taller than a man leans against a shop on the east side
of the avenue, and a carved wooden mermaid juts out above its door like
the figurehead of a vessel run aground. This is the Ship Shop, a strange
sight so far from any sea, though boats are always wanted on the Long
Lake and the rivers. The smell of tar and hemp drifts out onto the
street, which runs north and south.

9734.name: Shokogya Street

east.description: To the east lies Shokogya Street.

south.description: To the south lies Shokogya Street.

9734.description:
Shokogya Street turns a corner here, running east along the inner wall
and south back among the cookshops. A tea house occupies the angle, its
round window framed in lacquered red wood and its doorway hung with a
curtain of clicking wooden beads. The scent of smoky tea and jasmine
drifts out into the street.

9735.name: Butcher's Shop

east.description: To the east lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

9735.description:
Iron hooks hang in rows from a rail along the ceiling of the Butcher's
Shop, and a great chopping block, worn hollow by the cleaver, stands in
the middle of a floor strewn with sawdust. A cold slab of slate runs the
length of the counter, and a board above it chalks up the prices of
mutton, pork and beef. The air is cool and smells of blood and brine. A
door in the east wall lets out onto Pasocaoa Boulevard.

9736.name: Jeweller's

west.description: To the west lies Danozi Avenue.

9736.description:
The Jeweller's is a small yard paved with white stone and walled on
three sides, open to the sky so that the jeweller can work by honest
daylight. A workbench fitted with tiny vices and a lens on a brass arm
stands beneath a canvas awning, and a barred window in the back wall
looks into the strongroom where the finer pieces are kept. The iron gate
to Danozi Avenue lies west.

9737.name: Shokogya Street

north.description: To the north lies Shokogya Street.

south.description: To the south lies Trade Road.

9737.description:
Shokogya Street begins beneath a canopy of striped awnings, red and
white and saffron, stretched from house to house so that the light below
is warm and coloured. Strings of paper lanterns sway between the awning
poles. The street runs north from here, and south it opens onto the
crossing of the Trade Road.

9738.name: Rubble and Ruin

east.description: To the east lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

9738.description:
Here a house once stood between its neighbours, but now there is only a
hummock of tumbled stone, charred beams and broken roof tiles, grown
over with nettles, gorse and tufts of heather. The soot-blackened walls
of the houses on either side rise above the mound like the sides of a
narrow valley, open to the sky. Wind whistles through their empty window
holes. East, a rough path picks its way over the stones back to Pasocaoa
Boulevard.

9739.name: Brewery

west.description: To the west lies Danozi Avenue.

9739.description:
Great copper kettles squat over brick furnaces in this hot and steamy
hall, and a row of oaken mash tuns stands along one wall, each big
enough to drown an ox. The air is thick with the smell of malt and hops,
and the stone floor is slick underfoot. A chalk board by the door keeps
a tally of barrels sold. The way out to Danozi Avenue is west.

9740.name: Sakifan's Library

east.description: To the east lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

9740.description:
Shelves of dark wood climb every wall of Sakifan's Library, crammed with
books, scrolls in pigeonholes and bundles of papers tied with faded
ribbon. Reading desks stand in a row beneath shaded lamps, and a
lettered board by the door sets out the library's rules. The air is
hushed and smells of old paper, leather and lamp oil. The door out to
Pasocaoa Boulevard lies east.

extra_descs.board rules lettered:
NO INK NEAR THE SCROLLS. NO FOOD. NO FIRE BUT THE LAMPS. NO SINGING,
SHOUTING OR DUELLING. BOOKS LEAVE THIS ROOM BY NO MEANS WHATSOEVER,
MAGICAL OR OTHERWISE. Someone has underlined the last rule twice.

9741.name: Leatherworker's Shop

west.description: To the west lies Danozi Avenue.

9741.description:
Hides of every shade hang from rails beneath the ceiling of the
Leatherworker's Shop, from pale kidskin to oxhide as stiff as board. A
long bench under the window is scarred by countless knife cuts and
fitted with a clamp for stitching, and the air is heavy with the smell
of tannin and neatsfoot oil. Pegs along one wall hold belts, satchels
and saddlebags. The street door is west.

9742.name: Ceran's Contracting

east.description: To the east lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

9742.description:
Ceran's Contracting is more office than workshop, a cluttered room where
plans of houses, walls and bridges are pinned over every inch of
plaster. A broad drawing table stands beneath the window, its sheets
held down with stones and set squares, and measuring rods, plumb bobs
and knotted cords hang from pegs by the door. Samples of brick and tile
are lined along a shelf like a collection of curiosities. The door out
to Pasocaoa Boulevard is east.

9743.name: Boarding House

east.description: To the east lies Hallway.

south.description: To the south lies Stonewalk Way.

9743.description:
The front room of the boarding house is plain but scrubbed, with a row
of hooks for wet cloaks beside the door and a worn rag rug before a
small hearth. A high desk holds a fat ledger and an inkpot, and behind
it hangs a board of numbered pegs for the keys of the rooms. A doorway
leads east into a narrow hallway, and the street door opens south onto
Stonewalk Way.

9744.name: Hallway

west.description: To the west lies Boarding House.

9744.description:
A narrow hallway runs back from the front room of the boarding house,
its floorboards creaking at every step. Doors line both walls, each
painted with a number and each firmly locked, and a single lamp in a
niche at the far end gives the only light. The air smells of boiled
cabbage and damp wool. The way out lies west, back to the front room.

9745.name: A private home

south.description: To the south lies Shokogya Street.

9745.description:
This is the main room of a modest family home, warm and a little
cluttered. A table scrubbed pale stands before a hearth where a
blackened kettle hangs on its hook, and a bench along the wall is heaped
with cushions stitched from scraps of bright cloth. Children's drawings
are pinned to the plaster, and a curtained alcove hides a bed. The
street door lies south.

9746.name: A private home

south.description: To the south lies Esh Road.

9746.description:
The ground floor of this narrow house is a single long room, cool and
dim behind closed shutters, with a floor of red tiles and walls hung
with painted silk. A shrine shelf holds a few small figures and a dish
of grey incense ash. A cushioned bench runs beneath a row of empty
birdcages of delicate bamboo. The door south, painted with golden fish,
opens back onto Esh Road.

9747.name: A private home

north.description: To the north lies Esh Road.

9747.description:
This snug home belongs to a family of merchants, and their trade shows
in every corner: a rug woven with birds and vines covers the floor,
lacquered chests stand against the walls, and a brass lamp of fine
filigree hangs from a beam, scattering tiny points of light. Low
cushions surround a table barely a foot high. The air smells of
sandalwood and tea. The green door north leads back out to Esh Road.

9748.name: Esh Road

north.description: To the north lies Esh Road.

south.description: To the south lies Esh Road.

9748.description:
The smell of spices hangs thick in the air here, pouring from the open
doors of a long warehouse where sacks are stacked to the rafters:
pepper, cinnamon, cloves and stranger things from lands beyond the
desert. A brass weighing beam hangs above the doorway. The road runs on
north toward the trading post and south toward the Trade Road. The
gutter beside the cobbles is stained yellow with spilled saffron.

9749.name: Esh Road

north.description: To the north lies Esh Road.

south.description: To the south lies Trade Road.

9749.description:
Esh Road leaves the bustle of the Trade Road here and runs north between
tall houses of timber and pale plaster, their upper floors jutting out
on carved brackets until they nearly meet overhead. Painted shutters in
red and saffron hang open beside the windows. The street is paved with
small, close-set cobbles laid in sweeping fan patterns. South, the
clamour of the gatehouse crossing carries up the street.

9750.name: Ship Shop

west.description: To the west lies Danozi Avenue.

9750.description:
Coils of rope as thick as a man's wrist are heaped around the walls of
the Ship Shop, and oars of every length stand racked in a corner like
spears in an armoury. The half-built hull of a small rowing boat rests
on trestles in the middle of the floor, its ribs bare and smelling of
fresh pine and pitch. A painted chart of the Long Lake is nailed above
the counter. The door to Danozi Avenue lies west.

extra_descs.chart long lake map:
The chart shows the Long Lake as a long blue finger among green woods,
with the rangers' camp marked by a tiny tent on its shore. In the
deepest water someone has painted a coiling serpent, more in jest than
in warning, or so you hope.

9751.name: Wrecked Shop

south.description: To the south lies Stonewalk Way.

9751.description:
Whatever this shop once sold, nothing of it is left. Its shelves have
been dragged down and smashed, its counter split with an axe, and its
drawers wrenched out and flung across the floor. Several floorboards
have been prised up, as if someone searched for a hidden strongbox, and
the air smells of damp plaster and spilled lamp oil. Pale light falls
through the broken window and the doorway to the south, which opens onto
Stonewalk Way.

9752.name: Grebe's Tavern

west.description: To the west lies Shokogya Street.

9752.description:
Grebe's Tavern is low-beamed and smoky, its ceiling hung with pewter
tankards on hooks and its walls with paintings of water birds in every
attitude of dignity and foolishness. A long bar of dark wood runs down
one side, backed by casks with brass taps, and a fire crackles in a wide
stone hearth. Benches and tables crowd every corner. The door out to
Shokogya Street lies west.

9753.name: Trading Post

east.description: To the east lies Esh Road.

9753.description:
Long counters of scarred oak divide this trading post in two, and a
great brass-bound balance hangs on chains from a beam above the nearer
one. Racks and bins along the back wall are chalked with merchants'
marks, and bales of wool and rolled hides are stacked almost to the
rafters. A slate by the counter lists the day's prices in three
different scripts. The whole room smells of tallow, dust and sheep, and
the door east opens back onto Esh Road.

9754.name: Pasocaoa Boulevard

north.description: To the north lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

south.description: To the south lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

9754.description:
An arched gateway faces the boulevard here, its doors of dark wood
studded with brass bosses and framed in tiles glazed turquoise and
green. Through a grille set in one door you can glimpse a paved
courtyard and the glint of a small fountain, a cool private world hidden
from the street. The lindens throw a dappled shade across the paving,
which runs north and south.

9755.name: Pasocaoa Boulevard

north.description: To the north lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

south.description: To the south lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

west.description: To the west lies Rubble and Ruin.

9755.description:
The neat row of houses breaks off here, and to the west a gap opens
where one of them has fallen in, leaving a mound of rubble and charred
timbers grown over with weeds. Soot still streaks the walls of its
neighbours where they once leaned against it. The boulevard itself is
swept clean, and its lindens run on north and south as though nothing
were amiss.

9756.name: Pasocaoa Boulevard

north.description: To the north lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

south.description: To the south lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

9756.description:
A public well stands in the middle of the boulevard beneath a little
domed canopy on four stone pillars, its windlass worn bright where
countless hands have turned it. The flagstones around it are always
damp, and moss grows green in the cracks between them. A tin cup hangs
from a chain on one pillar for any thirsty passer-by. Lindens shade the
way as it runs north and south.

9757.name: Pasocaoa Boulevard

north.description: To the north lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

south.description: To the south lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

9757.description:
A bronze statue of a robed trader stands on a plinth beside the way, a
pair of scales in one hand and the other raised to shade his eyes, as
though he were watching for a caravan on the horizon. The weather has
turned him a mottled green, all but the toe of one sandal, which
passers-by rub bright for luck. The boulevard leads on north and south
beneath the lindens.

extra_descs.statue trader plinth bronze:
Letters cut into the plinth read PASOCAOA, WHO CAME WITH A MULE AND LEFT
A STREET. Beneath them, in chalk and a much newer hand, someone has
added AND A GREAT MANY DEBTS.

9758.name: Pasocaoa Boulevard

north.description: To the north lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

south.description: To the south lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

9758.description:
Strings of little brass bells hang from the balconies along this
stretch, and the slightest breeze sets them chiming softly over the
street. The houses here are quieter than those nearer the Trade Road,
their shutters painted a faded saffron and their doorsteps scrubbed
white. A sundial painted on one wall has lost its pointer, so that it
tells no hour at all. The boulevard goes on north and south.

9759.name: Pasocaoa Boulevard

north.description: To the north lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

south.description: To the south lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

west.description: To the west lies Sakifan's Library.

9759.description:
On the west side of the boulevard a narrow house of grey stone bears a
carved open book above its door, the sign of Sakifan's Library. A lamp
burns in an iron cage beside the entrance at every hour, and a brass
plate beneath it asks visitors to wipe their feet and lower their
voices. North and south the lindens stretch away along the busy street.

9760.name: Pasocaoa Boulevard

north.description: To the north lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

south.description: To the south lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

9760.description:
A warehouse with a steep tiled roof fronts the boulevard here, and
through its half-open doors drifts a heady smell of pepper, cloves and
cumin. Painted on the wall beside the doors, in letters taller than a
man, is a single word in a flowing foreign script that few in the street
can read. The lindens grow thinner along this stretch, and the boulevard
runs on north and south.

9761.name: Pasocaoa Boulevard

north.description: To the north lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

south.description: To the south lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

9761.description:
Three gilded balls hang from an iron bracket above a narrow and heavily
barred door, the old sign of a moneylender. The paving before it has
been patched with newer stones of a paler grey, where some overladen
cart must once have cracked the old ones. North the boulevard runs back
past the library, and south it continues beneath the lindens.

9762.name: Pasocaoa Boulevard

north.description: To the north lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

south.description: To the south lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

9762.description:
The steady knock of mallets comes from a cooper's yard behind a low wall
here, where half-finished barrels stand in rows waiting for their hoops.
Curls of oak shaving have blown out onto the paving and gather in drifts
against the kerb. The boulevard runs north toward the heart of the
quarter and south toward the place where it turns.

9763.name: Pasocaoa Boulevard

north.description: To the north lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

south.description: To the south lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

9763.description:
A stone watch box with a pointed roof stands at the edge of the paving
here, just big enough for one of the town watch to shelter from the
rain. Beside it a wooden board is plastered with notices, layer upon
layer, their edges curling in the damp. The lindens give out a little
further south, and north the boulevard runs back between its trees.

extra_descs.notices board notice:
Most of the notices offer rewards for strayed mules or call for masons
and carters. The newest, nailed over the rest, promises good silver to
anyone who will carry a letter to Townsbridge and asks no questions.
Across it someone has scrawled in charcoal: NOBODY LIVES THERE.

9764.name: Danozi Avenue

north.description: To the north lies Danozi Avenue.

south.description: To the south lies Danozi Avenue.

9764.description:
A warm, sweet smell of malt rolls down the avenue from the brewery just
to the north, thick enough to taste. Empty barrels are stacked three
high beneath an awning here, waiting for the brewer's dray to collect
them. The houses on this stretch have small gardens behind low walls,
where hops climb on strings up the fronts of the porches. Danozi Avenue
runs north and south.

9765.name: The Northern Gatehouse

north.description: To the north lies Road Through the Plains.

south.description: To the south lies Trade Road.

9765.description:
Two squat towers of grey stone flank the road here, joined above the
arch by a covered walk where the watch hangs its lanterns. The iron-
studded gates stand folded back against the walls, and letters cut into
the lintel have been worn almost smooth by the weather. Beyond the arch
the road runs north out of the town toward the open plains, passing the
gutted shell of a house by the wayside. South, the Trade Road leads back
among warehouses and shops toward the heart of Garathorm.

extra_descs.letters lintel inscription arch:
You can just make out the old carving: LET ALL WHO TRADE HONESTLY PASS
FREELY. Beneath it someone has scratched a tally of tolls, as if to
argue the point.

9766.name: Danozi Avenue

north.description: To the north lies Danozi Avenue.

south.description: To the south lies Danozi Avenue.

9766.description:
A broad hall with a steep roof of red tile stands back from the avenue
here, the meeting house of the craftsmen of the outer town. Above its
door a long carved panel shows the tools of every trade in the quarter,
from hammer and awl to mash paddle and jeweller's loupe. The avenue runs
north and south past its steps.

extra_descs.panel carving tools:
The carving is crowded but skilful: awl and adze, needle and mallet,
mash paddle, loupe and a dozen more, all bound together by a single
carved rope. At the rope's end a smaller and less skilful hand has added
a tiny tankard.

9767.name: Danozi Avenue

north.description: To the north lies Danozi Avenue.

south.description: To the south lies Danozi Avenue.

9767.description:
The roar of a furnace comes from a glassblower's workshop here, and its
window is crowded with bottles and beads in every colour, catching the
light like a handful of jewels. The wall beside its door is warm to the
touch even in winter. The avenue runs north toward the Jeweller's and
south past the craftsmen's hall.

9768.name: The Western Gatehouse

east.description: To the east lies Trade Road.

west.description: To the west lies A Road Through The Plains.

9768.description:
The Western Gatehouse is an old arch hung with ivy, flanked by two stout
towers with conical roofs of grey slate. Its gates of iron-bound oak are
folded back and wedged open with stones. West, beyond the arch, a dusty
road strikes out across the grassy plains toward the distant forest of
Haon-Dor, while east the Trade Road leads into the bustle of the town.

9769.name: Danozi Avenue

north.description: To the north lies Danozi Avenue.

south.description: To the south lies Danozi Avenue.

9769.description:
Between two leaning houses a narrow alley, too tight for a cart, gives a
glimpse of the town wall and a slice of green country beyond it. A rain
barrel stands at the alley's mouth, brimming over and skinned with
fallen leaves. Danozi Avenue runs north and south past the alley, shaded
by its chestnut trees.

9770.name: Danozi Avenue

north.description: To the north lies Danozi Avenue.

south.description: To the south lies Danozi Avenue.

9770.description:
A wooden boot as big as a barrel hangs over a cobbler's door here,
painted black and polished until it gleams. The cobbler's window is
crowded with wooden lasts carved in the shapes of feet, large and small.
The smell of leather grows stronger as the avenue runs north toward the
leatherworker's, and south it continues beneath the chestnuts.

9771.name: The Southern Gatehouse

north.description: To the north lies Trade Road.

east.description: To the east lies Stonewalk Way.

south.description: To the south lies Road Through The Plains.

west.description: To the west lies Stonewalk Way.

9771.description:
The Southern Gatehouse is a single blocky tower of rough grey stone,
pierced by an arch so deep that it stays cool and dim even at midday.
The vault of the arch is riddled with murder holes, long since stuffed
with old swallows' nests, and the oak gates are pinned back against the
walls with iron hooks. Through the arch the road runs south into open
grassland. Stonewalk Way branches east and west inside the town wall,
and north the Trade Road enters the customs hall.

9772.name: Danozi Avenue

north.description: To the north lies Danozi Avenue.

south.description: To the south lies Danozi Avenue.

9772.description:
The clack of looms sounds from the upper windows of the houses here, and
poles thrust out over the street hang with skeins of wool drying in
madder red and woad blue. Drips of dye have stained the paving below in
faded patches of colour. The avenue runs north and south between the
weavers' houses.

9773.name: Danozi Avenue

north.description: To the north lies Danozi Avenue.

south.description: To the south lies Danozi Avenue.

9773.description:
A bathhouse with a low dome of green copper stands here, wisps of steam
escaping from the vents around its rim. Over its door a painted panel
