shows a stout man up to his chin in a tub, looking deeply content with
the world. The paving around the door is always wet, and the avenue runs
north and south past it.

9774.name: Stonewalk Way

north.description: To the north lies Wrecked Shop.

east.description: To the east lies Stonewalk Way.

west.description: To the west lies Stonewalk Way.

9774.description:
A shop on the north side of the street stands wrecked, its shutters torn
from their hinges and its painted sign split in two, dangling by a
single chain. Glass from its window still glitters in the cracks of the
raised walk. The neighbouring houses keep their own shutters tightly
closed. Stonewalk Way runs east and west along the town wall.

9775.name: Danozi Avenue

north.description: To the north lies Trade Road.

south.description: To the south lies Danozi Avenue.

9775.description:
Danozi Avenue begins its long run south here, leaving the bustle of the
Trade Road just to the north. A tall corner house has a clock face
painted on its gable with the hands fixed forever at a quarter to noon,
and many a newcomer has been fooled into hurrying. The chestnut trees of
the avenue begin a few paces further on.

9776.name: Stonewalk Way

east.description: To the east lies Stonewalk Way.

west.description: To the west lies The Southern Gatehouse.

9776.description:
The outer wall of the town runs along one side of the street here, lower
and rougher than the great wall of the inner city, its stones patched
with brick wherever they have fallen. A wheelwright has leaned a row of
cartwheels against it in every stage of repair. West lies the Southern
Gatehouse, and east the raised stone walks carry on along the wall.

9777.name: Danozi Avenue

north.description: To the north lies Danozi Avenue.

east.description: To the east lies Leatherworker's Shop.

south.description: To the south lies Danozi Avenue.

9777.description:
Hides stretched on wooden frames lean against the front of the
Leatherworker's Shop, which opens on the east side of the avenue. A
saddle hangs over its door for a sign, cracked with age but still oiled
every spring. The sharp, sour smell of tanning hangs over this stretch
of Danozi Avenue, which runs on north and south.

9778.name: Pasocaoa Boulevard

north.description: To the north lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

south.description: To the south lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

9778.description:
Tall merchant houses stand back behind the lindens here, their upper
floors screened by balconies of carved wooden lattice so fine that it
looks like lace. A long stone trough runs beside the paving, filled by a
thin stream of water from the mouth of a bronze fish. The boulevard
continues north toward the Trade Road and south beneath the trees, and
the trickle of the spout follows you a long way along it.

9779.name: Pasocaoa Boulevard

north.description: To the north lies Trade Road.

south.description: To the south lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

9779.description:
Pasocaoa Boulevard opens here off the Trade Road, which crosses just to
the north in a ceaseless rumble of wheels and hooves. Two slender
pillars of blue-glazed brick mark the head of the boulevard, each
crowned with a brass lamp shaped like an onion dome. Beyond them a
double row of linden trees marches away south, shading a broad way paved
with pale stone. The air smells of horses and, very faintly, of
cinnamon.

9780.name: Trade Road

north.description: To the north lies Trade Road.

south.description: To the south lies The Southern Gatehouse.

9780.description:
The Trade Road runs here through the town's customs hall, a long vaulted
chamber of brick open at both ends so that carts can roll straight
through. A great weighing platform is set into the floor, its iron beam
and counterweights hanging from the vault above. Behind a grille in one
wall the clerks' desks stand heaped with ledgers, and lamps burn on
chains at every hour. The way runs north toward the inner city and south
to the Southern Gatehouse.

9781.name: Trade Road

north.description: To the north lies The Northern Gatehouse.

south.description: To the south lies Trade Road.

9781.description:
Warehouses with wide double doors line this stretch of the Trade Road,
their loading beams and hoist ropes jutting out over the street. The
cobbles are stained dark with spilled oil and wine from years of
unloading, and the air smells of tar, pepper and horses. To the north
the squat towers of the Northern Gatehouse rise above the rooftops,
while the road runs south toward the gate of the inner city.

9782.name: Danozi Avenue

north.description: To the north lies Danozi Avenue.

south.description: To the south lies Danozi Avenue.

9782.description:
Children have chalked a hopping game across the paving here, its squares
numbered in a wobbly hand, and drawings of horses and dragons run along
the foot of the walls. The houses on this stretch are homes rather than
shops, with pots of herbs crowding every sill. The avenue runs on north
beneath the chestnuts and back south toward the Ship Shop.

15070.name: The Eastern Gatehouse

north.description: To the north lies The Main Gate to the Carnival.

east.description: You can see the dirt road through the doorway to the east.

south.description: To the south lies Entrance to the Academy.

west.description: To the west lies Trade Road.

15070.description:
The vaulted passage of the Eastern Gatehouse runs through the thickness
of the outer wall, lit by lanterns in iron cages and cold even on the
warmest day. Great oak gates stand open at either end, west to the Trade
Road and east to the road across the plains. Two lesser doors in the
side walls are barred with heavy timbers: the north one is painted with
faded stars and tumbling clowns, and the south one bears the worn crest
of an academy. The flagstones are rutted deep by cartwheels.

9788.name: Pasocaoa Boulevard

north.description: To the north lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

south.description: To the south lies Pasocaoa Boulevard.

9788.description:
Stone benches stand in the shade of the lindens here, their seats worn
into shallow hollows by years of idle sitting. The paving between them
is laid in a pattern of interlocking eight-pointed stars, red stone set
into grey, a fashion the founders of this quarter brought with them from
far away. Over the rooftops the battlements of Garathorm's inner wall
show against the sky. The boulevard runs on north and south.

9789.name: Shokogya Street

east.description: To the east lies Shokogya Street.

west.description: To the west lies Shokogya Street.

9789.description:
The houses along this stretch have roofs of glazed green tile with
upturned eaves, and every ridge ends in a carved and painted dragon's
head, open-mouthed to frighten off ill luck. Fewer awnings are stretched
across the street here, and more daylight reaches the paving. The way
runs east and west, with the grey bulk of the inner wall rising behind
the rooftops.

9790.name: Shokogya Street

east.description: To the east lies Shokogya Street.

west.description: To the west lies Shokogya Street.

9790.description:
A gap between two houses has been made into a tiny garden, no bigger
than a room, where a gnarled pine leans over a pool and a stone lantern
stands among raked white gravel. A low bamboo fence keeps the street
out. Shokogya Street runs east and west past this small patch of calm.

9791.name: Shokogya Street

north.description: To the north lies A private home.

east.description: To the east lies Shokogya Street.

west.description: To the west lies Shokogya Street.

9791.description:
A modest house with a blue-painted door faces the street on the north
side, its step lined with pots of marigolds and its brass knocker shaped
like a small closed hand. Unlike the shops along the street it hangs out
no sign, only a little carved charm nailed above the lintel for luck.
The street runs on east and west beneath its awnings.

9792.name: Shokogya Street

east.description: To the east lies Trade Road.

west.description: To the west lies Shokogya Street.

9792.description:
A painted wooden arch spans the mouth of Shokogya Street here, its
crossbeam lettered with the street's name in two scripts. Beneath it the
striped awnings begin, and east the street opens onto the Trade Road,
where carts rumble past toward the gate of the inner city. West,
Shokogya Street wanders off among its tiled roofs and lanterns.

extra_descs.arch crossbeam lettering:
The lower line plainly reads SHOKOGYA STREET. The upper line is written
in a looping, hooked script that the old traders still use among
themselves, and they will tell you, if asked, that it means something
closer to the street where nobody goes hungry.

9793.name: Esh Road

east.description: To the east lies Esh Road.

west.description: To the west lies Trade Road.

9793.description:
Esh Road begins here, branching off the Trade Road past a row of solid
counting-houses whose iron-bound doors and barred windows speak of the
money kept inside. Brass plates beside each door bear the names of
merchant houses in several scripts. West, the Trade Road bustles in the
shadow of the inner city's wall. Esh Road runs east toward a street of
tall houses and swaying lanterns.

9794.name: Esh Road

north.description: To the north lies A private home.

east.description: To the east lies Esh Road.

west.description: To the west lies Esh Road.

9794.description:
A tall, narrow house with a carved balcony stands on the north side of
the street here, its door painted with a pair of golden fish swimming in
a circle. Wind chimes of thin brass hang from its eaves and ring softly
in every breeze. Esh Road leads east toward a public well and west
toward the Trade Road. Lanterns on tall poles line the street.

9795.name: Esh Road

east.description: To the east lies Esh Road.

west.description: To the west lies Esh Road.

9795.description:
A public well stands in a small square here, its stone curb worn hollow
by ropes and its pulley sheltered under a little tiled roof with
upturned eaves. Benches around it make a meeting place for the
neighbourhood. Esh Road runs east toward a house with a green door and
west past more tall houses. Children have chalked games of hops and
squares on the cobbles around the well.

9796.name: Esh Road

east.description: To the east lies Esh Road.

south.description: To the south lies A private home.

west.description: To the west lies Esh Road.

9796.description:
A neat house with a green-painted door and a little courtyard garden
stands on the south side of the street here, its gate hung with a small
brass bell. Pots of herbs and bright flowers line its windowsills. Esh
Road runs east to a corner shrine and west along a row of tall houses.
The street is quieter here, away from the warehouses, and swept clean
every morning.

9797.name: Esh Road

south.description: To the south lies Esh Road.

west.description: To the west lies Esh Road.

9797.description:
Esh Road turns a corner here, and in the angle of the wall stands a
small shrine: a niche holding a squat bronze figure with a round belly
and a contented smile. Offerings of rice and marigolds are heaped at his
feet, and his belly has been rubbed bright by passing hands. The road
leads south toward the little shops and west between tall, quiet houses.
A smell of incense lingers about the niche.

extra_descs.shrine figure bronze niche:
The bronze figure is a god of trade and good fortune to the merchants
who built these streets, and it is thought lucky to rub his belly before
striking a bargain. A small brass plate beneath him reads HONEST WEIGHT,
HONEST WORD.

9798.name: Esh Road

north.description: To the north lies Esh Road.

south.description: To the south lies Esh Road.

9798.description:
Little shops crowd both sides of the street here, none wider than a
doorway: a moneychanger's booth with a barred window, a seller of inks
and fine paper, a maker of brass lamps whose wares hang glinting in
clusters from the eaves. Strings of paper lanterns are slung across the
street from balcony to balcony. Esh Road runs north to a corner and
south toward the trading post.

9799.name: Esh Road

north.description: To the north lies Esh Road.

south.description: To the south lies Esh Road.

west.description: To the west lies Trading Post.

9799.description:
A broad doorway in a building of honey-coloured stone opens west into
the Trading Post, its lintel carved with a pair of scales, a camel and a
ship under sail. Iron hitching rails line the street outside, polished
by countless reins. Esh Road continues north past a row of tiny
shopfronts and south toward the spice warehouses. The cobbles here are
worn smooth by the passage of handcarts.

15001.name: On The King's Road
15001.description:
The area opens in the center of the great King's Road. The road is very
well built, and goes in a straight line due east-west. Vendors and
pedestrians bustle past. The smell of smoke and humanity hangs in the
air.

east.description: The King's Road continues in a straight line to the east.

west.description: You see that the King's Road continues westwards towards a large city.

15002.name: On The King's Road
15002.description:
The area opens on the King's Road, which leads east and west. The skill
of the builders is apparent, since it is impossible to notice any turn
or irregularity in the road. The sounds of city life echo around. The
smell of smoke and humanity hangs in the air.

east.description: You see a castle in the far east.

west.description: The King's Road continues in a straight line to the west.

15003.name: On The King's Road Outside The Castle
15003.description:
This area is the King's Road. before is a large Castle, evidently built
not so much for strength as for beauty. It is not totally without
defences, though, for it is surrounded by a deep moat, and its windows
are just narrow slits for archers to shoot through. To the north there
is a drawbridge across the moat. Buildings crowd together on all sides.
Vendors and pedestrians bustle past.

north.description: You see the drawbridge.

east.description: To the east lies On The King's Road.

south.description: To the south lies The Stable Entrance.

west.description: The King's Road continues in a straight line to the west.

19705.name: The Outskirts Of The Woods

north.description: To the north lies The Outskirts Of The Woods.

east.description: To the east lies On The Caravan Road.

19705.description:
Young trees grow thick here at the edge of the woods, hazel and birch
and holly, with bracken waist-high between them. Old stumps show where
woodcutters once worked, though their axe marks are grey with age. The
ground is soft with leaf litter and crossed by the slots of deer. A
trail leads north into the deepening trees, and east the rutted end of
the Caravan Road opens onto daylight.

19706.name: The Outskirts Of The Woods

north.description: To the north lies A Trail Through The Thick Woods.

south.description: To the south lies The Outskirts Of The Woods.

19706.description:
The trees grow taller and closer together here, and the bracken gives
way to bramble and moss. A woodcutter's shelter of lashed poles stands
collapsed beside the trail, its roof of branches long since fallen in.
Somewhere water drips steadily from the leaves. The trail continues
north into thicker woods where the shadows deepen, and runs south toward
the edge of the forest.

19708.name: An Overgrown Path

east.description: To the east lies A Trail Through The Thick Woods.

west.description: To the west lies An Overgrown Path.

19708.description:
An overgrown path pushes through brambles and nettles here, so choked
that it is hard to believe anyone has walked it in years. Thorny
tendrils catch at clothing, and the trees lean close overhead. Here and
there a cut stem shows that someone has hacked a way through, not long
ago. The path struggles on west, and east it leads back to the hollow
oak on the woodland trail.

19709.name: An Overgrown Path

north.description: To the north lies An Overgrown Path.

east.description: To the east lies An Overgrown Path.

19709.description:
The path turns north here beside the ruin of a low stone wall, half
swallowed by ivy and moss. It may once have been a sheepfold or the
corner of a cottage, but the woods reclaimed it long ago. A spindly
rowan grows out of the middle of the ruin, hung with bright berries.
East, the path pushes back through the brambles toward the main trail.

19710.name: An Overgrown Path

south.description: To the south lies An Overgrown Path.

19710.description:
The overgrown path ends in a tiny glade where a ring of pale toadstools
grows in the grass. Wild garlic scents the air, and a single thread of
sunlight falls through a gap in the leaves to light the ring. The
brambles close in on every side but one, and the only way out is south,
back past the ruined wall.

extra_descs.toadstools ring glade:
The toadstools form an almost perfect circle, and the grass inside it is
greener and softer than the grass without. Country folk say it is
unlucky to step inside such a ring, and luckier still to step out again.

19713.name: A Trail Through The Thick Woods

east.description: To the east lies A Trail Through The Thick Woods.

south.description: To the south lies The Outskirts Of The Woods.

west.description: To the west lies An Overgrown Path.

19713.description:
Oak and hornbeam grow thickly here, their branches knotted together into
a roof that lets through only a dim green light. The trail forks at an
old oak with a hollow trunk large enough to shelter in. One way runs
east along the foot of a steep bank, while to the west an overgrown path
wanders off among the brambles. The trail also leads back south toward
the outskirts of the woods.

19714.name: A Trail Through The Thick Woods

west.description: To the west lies A Trail Through The Thick Woods.

up.description: To the up lies A Trail Through The Thick Woods.

19714.description:
The trail ends at the foot of a steep bank, where the roots of the trees
have broken through the earth like the rungs of a ladder. Using them,
you could climb up the slope to the higher ground above. The air here is
damp and still, and toadstools grow in clusters on the fallen logs.
West, the trail returns to the hollow oak.

19715.name: A Trail Through The Thick Woods

north.description: To the north lies A Dark Trail Through The Dense Woods.

down.description: To the down lies A Trail Through The Thick Woods.

19715.description:
From the top of the bank the trail runs on through close-set trees,
their trunks pale with lichen. Behind, a scramble of roots leads down
the slope to the lower trail. North, the path plunges into darker woods
where the trees grow denser and the light fails. A cold breath of air
comes from that way, smelling of pine and wet earth.

19722.name: A Dark Trail Through The Dense Woods

south.description: To the south lies A Trail Through The Thick Woods.

west.description: To the west lies A Dark Trail Through The Dense Woods.

19722.description:
The dense woods close in here, firs and old yews growing so close that
their branches interlace over the trail. Little light reaches the
ground, which is bare and brown with fallen needles. The trail turns
west deeper into the gloom, and runs back south toward the top of the
bank. There is no sound but the slow creak of branches overhead.

19723.name: A Dark Trail Through The Dense Woods

east.description: To the east lies A Dark Trail Through The Dense Woods.

west.description: To the west lies A Dark Trail Through The Dense Woods.

19723.description:
A fallen fir lies across the trail here, and the path ducks beneath its
trunk where feet have worn the earth into a hollow. Long beards of grey
moss hang from the branches, stirring in a draught you cannot feel. The
darkness makes it hard to judge how far anything is. The trail continues
west and back east through the dense trees.

19724.name: A Dark Trail Through The Dense Woods

north.description: To the north lies A Trail Through The Black Woods.

east.description: To the east lies A Dark Trail Through The Dense Woods.

19724.description:
The trail bends here at the edge of a small, sunless hollow where water
has gathered in a black pool. Strange pale fungi crowd the roots around
its rim, glowing faintly in the gloom. North, the trees grow blacker
still, their bark dark as soot: the beginning of the Black Woods. East,
the trail leads back beneath the fallen fir.

19738.name: A Trail Through The Black Woods

south.description: To the south lies A Dark Trail Through The Dense Woods.

up.description: To the up lies A Trail Through The Black Woods.

19738.description:
The trees of the Black Woods rise like charred pillars here, their bark
black and furrowed and their crowns lost in darkness. The trail stops at
the foot of a rocky step, where a cleft in the stone offers footholds to
climb up to the higher ground. The air is heavy and smells of rot.
South, the trail leads back to the hollow with its black pool.

19739.name: A Trail Through The Black Woods

east.description: To the east lies A Trail Through The Black Woods.

down.description: To the down lies A Trail Through The Black Woods.

19739.description:
Above the rocky step the trail runs along a spine of bare stone, where
the black trees grip the rock with roots like clutching fingers. The
canopy is so thick that it is hard to tell whether it is day or night. A
cleft in the rock leads back down to the lower trail, and the path winds
on east between the trunks. Old claw marks score the bark of the nearest
tree at the height of a tall man.

19740.name: A Trail Through The Black Woods

east.description: To the east lies A Bend In The Trail.

west.description: To the west lies A Trail Through The Black Woods.

19740.description:
The trail runs level here through a stand of ancient black oaks, their
trunks so broad that three people could not link arms around one.
Mistletoe hangs in pale clumps from the high branches, and the ground is
spongy with centuries of rotted leaves. Somewhere far off a branch
cracks, and the sound echoes for a long time. The way continues east
toward a bend and back west to the spine of stone.

19741.name: A Trail Through The Black Woods

north.description: To the north lies A Large Clearing Near The Cliff.

south.description: To the south lies A Bend In The Trail.

19741.description:
The black trees thin a little here, and a grey light filters down
through gaps in the canopy. The trail climbs over a tangle of exposed
roots, slick with moisture, and grey rock begins to break through the
soil. North, the trees open onto a wide clearing, and the roar of
falling water grows louder from that way. South, the trail returns to
the boulder at the bend.

19742.name: A Large Clearing Near The Cliff

east.description: To the east lies Before The Great Northern Bridge.

south.description: To the south lies A Trail Through The Black Woods.

19742.description:
The Black Woods end abruptly at a wide clearing of coarse grass and
scattered stones, open to a sky the colour of slate. A short way off the
ground stops at the lip of a sheer cliff, and a river thunders unseen in
the gorge far below. The blackened rings of old campfires mark the
grass, and a path leads east along the cliff top toward the head of a
great bridge. South, the trail returns into the dark trees.

19743.name: Before The Great Northern Bridge

north.description: To the north lies On The Great Northern bridge.

west.description: To the west lies A Large Clearing Near The Cliff.

19743.description:
Two massive stone pillars, carved with the worn shapes of kings or gods,
guard the head of a great bridge that leaps out across the gorge. The
bridge runs north over the abyss toward the badlands beyond, its
parapets broken in many places. Wind howls out of the chasm, carrying a
fine spray from the river. West, a path leads back along the cliff top
to the clearing.

extra_descs.pillars carvings figures:
The figures on the pillars are so weathered that their faces are gone,
but one holds a key and the other a sword. Between them, on the first
stone of the bridge, someone has cut a deep line across the paving.

19744.name: On The Great Northern bridge

north.description: To the north lies At The Far End Of The Sundered Bridge.

south.description: To the south lies Before The Great Northern Bridge.

19744.description:
The great bridge spans the gorge on a single soaring arch of grey stone
under a wide, cold sky, and the river roars white through the chasm far
beneath your feet. Midway across, the span is split by a jagged crack,
crossed by heavy timbers lashed together, and the whole structure seems
to tremble in the wind. North lies the far end of the sundered bridge
and the broken lands beyond. South, the carved pillars mark the way back
into the Black Woods.

19748.name: A Bend In The Trail

north.description: To the north lies A Trail Through The Black Woods.

west.description: To the west lies A Trail Through The Black Woods.

19748.description:
The trail turns sharply here around a huge boulder furred with black
moss and half buried in the forest floor. Someone has scratched a crude
arrow on its face pointing the way north, and beneath it a second mark
like a skull. A thin, cold wind blows from that direction, carrying the
sound of rushing water far below. West, the trail runs back among the
old oaks.

extra_descs.boulder marks arrow skull:
The arrow is old and weathered, but the skull beside it looks recent,
scratched deep with the point of a knife. Outlaws use such marks to warn
one another, or to mark the ground they claim.

640800.name: hare field brown
640800.long_desc: A brown field hare sits up in the grass, its long ears turning at every sound.
640800.description:
A long-legged hare with a coat of brindled brown and a pale belly, its
black-tipped ears never still. It sits up on its haunches to watch you
with one wide amber eye, ready to bolt across the open ground at the
first wrong move.

640801.name: boar wild pig tusker
640801.long_desc: A bristly wild boar roots in the earth here, grunting to itself.
640801.description:
A heavy-shouldered boar with a coat of coarse grey-black bristles and a
stiff crest along its spine. Yellowed tusks curl up from its lower jaw,
caked with earth from rooting, and its small eyes regard you with surly
suspicion. It will leave you alone if you leave it alone.

640802.name: wolf grey lean
640802.long_desc: A lean grey wolf slinks between the trees, watching you with pale, hungry eyes.
640802.description:
The wolf is rangy and long in the leg, its grey coat darkening to black
along the spine and torn in places by old fights. It carries its head
low, lips drawn back from yellow fangs, and its pale eyes never leave
you. Where there is one, there are usually others.

640803.name: highwayman bandit robber masked
640803.long_desc: A masked highwayman steps out to bar the road, one hand resting on his sword.
640803.description:
A wiry man in a patched riding coat and a broad-brimmed hat, with a
strip of black cloth tied across his face below the eyes. His boots are
better than his coat, his short sword is notched from use, and he looks
you over the way a moneylender weighs a purse.

640804.name: wolf dire black huge
640804.long_desc: A black dire wolf pads out of the gloom, its hackles raised and its jaws dripping.
640804.description:
This wolf is as big as a pony, with a shaggy black coat, a heavy ruff
about its neck and jaws that could close around a man's thigh. Old scars
seam its muzzle, and its eyes burn a dull yellow in the gloom. It moves
with the unhurried confidence of something that has never lost a fight.

640805.name: outlaw captain bandit scarred
640805.long_desc: A scarred outlaw captain stands here, coolly sizing you up for ransom.
640805.description:
A tall, hard-faced man with a scar running from brow to jaw, wearing a
battered steel cap and a ranger's green cloak that was surely never his.
He carries himself like an old soldier, and the outlaws of the deep
woods take his orders without question. His sword hand never strays far
from the hilt.

640806.name: merchant trader travelling
640806.long_desc: A travelling merchant pauses here to shift the heavy pack on his back.
640806.description:
A stout, sunburned man in a dusty coat with a great many pockets, a
heavy pack of wares strapped to his back. He has the easy smile of
someone who has walked every road between Garathorm and the hills, and a
story for each mile of them.

640807.name: stag white hart deer
640807.long_desc: A white stag stands among the golden trees, watching you with calm dark eyes.
640807.description:
A tall stag with a coat as white as new snow and antlers that shine
faintly gold where the light catches them. He holds his head high and
still, and seems less afraid of you than curious. The foresters say it
is ill luck to harm him.

640808.name: bear brown
640808.long_desc: A big brown bear shambles through the undergrowth, sniffing the air.
640808.description:
A heavy brown bear, its shaggy coat flecked with burrs and bracken, with
a hump of muscle across its shoulders and claws as long as fingers. Its
small eyes are short-sighted but its nose misses nothing, and it does
not like to be disturbed at its foraging.

640809.name: spider giant web black
640809.long_desc: A giant web spider hangs head-down among the branches, its many eyes glittering.
640809.description:
A spider the size of a small pony, with a bloated black body patterned
in faint grey bands and legs furred with bristles. Its cluster of eyes
gleams like wet beads, and its fangs drip a thin, clear venom. Strands
of fresh silk trail behind it wherever it goes.

640810.name: troll bog marsh
640810.long_desc: A hulking bog troll squats in the mire, picking its teeth with a splinter of bone.
640810.description:
A stooped, long-armed brute twice the height of a man, its warty grey-
green hide caked with peat and hung with strands of marsh weed. Its nose
is long and drooping, its eyes small and red, and it smells powerfully
of stagnant water. It carries a knotted club of black bog oak.

640811.name: robber tomb thief man
640811.long_desc: A tomb robber crouches among the ruins, prying at a loose stone with a crowbar.
640811.description:
A lean, grimy man in a dark hooded coat with many pockets, a coil of
rope over one shoulder and a shuttered lantern at his belt. His
fingernails are black with grave dirt, and his eyes keep straying to the
sealed temple at the heart of the ruins. He does not mean to share
whatever he finds.

640812.name: wraith shadow ghost
640812.long_desc: A shadow wraith drifts between the black trees, cold and silent.
640812.description:
A tall shape of darkness in the rough form of a cloaked man, its edges
fraying into the gloom like smoke. Where its face should be there is
only a deeper shadow and two pinpricks of pale light. The air around it
is bitterly cold, and frost forms on the leaves where it passes.

640813.name: watchman guard villager man
640813.long_desc: A village watchman walks his round, a lantern in one hand and a braid of garlic at his belt.
640813.description:
A sturdy, grey-whiskered villager in a padded jerkin, carrying a stout
ash staff and an unlit lantern. A braid of garlic and a little tin sun
hang from his belt, and he keeps glancing at the sky to judge how long
is left until dusk. He nods to travellers, but he does not linger on the
road.

640814.name: stag deer golden hart
640814.long_desc: A golden stag stands among the trees, light gathering in the tines of its antlers.
640814.description:
The stag's coat is the warm colour of the forest's leaves, and its
antlers branch wide and high with a faint gilt sheen along every tine.
It holds its head proudly and watches you with large dark eyes, more
curious than afraid. The elves are said to count the killing of one of
these beasts a grave offence.

640815.name: spider giant black hairy
640815.long_desc: A giant black spider waits in a sagging web strung across the edge of the light.
640815.description:
Its body is as large as a hound's, covered in coarse black hair, and its
eight long legs are banded with dull red. A cluster of glassy eyes
catches the golden light as it shifts its weight on the web. These
spiders creep out of the Old Forest to hunt along its border, though
they never venture far into the radiant wood.

640816.name: horse wild dun mare
640816.long_desc: A dun wild horse grazes in the long grass, swishing its black tail at the flies.
640816.description:
A sturdy, short-legged horse with a dun coat, a black mane that has
never known a comb and a dark stripe along its spine. It lifts its head
to watch you, ears pricked, ready to wheel away across the meadow with
the rest of its herd. The horses of the Thrithing have run wild here for
longer than anyone remembers.

640817.name: bear brown shaggy
640817.long_desc: A shaggy brown bear rears up against a birch, raking the white bark with its claws.
640817.description:
A huge brown bear with a hump of muscle across its shoulders and a coat
ragged with burrs and twigs. Its muzzle is sticky with honey from some
raided hive, and its small eyes regard you with short-tempered
suspicion. Risen on its hind legs, it stands taller than any man.

640818.name: poacher hunter bandit furtive
640818.long_desc: A furtive poacher crouches over a snare in the undergrowth, skinning knife in hand.
640818.description:
A lean, hollow-cheeked man in a patched jerkin of greasy leather, with a
game bag slung across his back and a coil of snare wire at his belt. He
has the darting eyes of someone who knows the rangers are never far
away, and he will fight like a cornered weasel rather than be taken.
Feathers and tufts of fur cling to his sleeves.

640819.name: wraith ghost ash grey
640819.long_desc: An ash-grey wraith drifts through the ruins, trailing a thin smell of old smoke.
640819.description:
It has the shape of a villager wrapped in a long, tattered shroud, but
the whole of it is made of drifting ash and smoke that never quite
settles. Where its face should be there are only two embers, dull red
and full of grief and hatred. It is one of the dead of Townsbridge, who
perished when the village burned and cannot rest.

640820.name: ranger hunter woman woodsman
640820.short_desc: a ranger of the Long Lake
640820.long_desc: A ranger of the Long Lake keeps watch here, leaning on an unstrung longbow.
640820.description:
A weathered woman in mottled green and brown, with a quiver at her hip
and a silver leaf pinned at the throat of her cloak. Her face is brown
and lined from years of wind and weather, and her grey eyes miss nothing
that moves in the grass. The rangers keep the meadow and the woods
around the Long Lake safe, and ask little in return.

640821.name: watchman guard watch
640821.short_desc: a watchman of the outer town
640821.long_desc: A watchman of the outer town strolls by, his lantern pole resting on one shoulder.
640821.description:
A thickset, good-humoured man in a quilted coat dyed the blue of the
town watch, with a short club at his belt and a lantern on a pole for
the night rounds. He knows every merchant on the street by name, and
most of their debts as well. His boots are worn down at the heels from
years of walking the same cobbles.

640822.name: lamplighter old man
640822.long_desc: An old lamplighter shuffles along beneath the lantern hooks, a long brass-tipped pole over his shoulder.
640822.description:
A stooped old man in a soot-streaked coat, with a long pole for reaching
the street lamps balanced over one shoulder and a hooded brass lantern
swinging from his belt. He seems to know every lamp in the outer town by
name and murmurs to each one as he passes. His fingers are black with
lamp oil, and his eyes are mild and kind.

640823.name: hound dog feral wild
640823.long_desc: A feral hound slinks through the grass, ribs showing and lips curled back from yellow teeth.
640823.description:
Once this was somebody's dog, a big rough-coated farm hound with a
brindled hide and a worn leather collar still buckled about its neck.
Years of running wild since its village emptied have made it gaunt and
savage. It watches you with the flat, measuring stare of a beast that
has learned to hunt in a pack.

640824.name: ghoul gaunt corpse undead
640824.long_desc: A gaunt ghoul crouches low here, gnawing at something it will not let you see.
640824.description:
It may once have been a man of Townsbridge, but its grey skin has shrunk
tight over its bones and its nails have grown into thick, filthy claws.
Its eyes are white and filmed, yet it turns unerringly toward the warmth
of the living. The rags of a farmer's smock still hang from its
shoulders, stiff with earth from the grave pit.

640825.name: aurochs bull wild ox
640825.long_desc: A shaggy aurochs bull grazes in the tall grass, lifting its great horned head to watch you.
640825.description:
The aurochs stands taller at the shoulder than a man, a mountain of
muscle under a coat of dark brown hair with a pale stripe running down
its spine. Its horns sweep forward and up in two pale curves, sharp
enough to toss a horse. It is no hunter, but it will not suffer anyone
to come too close.

640826.name: ogre wandering brute giant
640826.long_desc: A wandering ogre lumbers through the grass, dragging a club made from a cart axle behind it.
640826.description:
The ogre stands half again as tall as a man, with a slab of a face, a
jutting underbite and a belly sagging over a belt of knotted rope. It is
draped in a patchwork of travellers' cloaks crudely stitched together,
and a string of mismatched boots hangs about its neck, trophies of those
who lost their way on the plains. It sniffs the wind constantly, like a
hound casting for a scent.

640827.name: wraith ghost warden grey spectre
640827.long_desc: A grey wraith in the shape of a helmeted warden drifts along the old road, one hand held out as if demanding a toll.
640827.description:
Through its tattered grey substance you can see the paving behind it,
yet its shape is clear enough: a soldier in a crested helm and a long
cloak, a spear in one hand and the other held out palm upward. Its face
is a pale smudge with two cold points of light for eyes. Wardens kept
this highway long ago, and it seems that some of them never left their
posts.

740800.name: sword short notched highwayman
740800.room_desc: A short sword with a notched but well-honed edge lies here.
740800.description: A plain, sturdy short sword with a grip of leather gone dark with sweat. The edge is notched in several places but honed bright between the nicks, and a pair of crossed keys has been scratched into the crossguard.

740801.name: pelt wolf fur hide
740801.room_desc: A thick wolf pelt lies here, rolled up with the fur turned inward.
740801.description: A wolf's pelt, roughly skinned and rolled with the fur inward to keep it clean. The fur is dense and coarse, grey shading to black along the back, and any furrier in Hommlet or Garathorm would pay well for it.

740802.name: charm waymark pebble cord amulet
740802.room_desc: A small carved pebble on a leather cord lies here.
740802.description: A smooth grey pebble carved into the shape of a tiny milestone and threaded on a leather cord. Travellers wear such charms to keep from losing their way, and this one is polished by much anxious rubbing.

740803.name: cloak ranger green hooded
740803.room_desc: A hooded green cloak, stained by weather and travel, lies here in a heap.
740803.description: A long hooded cloak of tightly woven wool, dyed in the mottled greens and browns of forest shade. It sheds rain like a duck's back, and a small silver leaf pinned at the throat marks it as the gear of the rangers who keep watch by the Long Lake.

740804.name: rations trail food packet oilcloth
740804.room_desc: A small oilcloth packet of trail rations lies here.
740804.description: Hard biscuit, a twist of salted meat and a handful of dried apple rings, wrapped tight in oilcloth and tied with string. It is no feast, but it will keep a traveller walking for another day.

740805.name: antler white stag tine
740805.room_desc: A pale antler, faintly gleaming gold at its tips, lies here.
740805.description: A long, many-tined antler, smooth and creamy white, its tips touched with a faint golden sheen. Carvers in Garathorm prize such antlers for knife hilts, though the foresters of the Radiant Forest would ask hard questions about how you came by it.

740806.name: silk skein spider web
740806.short_desc: a skein of giant spider silk
740806.room_desc: A skein of grey, gleaming spider silk lies here.
740806.description: A tangled skein of silk from a giant spider, grey and gleaming and stronger than any rope of the same thickness. Weavers and bowyers will pay well for it, once the last of the sticky coating has been boiled away.

740807.name: club bog oak knotted troll
740807.room_desc: A heavy club of black bog oak lies here, crusted with peat.
740807.description: A great club cut from bog oak that lay for centuries in the marsh, its wood turned black and hard as iron. The head is a mass of knots, and the grip has been worn smooth by a hand much larger than yours.

740808.name: lantern shuttered hooded robber
740808.room_desc: A small lantern with sliding iron shutters lies here.
740808.description: A small brass lantern fitted with sliding iron shutters, so that its light can be narrowed to a thin beam or hidden altogether at the sound of footsteps. Its glass is smoked from long use in dark places.

740809.name: ring band black iron wraith
740809.short_desc: a cold band of black iron
740809.room_desc: A plain ring of black iron lies here, rimed with frost.
740809.description: A plain band of black iron, so cold that it mists the air around it, though it seems to drink in the warmth of the hand that wears it and give back a strange vigour. Tiny letters inside the band have been worn away to nothing.

740810.name: antler stag gilded golden
740810.room_desc: A stag's antler with a faint golden sheen lies here.
740810.description: A long, many-tined antler from one of the stags of the Radiant Forest. Its surface has a faint golden sheen that catches the light like old gilt, and carvers in Garathorm pay well for such antlers to make handles and charms.

740811.name: silk skein spider web glimmering
740811.short_desc: a skein of glimmering spider silk
740811.room_desc: A skein of grey spider silk lies here, glimmering faintly.
740811.description: A loose skein of spider silk wound around a twig, still a little sticky at one end. Where it has hung in the light of the Radiant Forest it has taken on a faint golden glimmer, and weavers prize it for the finest thread.

740812.name: knife skinning poacher hooked
740812.room_desc: A short skinning knife with a hooked tip lies here.
740812.description: A short, heavy-backed knife with a hooked tip for opening hides, its bone handle wrapped in strips of rabbit skin. The blade has been sharpened so often that it has worn thin and wickedly keen.

740813.name: locket silver tarnished townsbridge
740813.room_desc: A tarnished silver locket on a thin chain lies here.
740813.description: A small silver locket, black with tarnish and warped by heat, on a chain mended with a twist of wire. Inside is a tiny painted portrait of a smiling family, and TOWNSBRIDGE is engraved on the back in careful letters. It is always cold to the touch.

740814.name: honeycomb honey comb wild
740814.room_desc: A broken slab of wild honeycomb lies here, oozing gold.
740814.description: A ragged slab of honeycomb torn from a wild hive in some hollow birch, heavy and dripping with dark honey. It is sticky, sweet and very filling.

740815.name: lantern hooded brass
740815.room_desc: A hooded brass lantern sits here, its little door latched shut.
740815.description: A sturdy lantern of soot-darkened brass with a hinged hood that can be lowered to hide its light, and a ring on top for hanging from a pole or a belt. The glass is thick and faintly green, and the wick has been trimmed with care.

740816.name: collar dog studded leather brass
740816.room_desc: A worn leather dog collar studded with brass lies here.
740816.description: A broad collar of thick leather, cracked with age and studded with little brass bosses. A small plate riveted to it is stamped with the name of a village, TOWNSBRIDGE, though the dog's own name has long since worn away. A collector of curios might pay a few coins for it.

740817.name: locket silver tarnished chain
740817.room_desc: A tarnished silver locket on a fine chain lies here.
740817.description: A small oval locket of silver gone black with tarnish, hung on a fine chain. Inside is a curl of fair hair tied with red thread, and the lid is engraved with two sets of initials joined by a heart. Wearing it brings an odd, quiet steadiness, as though someone were glad to see it carried into the light again.

740818.name: club axle cart heavy
740818.short_desc: a club made from a cart axle
740818.room_desc: A massive club made from a broken cart axle lies here.
740818.description: Someone strong beyond reason has snapped the axle from a heavy wagon and wrapped one end in rawhide for a grip, leaving the iron hub on the other end as a striking head. It is crude, ungainly and brutally effective.

740819.name: ring signet bronze warden
740819.room_desc: A heavy signet ring of greenish bronze lies here.
740819.description: A heavy ring of bronze, green with age, its flat face cut with the sign of a road running between two towers. It is cold to the touch and never quite warms, however long it is worn. The wardens who kept the old highway are said to have worn such rings as their badge of office.
